abortion-bans-world-vs-india-who.en:
Every year about 73 million induced abortions take place worldwide. Six in ten unintended pregnancies, and three in ten of all pregnancies, end in one [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Arguments about abortion are often framed as a choice between abortion and no abortion. WHO's figures describe a different divide: between abortions that are safe and abortions that are not. India's own history shows what a legal route can do, and what a law alone cannot.

## 73 million a year: abortion is common

With 29% of all pregnancies ending in induced abortion, abortion is a common outcome of pregnancy worldwide [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. India alone had an estimated 15.6 million abortions in 2015, according to a national study published in The Lancet Global Health [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

The reasons come from ordinary lives. In NFHS-5, the main reason Indian women gave for an abortion was simply an unplanned pregnancy (47.6%), followed by health not permitting (11.3%) and the last child being too young (9.7%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. No abortion law removes these reasons. What a law can change is whether a woman has a lawful way to a trained provider.

## Under 1 or over 200: safe versus unsafe

This is the number that matters most. Deaths from safe abortion are negligible, under 1 per 100,000 abortions. Where unsafe abortion is common, deaths exceed 200 per 100,000 [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. The same event becomes more than 200 times as deadly depending on who performs it and how.

Unsafe abortion is not rare. WHO's global estimates for 2010-2014 found that 45% of all induced abortions were unsafe. A third of those were done in the least safe conditions, by untrained people using dangerous methods, and more than half of all unsafe abortions took place in Asia, mostly in south and central Asia [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]], the region India belongs to. About 8% of maternal deaths worldwide in 2009-2020 were linked to abortion, and WHO warns that such deaths are often misclassified and under-reported because of stigma [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

## What a ban looks like: India's own penal code

A ban on abortion is not a foreign idea. One is still written into India's criminal law. Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, in force since 1 July 2024, punishes anyone who voluntarily causes a woman to miscarry, unless it is done in good faith to save her life, with up to three years in prison (seven if she is "quick with child"), and it expressly covers a woman who ends her own pregnancy. It repeats, word for word, the old abortion section of the Indian Penal Code [[gazette-bns-2023]], the code of 1860 that the BNS replaced [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]].

Read on its own, that section has a single exception: saving the woman's life. Under it, a girl raped at 14, a woman whose pregnancy is wrecking her health and a mother who cannot feed another child would have no legal route at all. The section does nothing about the reasons women seek abortions. It only closes the lawful way to a trained doctor.

## India's 1971 choice

India never repealed that rule. It cut a door into it. A government committee constituted in 1964 and headed by Shantilal Shah reported in 1966 that the existing abortion law was too restrictive and should be liberalised [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]]. Parliament passed the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act in 1971, and it came into force on 1 April 1972 [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. It shields registered doctors who end a pregnancy within its conditions: originally up to 12 weeks on one doctor's opinion and up to 20 weeks with two [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

The door has since widened (what follows is general information, not legal advice). Since 2021, one doctor's opinion is enough up to 20 weeks, and there is no upper limit where a Medical Board finds a substantial foetal abnormality [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Rape survivors, minors and other listed groups can go up to 24 weeks with two doctors [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. An adult woman's own consent is the only consent the law asks for [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Set beside the bare penal section, the difference is plain: a girl raped at 14 has a legal route to end the pregnancy through a registered doctor.

## Legal is not the same as accessible

And yet the deaths have not stopped. UNFPA India estimated in 2022 that unsafe abortion remains the third leading cause of maternal deaths in India, that close to eight women die every day from causes related to it, and that girls aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from abortion complications [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. These estimates rest on old data: the Health Ministry's figure that unsafe abortion causes about 8% of maternal deaths comes from cause-of-death data for 2001-03 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Most abortions never pass through the door. Of India's estimated 15.6 million abortions in 2015, about 11.5 million (73%) were medication abortions outside health facilities [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Pills taken outside a clinic are not automatically unsafe, but the researchers note that little is known about what women are told by chemists or whether they take the pills correctly. In NFHS-5, 26.9% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion said they had done it themselves [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Some barriers are built into the system. The Supreme Court observed in 2022 that because of POCSO's reporting rule, a pregnant minor and her guardian may choose an unqualified provider over a registered doctor [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Put WHO's two numbers beside India's record and the lesson is the same: the word "legal" in a statute protects a woman only when she can reach a trained provider without fear.
abortion-bans-world-vs-india-who.hg:
Duniya bhar mein har saal lagbhag 73 million induced abortions hote hain. Har das mein se chhe unintended pregnancies, aur saari pregnancies mein se har das mein se teen, abortion par khatam hoti hain [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Abortion par behas aksar aise hoti hai jaise chunaav "abortion" aur "koi abortion nahi" ke beech ho. WHO ke figures ek alag fark dikhate hain: safe abortion aur unsafe abortion ke beech. India ka apna itihaas dikhata hai ki kanooni raasta kya kar sakta hai, aur akela kanoon kya nahi kar sakta.

## 73 million har saal: abortion aam hai

Jab saari pregnancies mein se 29% induced abortion par khatam hoti hain, toh abortion duniya bhar mein pregnancy ka ek aam nateeja hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. The Lancet Global Health mein chhape ek national study ke mutabik, akele India mein 2015 mein andaazan 15.6 million abortions hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Wajahein aam zindagi se aati hain. NFHS-5 mein Indian auraton ne abortion ki sabse badi wajah bas ek unplanned pregnancy (47.6%) batayi, uske baad sehat ka saath na dena (11.3%) aur pichhla bachcha bahut chhota hona (9.7%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Abortion ka koi bhi kanoon yeh wajahein khatam nahi karta. Kanoon yeh badal sakta hai ki aurat ke paas trained provider tak pahunchne ka kanooni raasta hai ya nahi.

## 1 se kam ya 200 se zyada: safe aur unsafe ka fark

Sabse zaroori number yeh hai. Safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hoti hai: har 1 lakh abortions par 1 se bhi kam. Jahan unsafe abortion aam hai, wahan maut har 1 lakh par 200 se zyada hoti hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Ek hi cheez 200 guna se bhi zyada jaanleva ho jaati hai, bas is baat par ki use kaun kar raha hai aur kaise.

Unsafe abortion koi kabhi-kabhaar ki baat nahi. WHO ke 2010-2014 ke global estimates ke mutabik saare induced abortions mein se 45% unsafe the. Inmein se ek-tihaai sabse kam safe haalaat mein hue, untrained logon ke haathon aur khatarnaak tareekon se, aur saare unsafe abortions mein se aadhe se zyada Asia mein hue, zyada tar south aur central Asia mein [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]], yaani wahi ilaaka jahan India hai. 2009-2020 mein duniya bhar ki lagbhag 8% maternal deaths abortion se judi thi, aur WHO chetaavni deta hai ki stigma ki wajah se aisi maut aksar galat category mein darj hoti hai ya report hi nahi hoti [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

## Ban kaisa dikhta hai: India ka apna penal code

Abortion par ban koi videshi idea nahi hai. Aisa ek ban aaj bhi India ke criminal law mein likha hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 88, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hai, kisi aurat ka jaan-boojhkar miscarriage karane wale ko, agar yeh uski jaan bachane ke liye nek-neeyati se na kiya gaya ho, 3 saal tak ki jail deta hai (agar woh "quick with child" ho toh 7 saal tak), aur saaf kehta hai ki khud apni pregnancy khatam karne wali aurat bhi iske daayre mein hai. Yeh Indian Penal Code ke purane abortion section ko shabd-ba-shabd dohraata hai [[gazette-bns-2023]], yaani 1860 ka woh code jiski jagah BNS ne li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]].

Akele padha jaaye, toh is section mein sirf ek chhoot hai: aurat ki jaan bachana. Iske tahat 14 saal ki rape survivor, woh aurat jiski pregnancy uski sehat tabaah kar rahi hai, aur woh maa jo ek aur bachche ka pet nahi bhar sakti, kisi ke paas koi kanooni raasta nahi hota. Yeh section un wajahon ka kuch nahi karta jinki wajah se auratein abortion chahti hain. Yeh sirf trained doctor tak pahunchne ka kanooni raasta band karta hai.

## India ka 1971 ka chunaav

India ne yeh niyam kabhi khatam nahi kiya. Usne is deewar mein ek darwaaza bana diya. 1964 mein bani aur Shantilal Shah ki adhyakshata wali ek sarkari committee ne 1966 mein report di ki us waqt ka abortion kanoon bahut sakht hai aur use udaar banaya jaana chahiye [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]]. Parliament ne 1971 mein Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act paas kiya, aur yeh 1 April 1972 se laagu hua [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Yeh un registered doctors ko bachata hai jo iski sharton ke andar pregnancy khatam karte hain: shuru mein 12 hafte tak ek doctor ki raay par, aur 20 hafte tak do doctors ki raay par [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Tab se yeh darwaaza chauda hua hai (aage ki baatein general jaankari hain, legal advice nahi). 2021 se, 20 hafte tak ek doctor ki raay kaafi hai, aur agar Medical Board foetus mein koi badi abnormality paaye toh koi upper limit nahi hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Rape survivors, minors aur doosre listed groups do doctors ki raay se 24 hafte tak ja sakti hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Adult aurat ki apni consent hi woh akeli consent hai jo kanoon maangta hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Akele penal section ke saamne rakhiye, toh fark saaf hai: 14 saal ki rape survivor ke paas registered doctor ke zariye pregnancy khatam karne ka kanooni raasta hai.

## Legal hona aur pahunch mein hona ek baat nahi

Phir bhi maut nahi ruki. UNFPA India ne 2022 mein andaaza lagaya ki India mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah ab bhi unsafe abortion hai, isse judi wajahon se roz kareeb aath auratein marti hain, aur 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko abortion complications se maut ka sabse zyada khatra hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Yeh andaaze purane data par tike hain: Health Ministry ka yeh figure ki unsafe abortion lagbhag 8% maternal deaths ki wajah hai, 2001-03 ke cause-of-death data se aata hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Zyada tar abortions is darwaaze se guzarte hi nahi. 2015 mein India ke andaazan 15.6 million abortions mein se lagbhag 11.5 million (73%) health facilities ke bahar hue medication abortions the [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Clinic ke bahar li gayi pills apne aap unsafe nahi hoti, lekin researchers kehte hain ki yeh bahut kam pata hai ki chemist auraton ko kya batate hain, ya woh pills sahi tarah leti hain ya nahi. NFHS-5 mein jin auraton ki pichhli pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone yeh khud kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Kuch rukaavatein system mein hi bani hui hain. Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki POCSO ke reporting rule ki wajah se ek pregnant minor aur uske guardian registered doctor ki jagah kisi unqualified provider ko chun sakte hain [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. WHO ke do numbers India ke record ke saath rakhiye, toh sabak wahi hai: kisi kanoon mein likha "legal" shabd aurat ko tabhi bachata hai jab woh bina darr ke kisi trained provider tak pahunch sake.

abortion-consent-husband-mother-in-law.en:
At an Indian abortion clinic, the consent form needs one signature: hers. Not her husband's, not her mother-in-law's. That rule goes back to the MTP Act of 1971 [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. But a law cannot stop a family from deciding first and then bringing her in to sign. Read the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) closely and its tables become a map of who else is deciding.

## What the law says about whose consent counts

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act is plain. No pregnancy can be ended "except with the consent of the pregnant woman" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. A guardian's written consent is needed only if she is under 18 or, in the law's words since 2002, a "mentally ill person". The Act mentions neither husbands nor in-laws.

The rule cuts both ways: without her consent, nobody can lawfully end her pregnancy, whatever the family wants. And since 2021, a doctor who reveals the name or details of a woman who had an abortion to anyone not authorised by law faces up to a year in prison [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. There is no exception for family.

If a clinic insists on a husband's signature, that is the clinic's habit, not the law. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

## The reasons women gave, and whose reasons they were

NFHS-5 (2019-21) asked women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion for the main reason. The most common answer, at 47.6%, was an unplanned pregnancy. Others cited their health (11.3%), a last child still too young (9.7%) or complications in the pregnancy (9.1%). Further down comes a line that names other people: 4.1% said their husband or mother-in-law did not want the pregnancy. That is more than the 3.6% who named contraceptive failure [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Another 2.1% openly named a female foetus as the main reason; among the larger states, the share was highest in Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) and Punjab (4.2%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sex selection is a crime, so the real share is almost certainly higher.

> The survey asks for one main reason. Pressure rarely arrives as one.

The sex-selection law itself assumes the pressure comes from the family. Under the PCPNDT Act, anyone who seeks sex selection faces up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 50,000. But it presumes a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives, and does not punish a woman who was forced [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

That pressure is not only male. In a 2014 ICRW-UNFPA survey in seven states, more women than men said it was very important to have at least one son: 81% of women against 76% of men [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

## What men told the same survey

NFHS-5 also asked men what a husband may do if his wife refuses sex. 12.2% of men aged 15-49, about one in eight, said he has the right to use force. 19.2% said he may get angry and reprimand her [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

On contraception, 35.1% of men agreed that it is "women's business and a man should not have to worry about it". 19.6% said women who use it may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Put those answers side by side. For more than a third of men, preventing pregnancy is her job. For one man in eight, saying no to sex is not her right. Neither view leaves her much room to decide about a pregnancy.

"Showing disrespect to in-laws" was the reason most often accepted for wife-beating, by 31% of men and 32% of women [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In a home that thinks this way, saying no to a mother-in-law about a pregnancy is not a small act.

## Coercion both ways: to end, to continue, to conceive

This has a name: reproductive coercion. Pressure to end a pregnancy, or to continue one. Pills thrown away. Sex she did not agree to.

Consider a hypothetical. A 23-year-old in a joint family has a daughter. Her husband hides her pills because his mother wants a grandson within the year. When she is pregnant again, she is taken for a scan "to check the baby's health". Every step is someone else's decision. None of it shows up in a survey table as coercion.

And the survey sees only abortions that happened, not the women who wanted one and were refused. If those pregnancies end in births, no survey table records them as coerced.

Sometimes it starts with forced sex. In NFHS-5, 4.6% of ever-married women said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Criminal law still does not call this rape if the wife is 18 or older (Exception 2 to Section 63, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and petitions challenging that exception are still pending in the Supreme Court [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. But under the abortion law, the Supreme Court held in September 2022, she counts as a rape survivor: she can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks without an FIR or proof in court [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Our explainer on that ruling covers it in depth.

## Where a woman under pressure can turn

She already holds two protections: her own signature and her doctor's duty of silence. Beyond that, the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts sexual abuse as domestic violence, and courts can issue protection orders under it. Whoever breaks one faces up to a year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

As of March 2026, 926 One Stop Centres (Sakhi) were running across India and had assisted more than 13 lakh women [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]]. The centres and the Women Helpline both run under the government's Mission Shakti scheme [[wcd-mission-shakti]], and legal services authorities give free legal aid [[nalsa]].

The hardest step is the first one. Among women abused only by their current husband, just 11.3% ever sought help, against 23.6% of women abused only by a former husband; most of those abused by their current husband never told anyone at all [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is why the people around her matter: a sister, a friend, a nurse who asks to speak to her alone.

The law already says this decision is hers. The work now is making that true inside the home.
abortion-consent-husband-mother-in-law.hg:
Abortion clinic mein jo consent form sabse zaroori hai, us par sirf ek signature chahiye: aurat ka. Pati ka nahi, saas ka nahi. Yeh rule 1971 ke MTP Act se chala aa raha hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Lekin law yeh nahi rok sakta ki family pehle hi faisla kar le aur phir use sign karwane le aaye. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) ke tables dhyaan se padhiye. Woh ek map ban jaate hain ki yeh faisla asal mein aur kaun-kaun le raha hai.

## Law kiski consent maangta hai

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act is par bilkul saaf hai. Pregnant aurat ki consent ke bina koi pregnancy khatam nahi ki ja sakti [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Guardian ki written consent sirf do cases mein chahiye: jab woh 18 se kam ki ho, ya jab woh law ke shabdon mein, 2002 se, ek "mentally ill person" ho. Act mein na pati ka zikr hai, na sasural walon ka.

Yeh rule dono taraf kaam karta hai. Uski haan ke bina koi uska abortion legally nahi karwa sakta, family chahe kuch bhi chahe. Aur 2021 se, agar koi doctor abortion karwane wali aurat ka naam ya details kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne permission nahi di, toh use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Family ke liye koi exception nahi hai.

Agar koi clinic pati ke signature par ad jaaye, toh yeh clinic ki aadat hai, law nahi. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

## Aurton ne kya wajah batayi, aur woh wajah kiski thi

NFHS-5 (2019-21) ne un aurton se poocha jinki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui: main wajah kya thi? Sabse aam jawab tha ki pregnancy plan nahi ki thi (47.6%). Kuch ne apni health ki baat ki (11.3%), kuch ne kaha ki pichhla bachcha abhi bahut chhota tha (9.7%), aur kuch ne pregnancy mein complications batayi (9.1%). Thoda neeche ek line aati hai jismein doosre logon ka naam hai: 4.1% ne kaha ki unke pati ya saas yeh pregnancy nahi chahte the. Yeh un 3.6% se bhi zyada hai jinhone contraceptive fail hone ki baat ki [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

2.1% aurton ne khul kar kaha ki main wajah yeh thi ki pet mein ladki thi. Bade states mein yeh sabse zyada Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) aur Punjab (4.2%) mein tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sex selection crime hai, isliye asli share almost pakka isse zyada hoga.

> Survey ek main wajah poochta hai. Pressure shayad hi kabhi ek wajah ban kar aata hai.

Sex selection wala law khud maan kar chalta hai ki pressure family se aata hai. PCPNDT Act ke under, jo bhi sex selection karwana chahe, use teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 50,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai. Lekin Act yeh maanta hai ki pregnant aurat par uske pati ya rishtedaaron ne dabav dala hoga, aur jis aurat ko majboor kiya gaya, use saza nahi deta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Yeh pressure sirf mardon se nahi aata. 2014 mein saat states mein hue ICRW-UNFPA survey mein mardon se zyada aurton ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai: 81% aurton ne, jabki 76% mardon ne [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

## Usi survey mein mardon ne kya kaha

NFHS-5 ne mardon se bhi poocha: agar biwi sex se mana kare, toh pati kya kar sakta hai? 15-49 saal ke 12.2% mardon ne, yaani lagbhag har aath mein se ek ne, kaha ki pati ko zabardasti karne ka haq hai. 19.2% ne kaha ki pati gussa ho kar use daant sakta hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Contraception par 35.1% mardon ne maana ki yeh "aurton ka kaam hai, mard ko iski tension lene ki zaroorat nahi". 19.6% ne kaha ki contraception use karne wali aurtein "badchalan" ho sakti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

In jawabon ko saath rakh kar dekhiye. Ek-tihaai se zyada mardon ke hisaab se pregnancy rokna aurat ki zimmedari hai. Har aath mein se ek mard ke hisaab se, sex ko na kehna uska haq hi nahi hai. Aisi soch mein pregnancy ke baare mein khud faisla lene ki jagah uske paas bahut kam bachti hai.

Biwi ko maarne ki jo wajah sabse zyada logon ne sahi maani, woh thi "sasural walon ki izzat na karna": 31% mardon aur 32% aurton ne [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aise ghar mein pregnancy ke baare mein saas ko "na" kehna chhoti baat nahi hai.

## Pressure dono taraf: girane ka, rakhne ka, pregnant hone ka

Iska ek naam hai: reproductive coercion. Pregnancy girane ka pressure, ya rakhne ka pressure. Chupke se phenki gayi pills. Bina marzi ka sex.

Ek hypothetical example lijiye. Joint family mein rehne wali 23 saal ki ek aurat ki ek beti hai. Uska pati uski pills chhupa deta hai, kyunki uski maa ko saal bhar mein pota chahiye. Jab woh phir pregnant hoti hai, use "bachche ki health check karne" ke naam par scan ke liye le jaaya jaata hai. Har step par faisla kisi aur ka hai. Lekin survey ki kisi table mein yeh coercion nahi dikhta.

Aur survey sirf woh abortions dekhta hai jo hue. Woh un aurton ko nahi dekh pata jo abortion chahti thi par unhe karne nahi diya gaya. Agar aisi pregnancy bachche ke janam par khatam hoti hai, toh survey ki koi table use zabardasti ke roop mein record nahi karti.

Kabhi-kabhi shuruaat zabardasti ke sex se hoti hai. NFHS-5 mein, jin aurton ki kabhi shaadi hui, unmein se 4.6% ne bataya ki pati ne unki marzi ke khilaaf zabardasti physical relation banaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Agar biwi 18 ya usse badi hai, toh criminal law aaj bhi ise rape nahi maanta (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 63 ka Exception 2) [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur is exception ko challenge karne wali petitions abhi bhi Supreme Court mein pending hain [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. Lekin abortion ke maamle mein Supreme Court ne September 2022 mein kaha ki "rape" mein marital rape bhi shaamil hai. Pati ki zabardasti se pregnant hui biwi rape survivor ke taur par 24 hafte tak abortion karwa sakti hai, bina FIR ke aur bina court mein kuch saabit kiye [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Is ruling par hamara alag explainer ise detail mein samjhata hai.

## Pressure mein phansi aurat kahan jaaye

Do cheezein pehle se uske paas hain: uska apna signature, aur doctor ka chup rehne ka farz. Iske alawa Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 sexual abuse ko bhi domestic violence maanta hai, aur iske under court protection order de sakta hai. Jo ise tode, use ek saal tak ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

March 2026 tak poore desh mein 926 One Stop Centres (Sakhi) chal rahe the, aur 13 lakh se zyada aurton ki madad kar chuke the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-03]]. Yeh centres aur Women Helpline, dono sarkar ki Mission Shakti scheme ke under chalte hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]], aur free legal aid legal services authorities se milti hai [[nalsa]].

Sabse mushkil step pehla hota hai. Jin aurton ke saath violence sirf current pati ne ki, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi madad maangi. Jinke saath sirf pehle wale pati ne ki thi, unmein yeh 23.6% tha. Current pati se violence jhelne wali zyada tar aurton ne kabhi kisi ko kuch nahi bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Isliye aas-paas ke log matter karte hain: ek behen, ek dost, ya woh nurse jo kahe, "Mujhe inse akele mein baat karni hai."

Law pehle hi keh chuka hai ki yeh faisla uska hai. Ab kaam hai ise ghar ke andar bhi sach banana.

abortion-infertility-health-myths-eviden.en:
Imagine a 24-year-old in Kanpur, seven weeks pregnant, who has decided she cannot continue the pregnancy. Before she reaches a doctor, she hears four warnings from people who love her. Abortion kills. The pills fail. One abortion ruins every future pregnancy. And if she ever struggles to have a baby, everyone will know why. Each warning sounds like caution. Checked against the evidence, each one blurs the only distinction that matters for her health: whether the abortion is safe or unsafe.

## Myth: one abortion ruins every future pregnancy

This is the warning that frightens women most, and for a safe abortion it is false. The World Health Organization calls abortion a safe procedure when it is done with a recommended method suited to the length of the pregnancy, by someone with the right skills. A safe abortion does not normally affect a woman's chances of getting pregnant again [[who-abortion]].

The myth survives because it holds a grain of truth with one word cut out. Among the causes of infertility in women, WHO lists blocked fallopian tubes, which can follow untreated sexually transmitted infections or the complications of *unsafe* abortion [[who-infertility]]. The honest version of the warning is this: an unsafe abortion, or an infection left untreated, can damage fertility. That version sends a woman to a doctor. The myth, which treats every abortion as the same danger, sends her away from one.

## What the evidence says about safe abortion

Start with death, the fear under all the others. WHO puts deaths from safe abortion at under 1 per 100,000 abortions [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

Then the pills. India's Health Ministry approves the combination of mifepristone and misoprostol for ending a pregnancy of up to nine weeks (63 days), prescribed by a qualified doctor, and its 2023 guidelines say it succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. This is not a fringe method. Of an estimated 15.6 million abortions in India in 2015, 12.7 million (81%) were medication abortions [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

So "the pills won't work and you'll end up needing surgery" is wrong for almost every woman who uses the approved method correctly. The real gap lies elsewhere. About 11.5 million of those abortions (73%) were done with pills outside any health facility [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Pills from a chemist can work. But often nobody checks how many weeks pregnant the woman is, or whether the pregnancy is inside the uterus at all, and nobody is watching if something goes wrong.

## Where real harm comes from

Where unsafe abortion is common, WHO counts more than 200 deaths per 100,000 abortions. Worldwide, 45% of induced abortions in 2010-2014 were unsafe, a third of those in the least safe conditions, by untrained people using dangerous methods. More than half of all unsafe abortions took place in Asia, mostly in south and central Asia [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

India sits inside that statistic. Unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths in the country, close to eight women die every day from causes related to it, and young women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from its complications, according to UNFPA India [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. These are estimates, not a death register, but they all point the same way.

The injuries are specific. In a 2015 survey of six states (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh), 4-16% of women receiving care after an abortion were being treated for serious complications such as infection of the uterus, perforation, sepsis and shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Infections like these are how fallopian tubes get scarred and blocked [[who-infertility]]. They are what the infertility myth is really describing, and they belong to unsafe abortion and delayed care.

## Why a past abortion gets the blame

Infertility is common for reasons that have nothing to do with abortion. About 17.5% of adults worldwide, roughly 1 in 6, experience it at some point in their lives, at similar rates in rich countries (17.8%) and poorer ones (16.5%) [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. The causes include problems with ovulation, blocked tubes and, in men, problems with sperm [[who-infertility]].

Yet when a couple cannot conceive, the search often stops at the woman's past. A secret abortion becomes the explanation, and the husband may never be tested. Our explainer on why "my abortion made me infertile" feels true walks through that coincidence. The cost is practical: a wrong explanation leaves the real cause, in either partner, undiagnosed and untreated.

## Protecting your future fertility

What protects fertility is not avoiding an abortion you need. It is three things the myths discourage.

**Safe care, early.** See a registered doctor or an approved facility as soon as you can; the pills are approved only up to nine weeks [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

**Fast treatment of complications.** In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 15.6% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion reported complications, and 89.7% of them sought treatment [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Heavy bleeding, fever, severe pain or a foul-smelling discharge after an abortion need a hospital the same day, and the doctor needs to know what was taken. Shame that keeps a woman at home with a fever is how a treatable infection becomes a damaged tube.

**Contraception afterwards.** Pregnancy can happen again soon after an abortion, so if you do not want another one yet, ask for contraception at the same visit. With typical use, fewer than 1 in 100 women using an implant or an IUD get pregnant in a year, against about 7 in 100 on the pill and 13 in 100 relying on condoms [[who-fp]].

The woman in Kanpur does not need to hear that abortion is harmless, because unsafe abortion is not. She needs to hear the difference, and in time.
abortion-infertility-health-myths-eviden.hg:
Socho, Kanpur ki ek 24 saal ki ladki hai, saat hafte pregnant, aur usne tay kar liya hai ki woh yeh pregnancy aage nahi le ja sakti. Doctor tak pahunchne se pehle hi use apne hi logon se chaar warnings milti hain. Abortion se jaan chali jaati hai. Pills kaam nahi karti. Ek abortion aage ki har pregnancy bigaad deta hai. Aur agar kabhi baccha hone mein dikkat hui, toh sabko pata hoga kyun. Har warning ehtiyaat jaisi lagti hai. Lekin evidence ke saamne rakho, toh har warning us ek farak ko dhundhla kar deti hai jo uski sehat ke liye sach mein maayne rakhta hai: abortion safe hai ya unsafe.

## Myth: ek abortion aage ki har pregnancy bigaad deta hai

Yeh woh warning hai jo aurton ko sabse zyada darati hai, aur safe abortion ke liye yeh galat hai. World Health Organization ke mutabik abortion ek safe procedure hai jab use pregnancy ki length ke hisaab se recommended method se, kisi trained insaan ke haathon kiya jaaye. Safe abortion se aam taur par aurat ke dobara pregnant hone ke chances par koi asar nahi padta [[who-abortion]].

Yeh myth isliye zinda hai kyunki ismein sach ka ek tukda hai, bas ek shabd kaat diya gaya hai. Aurton mein infertility ki wajahon mein WHO blocked fallopian tubes ko ginata hai, jo bina ilaaj ke chhode gaye sexually transmitted infections ke baad, ya *unsafe* abortion ki complications ke baad ho sakti hain [[who-infertility]]. Warning ka imaandaar version yeh hai: unsafe abortion, ya bina ilaaj ka infection, fertility ko nuksaan pahuncha sakta hai. Yeh version aurat ko doctor ke paas bhejta hai. Myth, jo har abortion ko ek jaisa khatra batata hai, use doctor se door bhejta hai.

## Safe abortion ke baare mein evidence kya kehta hai

Shuruaat maut ke darr se karo, jo baaki saare darr ke neeche chhupa hai. WHO ke mutabik safe abortion se maut har 100,000 abortions mein 1 se bhi kam hoti hai, yaani under 1 per 100,000 [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

Ab pills ki baat. India ki Health Ministry mifepristone aur misoprostol ke combination ko 9 hafte (63 din) tak ki pregnancy khatam karne ke liye approve karti hai, qualified doctor ke prescription par. Ministry ki 2023 ki guidelines kehti hain ki yeh shuruaati abortions mein 95-99% cases mein kaam karta hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Yeh koi kinare ka tareeka nahi hai. 2015 mein India ke estimated 15.6 million abortions mein se 12.7 million (81%) medication abortions the [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Toh "pills kaam nahi karengi, aakhir mein surgery hi karwani padegi" wali baat un lagbhag sabhi aurton ke liye galat hai jo approved method sahi tareeke se leti hain. Asli kami kahin aur hai. Unmein se lagbhag 11.5 million abortions (73%) kisi bhi health facility ke bahar pills se hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Chemist ki pills kaam kar sakti hain. Lekin aksar koi check nahi karta ki aurat kitne hafte pregnant hai, ya pregnancy uterus ke andar hai bhi ya nahi, aur kuch galat ho jaaye toh koi dekhne wala nahi hota.

## Asli nuksaan kahan se aata hai

Jahan unsafe abortion aam hai, wahan WHO har 100,000 abortions par 200 se zyada maut ginta hai. Duniya bhar mein 2010-2014 ke beech 45% induced abortions unsafe the, aur unmein se ek-tihaai sabse kharab haalaat mein hue, untrained logon ke haathon, khatarnaak tareekon se. Saare unsafe abortions mein se aadhe se zyada Asia mein hue, zyada tar south aur central Asia mein [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

India isi statistic ke andar hai. UNFPA India ke mutabik desh mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah unsafe abortion hai, isse judi wajahon se har din lagbhag aath aurton ki maut hoti hai, aur 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko iski complications se marne ka sabse zyada khatra hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Yeh estimates hain, maut ka register nahi, lekin sab ek hi taraf ishaara karte hain.

Nuksaan bilkul specific hai. 2015 mein chhe states (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu aur Uttar Pradesh) ke ek survey mein, abortion ke baad care le rahi 4-16% aurton ka ilaaj serious complications ke liye ho raha tha, jaise uterus ka infection, perforation, sepsis aur shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Aise hi infections se fallopian tubes par nishaan padte hain aur woh block ho jaati hain [[who-infertility]]. Infertility wali myth asal mein inhi ki baat kar rahi hai, aur yeh unsafe abortion aur der se mile ilaaj ki den hain.

## Purane abortion par hi ilzaam kyun aata hai

Infertility aam hai, aur uski zyada tar wajahon ka abortion se koi lena-dena nahi. Duniya mein lagbhag 17.5% adults, yaani har 6 mein se 1, zindagi mein kabhi na kabhi infertility jhelte hain. Ameer deshon (17.8%) aur gareeb deshon (16.5%) mein yeh rate lagbhag ek jaisa hai [[who-infertility-estimates-2023]]. Wajahon mein ovulation ki problems, blocked tubes, aur mardon mein sperm ki problems shaamil hain [[who-infertility]].

Phir bhi jab koi couple conceive nahi kar paata, toh khoj aksar aurat ke ateet par aakar ruk jaati hai. Chhupa hua abortion explanation ban jaata hai, aur ho sakta hai pati ka test kabhi ho hi nahi. "Mere abortion ne mujhe infertile bana diya" itna sach kyun lagta hai, yeh hamare explainer mein detail se samjhaya gaya hai. Iski keemat bilkul practical hai: galat explanation ki wajah se asli wajah, chahe woh kisi bhi partner mein ho, na pakdi jaati hai, na uska ilaaj hota hai.

## Apni aage ki fertility kaise bachao

Fertility ko bachata hai zaroorat ka abortion taalna nahi. Use bachati hain teen cheezein, jinse yeh myths aurton ko door karti hain.

**Safe care, jaldi.** Jitni jaldi ho sake kisi registered doctor ya approved facility mein jao; pills sirf 9 hafte tak ke liye approved hain [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

**Complications ka turant ilaaj.** NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications batayi, aur unmein se 89.7% ne ilaaj karwaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Abortion ke baad bahut zyada bleeding, bukhaar, tez dard ya badboo wala discharge ho, toh usi din hospital jao, aur doctor ko batao ki kya liya tha. Jo sharam aurat ko bukhaar mein bhi ghar par rok kar rakhti hai, wahi ek theek ho sakne wale infection ko kharab tube mein badal deti hai.

**Baad mein contraception.** Abortion ke kuch hi samay baad dobara pregnancy ho sakti hai, isliye agar abhi aur pregnancy nahi chahiye, toh usi visit par contraception maango. Typical use mein implant ya IUD use karne wali 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam aurtein ek saal mein pregnant hoti hain, jabki pill par 100 mein se lagbhag 7 aur condom par 100 mein se 13 [[who-fp]].

Kanpur ki us ladki ko yeh sunne ki zaroorat nahi ki abortion bilkul harmless hai, kyunki unsafe abortion harmless nahi hai. Use yeh farak sunna hai, aur waqt rehte sunna hai.

abortion-law-myths-india-checked.en:
Ask around and you will hear it said with confidence: abortion is illegal in India. Or legal only for married women. Or legal, but only with the husband's signature, only after a police complaint if it was rape, and the doctor will tell your family anyway. Each of these is wrong, and each one pushes women towards delay or a quack. Here is every myth, the clause or judgment that answers it, and what you can say when a relative or a clinic repeats it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Myth 1: "Abortion is illegal in India"

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act came into force on 1 April 1972 [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Since its 2021 amendment, a pregnancy of up to 20 weeks can be ended on the opinion of one registered doctor, if continuing it would risk the woman's life or gravely injure her physical or mental health, or if there is a substantial risk of serious foetal abnormality. Between 20 and 24 weeks, two doctors must agree, for categories of women listed in the rules. Beyond 24 weeks, the Act allows it only when a Medical Board has diagnosed a substantial foetal abnormality [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

The myth survives because part of it is true. Abortion outside the Act is still a crime. Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita punishes causing a miscarriage and expressly covers a woman who causes her own [[gazette-bns-2023]]. An abortion by anyone who is not a registered doctor, or at a place not approved under the Act, carries two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

**What you can say:** It has been legal since 1972 under the MTP Act, when a registered doctor does it on the Act's grounds at an approved place. The illegal one is the quack.

## Myth 2: "Only married women can get one"

This myth has a source: the law's own old wording. The 1971 Act let a woman rely on failed contraception only if the method was used by "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. In 2021 Parliament rewrote it as "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Then, on 29 September 2022, the Supreme Court ruled in X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department that shutting unmarried or single women out of abortion between 20 and 24 weeks would violate Article 14 of the Constitution, the right to equality. They have the same access as married women [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**What you can say:** The Act now says "any woman or her partner", and the Supreme Court ruled in 2022 that single women have the same access as married women up to 24 weeks.

## Myth 3: "The husband must sign"

Section 3(4) of the MTP Act is short. No pregnancy can be terminated without the consent of the pregnant woman, and a guardian's written consent is needed only if she is under 18 or a mentally ill person [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The consent clause does not mention a husband, a partner, a mother-in-law, or the parents of an adult woman.

That cuts both ways. A husband's refusal cannot block an adult woman's abortion, and nobody can lawfully have her pregnancy ended without her own consent.

**What you can say:** I am over 18. Under Section 3(4) of the MTP Act, my consent is the only one you need.

## Myth 4: "After rape, you must go to the police first"

No. When a woman says her pregnancy was caused by rape, the MTP Act presumes that the anguish of that pregnancy is a grave injury to her mental health, which is a legal ground for termination [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Survivors of sexual assault, rape or incest are among the categories eligible up to 24 weeks [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. In 2022 the Supreme Court held that no FIR needs to be registered, and the rape need not be proved in court, before a woman can rely on this ground. It also held that, for the purposes of the MTP Act alone, "rape" includes forced sex by a husband [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Two honest caveats. A hospital that treats a rape survivor must give free treatment and inform the police under Section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; that is the hospital's duty, not a condition for your abortion. And for a girl under 18, the doctor must report the pregnancy to the police under POCSO, though the Supreme Court has said her name and details can be left out of that report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**What you can say:** The Supreme Court has said no FIR is needed for an abortion after rape. Please do not make me wait for one.

## Myth 5: "The doctor will tell your family"

Not lawfully. Section 5A of the MTP Act, added in 2021, bars any registered doctor from revealing the name or other particulars of a woman whose pregnancy was terminated, except to a person authorised by law. The penalty is up to a year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. The section carves out no exception for a husband, a parent or an in-law.

The limits are the ones already described. A girl under 18 needs a guardian's written consent, so at least her guardian will know, and the doctor must inform the police. A hospital treating a rape survivor must inform the police too. Otherwise, for an adult woman, the consent and the confidence are hers.

**What you can say:** Section 5A of the MTP Act says you cannot share my details with anyone who is not authorised by law. It makes no exception for family.

Each of these myths does the same damage: it sends a woman away from a registered doctor and towards delay or a quack. UNFPA India said in 2022 that unsafe abortion remained the third leading cause of maternal deaths in the country [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Knowing the clause is not pedantry. It can be the difference.
abortion-law-myths-india-checked.hg:
Kisi se bhi poochho, aur tumhe poore bharose ke saath sunne ko milega: India mein abortion illegal hai. Ya sirf shaadishuda aurton ke liye legal hai. Ya legal hai, par sirf pati ke signature ke saath, rape ka case ho to pehle police complaint ke baad, aur doctor waise bhi ghar walon ko bata dega. Inmein se har baat galat hai, aur har ek aurton ko der ya quack ki taraf dhakelti hai. Yahan har myth hai, uska jawab dene wala clause ya faisla, aur jab koi rishtedaar ya clinic yeh baat dohraye to tum kya keh sakti ho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Myth 1: "India mein abortion illegal hai"

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act 1 April 1972 ko lagu hua [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. 2021 ke amendment ke baad se, 20 hafte tak ki pregnancy ek registered doctor ki opinion par khatam ki ja sakti hai, agar use continue karne se aurat ki jaan ko khatra ho, uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan ho, ya foetus mein serious abnormality ka bada risk ho. 20 se 24 hafte ke beech do doctors ki haan chahiye, aur woh bhi rules mein likhi categories ki aurton ke liye. 24 hafte ke baad Act sirf tab ijazat deta hai jab Medical Board ne foetus mein substantial abnormality diagnose ki ho [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Yeh myth isliye zinda hai kyunki iska ek hissa sach hai. Act ke bahar abortion ab bhi apraadh hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 88 miscarriage karwane par saza deta hai, aur saaf taur par us aurat ko bhi cover karta hai jo khud apna miscarriage karti hai [[gazette-bns-2023]]. Agar koi aisa insaan abortion kare jo registered doctor nahi hai, ya aisi jagah kare jo Act ke tahat approved nahi hai, to do se saat saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

**Tum keh sakti ho:** MTP Act ke tahat yeh 1972 se legal hai, jab registered doctor Act ke grounds par approved jagah par kare. Illegal to quack hai.

## Myth 2: "Sirf shaadishuda aurton ko milta hai"

Is myth ki ek jad hai: law ke apne purane shabd. 1971 ke Act mein aurat contraception fail hone ka hawala tabhi de sakti thi jab method "any married woman or her husband", yaani shaadishuda aurat ya uske pati, ne use kiya ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 2021 mein Parliament ne ise badal kar "any woman or her partner" kar diya [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Phir 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court ne X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department case mein faisla diya ki unmarried ya single aurton ko 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion se bahar rakhna Constitution ke Article 14, yaani barabari ke adhikaar, ka ullanghan hoga. Unka access shaadishuda aurton jaisa hi hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**Tum keh sakti ho:** Act ab "any woman or her partner" kehta hai, aur Supreme Court ne 2022 mein faisla diya ki 24 hafte tak single aurton ka access shaadishuda aurton jaisa hi hai.

## Myth 3: "Pati ka signature zaroori hai"

MTP Act ka Section 3(4) chhota sa hai. Pregnant aurat ki consent ke bina koi pregnancy terminate nahi ki ja sakti, aur guardian ki likhit consent sirf tab chahiye jab woh 18 se kam ho ya mentally ill person ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Consent wale clause mein pati, partner, saas, ya adult aurat ke maa-baap ka koi zikr nahi hai.

Yeh baat dono taraf lagti hai. Pati ke mana karne se adult aurat ka abortion nahi ruk sakta, aur koi bhi uski apni consent ke bina legally uski pregnancy khatam nahi karwa sakta.

**Tum keh sakti ho:** Main 18 se upar hoon. MTP Act ke Section 3(4) ke tahat sirf meri consent chahiye.

## Myth 4: "Rape ke baad pehle police ke paas jaana padta hai"

Nahi. Jab aurat kehti hai ki uski pregnancy rape se hui hai, to MTP Act maan kar chalta hai ki us pregnancy ki takleef uski mental health ko gambhir chot hai, aur yeh termination ka legal ground hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Sexual assault, rape ya incest ki survivors un categories mein hain jinhe 24 hafte tak abortion mil sakta hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki is ground par bharosa karne se pehle na FIR register honi zaroori hai, na court mein rape saabit karna. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki sirf MTP Act ke liye "rape" mein pati ka zabardasti sex bhi shaamil hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Do imaandaar caveats. Jo hospital rape survivor ka ilaaj karta hai, use Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke Section 397 ke tahat free ilaaj dena hota hai aur police ko batana hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]; yeh hospital ki duty hai, tumhare abortion ki shart nahi. Aur 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke case mein doctor ko POCSO ke tahat pregnancy police ko report karni padti hai, lekin Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki agar ladki aur uska guardian maangein, to us report mein uska naam aur details chhodi ja sakti hain [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**Tum keh sakti ho:** Supreme Court keh chuka hai ki rape ke baad abortion ke liye FIR ki zaroorat nahi. Please mujhe uske liye intezaar na karwayein.

## Myth 5: "Doctor tumhare ghar walon ko bata dega"

Legally nahi. 2021 mein MTP Act mein jode gaye Section 5A ke tahat koi bhi registered doctor us aurat ka naam ya doosri details nahi bata sakta jiski pregnancy terminate hui, siway us insaan ke jo law ke tahat authorised ho. Saza hai ek saal tak ki jail, jurmana, ya dono [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Is section mein pati, maa-baap ya sasuraal walon ke liye koi chhoot nahi hai.

Iski seemayein wahi hain jo upar bataayi gayin. 18 se kam umar ki ladki ko guardian ki likhit consent chahiye, isliye kam se kam uske guardian ko pata hoga, aur doctor ko police ko batana padega. Rape survivor ka ilaaj karne wale hospital ko bhi police ko batana hota hai. Iske alawa, adult aurat ke liye consent bhi uski hai aur raaz bhi uska.

**Tum keh sakti ho:** MTP Act ka Section 5A kehta hai ki aap meri details kisi aise insaan ko nahi de sakte jo law ke tahat authorised nahi hai. Ismein family ke liye koi chhoot nahi hai.

Yeh saare myths ek hi nuksaan karte hain: aurat ko registered doctor se door, der ya quack ki taraf bhejte hain. UNFPA India ne 2022 mein kaha ki unsafe abortion ab bhi desh mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Clause jaanna nitpicking nahi hai. Yahi asli farak ban sakta hai.

abortion-not-on-request-doctors-opinion.en:
Is abortion legal in India? Yes. Can a woman walk into a clinic and get one simply because she does not want to be pregnant? Legally, no. The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, passed in 1971, came into force on 1 April 1972 [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]], and in more than five decades it has never made abortion available on request. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The myth: "my body, my legal right"

The belief that asking is enough is easy to understand. Abortion is legal, and women are told it is their choice. But the law is built differently. It does not start from what the woman wants. It starts from what a doctor thinks.

Consider a hypothetical. A 26-year-old software tester in Bengaluru, seven weeks pregnant, tells a gynaecologist: "I don't want this pregnancy." Under the Act, that sentence is not a legal ground. What makes her abortion legal is the doctor's opinion, formed in good faith, that continuing the pregnancy would risk her life or gravely injure her physical or mental health, or that there is a substantial risk of serious abnormality in the foetus [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

## The truth: grounds, opinions and gates

The Act sets three gates, and a doctor stands at each one.

| Stage of pregnancy | Who must agree | Who qualifies |
|---|---|---|
| Up to 20 weeks | 1 registered doctor | Any woman, if a legal ground applies |
| 20 to 24 weeks | 2 registered doctors | Only women in categories listed in the rules |
| Beyond 24 weeks | A state Medical Board | Only a substantial foetal abnormality |

All three gates come from the Act as amended in 2021 [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], and our plain-words guide to the MTP Act walks through each one. A separate emergency rule lets a doctor act at any stage when ending the pregnancy is immediately necessary to save the woman's life.

Her consent is required at every gate. For an adult woman, her own consent is the only consent the law asks for; no husband's signature is needed [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. But consent is a condition, not a ground. Without the doctor's opinion, it does not make the abortion legal.

The law also guards the gates closely. An abortion done by anyone who is not a registered medical practitioner, or at a place not approved under the Act, is punishable with two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

## How "grave injury to mental health" is presumed

Of the legal grounds, mental health is the widest door, because in two situations the Act itself props it open.

The first is contraceptive failure. If a pregnancy results from the failure of a device or method used by "any woman or her partner", the anguish it causes "may be presumed" to be a grave injury to her mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Until 2021 the words were "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

The second is rape. If a woman says her pregnancy was caused by rape, the anguish "shall be presumed" to be a grave injury to her mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. In 2022 the Supreme Court added that she needs no FIR and no court finding to rely on this, and that rape here includes forced sex by a husband [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Notice the two verbs. For rape, the presumption is firm: "shall". For a failed condom or pill it is "may", which leaves the final call with the doctor. And a woman who used no contraception at all, and simply cannot raise a child now, has no presumption to lean on. Her abortion depends on whether a doctor agrees that her situation amounts to grave injury.

## When a court says the statute is the limit

A law built on listed grounds and categories has a hard edge, and it showed in July 2022. An unmarried woman, about 22 weeks pregnant, asked the Delhi High Court to let her end the pregnancy. The rules for the 20 to 24 week window did not name single women, and on 15 July the High Court refused her interim relief, saying it "cannot go beyond the Statute" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The Supreme Court stepped in on 21 July 2022. It modified the High Court's order and allowed her to end the pregnancy if a Medical Board at AIIMS Delhi found it safe [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Two courts and a medical board: that is what it took for one woman to get a decision the Act's words did not clearly allow. Our explainer on the September 2022 ruling for unmarried women follows her case to the end.

## Autonomy in the Constitution, not yet in the Act

To widen access, the Supreme Court had to reach past the MTP Act to the Constitution. In its September 2022 judgment it relied on Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009), which recognised a woman's reproductive autonomy, and on the nine-judge privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017), which tied the statutory right to abortion to the right to make reproductive choices under Article 21 [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The court said reproductive autonomy, dignity and privacy give an unmarried woman, just like a married one, "the right of choice on whether or not to bear a child" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

When Parliament amended the Act in 2021, the government said the changes would ensure "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" for women [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Yet the text still routes every decision through a doctor's opinion.

What would a rights-based law change at the clinic counter? The first question would be "Is this your decision?", not "Which ground applies?" A woman's reasons would stay her own instead of being translated into a mental-health clause. And a doctor who personally disapproves could not quietly close her options by declining to form an opinion.

Until the law changes, the practical lesson is simple. Go early. Go to a registered doctor. Say plainly why you cannot continue. Used well, the law's presumptions give you more ground to stand on than the words "doctor's opinion" suggest.
abortion-not-on-request-doctors-opinion.hg:
Kya India mein abortion legal hai? Haan. Kya koi aurat clinic jaakar sirf isliye abortion karwa sakti hai kyunki woh pregnant nahi rehna chahti? Law ke hisaab se, nahi. Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act 1971 mein pass hua aur 1 April 1972 ko lagu hua [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Paanch dashak se zyada ho gaye, aur is law ne aaj tak abortion "on request", yaani sirf maangne par, kabhi nahi diya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Myth: "Mera body, mera legal right"

Yeh soch ki sirf maangna kaafi hai, samajh mein aati hai. Abortion legal hai, aur aurton ko bataya jaata hai ki yeh unki choice hai. Lekin law alag tarah se bana hai. Woh is baat se shuru nahi hota ki aurat kya chahti hai. Woh is baat se shuru hota hai ki doctor kya sochta hai.

Ek hypothetical socho. Bengaluru mein 26 saal ki ek software tester hai, saat hafte pregnant. Woh gynaecologist se kehti hai: "Mujhe yeh pregnancy nahi chahiye." Law ke hisaab se yeh line apne aap mein koi legal ground nahi hai. Uska abortion legal tab banta hai jab doctor good faith mein yeh opinion banaye ki pregnancy continue karne se uski jaan ko khatra hai, ya uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan hoga, ya foetus mein kisi serious abnormality ka bada risk hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

## Sach: grounds, opinions aur teen gate

Law ne teen gate banaye hain, aur har gate par ek doctor khada hai.

| Pregnancy ka stage | Kiski haan chahiye | Kise mil sakta hai |
|---|---|---|
| 20 hafte tak | 1 registered doctor | Koi bhi aurat, agar legal ground ho |
| 20 se 24 hafte | 2 registered doctors | Sirf woh aurtein jo rules ki list mein aati hain |
| 24 hafte ke baad | State ka Medical Board | Sirf substantial foetal abnormality hone par |

Yeh teeno gate 2021 mein amend hue Act mein likhe hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], aur MTP Act ko plain words mein samjhane wala hamara explainer har gate ko detail mein batata hai. Emergency ka rule alag hai: agar aurat ki jaan bachane ke liye turant pregnancy khatam karna zaroori ho, to doctor kisi bhi stage par kadam utha sakta hai.

Har gate par aurat ki consent zaroori hai. Adult aurat ke liye sirf uski apni consent kaafi hai; pati ke signature ki koi zaroorat nahi [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Lekin consent ek shart hai, ground nahi. Doctor ki opinion ke bina sirf consent se abortion legal nahi hota.

Law in gates par kadi nazar rakhta hai. Agar koi aisa insaan abortion kare jo registered medical practitioner nahi hai, ya aisi jagah kare jise Act ke tahat approval nahi mila, to do se saat saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

## "Mental health ko gambhir chot" kab maan li jaati hai

Legal grounds mein mental health sabse chauda darwaza hai, kyunki do situations mein Act khud ise khol kar rakhta hai.

Pehli, contraceptive failure. Agar "any woman or her partner", yaani koi bhi aurat ya uska partner, koi device ya method use kar rahe the aur woh fail ho gaya, to us pregnancy se hone wali anguish ko mental health par gambhir chot "may be presumed", yaani maana ja sakta hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2021 se pehle law mein likha tha "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Doosri, rape. Agar aurat kehti hai ki uski pregnancy rape se hui hai, to us anguish ko mental health par gambhir chot "shall be presumed", yaani maana hi jayega [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne saaf kiya ki iske liye na FIR chahiye, na court ki koi finding, aur yahan rape mein pati ki zabardasti bhi gini jayegi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Dono verbs par dhyan do. Rape ke liye presumption pakka hai: "shall". Condom ya pill fail hone par "may" hai, yaani final call doctor ke haath mein hai. Aur jis aurat ne koi contraception use hi nahi kiya, par abhi bachcha paal nahi sakti? Uske paas sahara lene ke liye koi presumption nahi hai. Uska abortion is par tika hai ki doctor uski situation ko "grave injury" maanta hai ya nahi.

## Jab court kahe ki statute hi limit hai

Listed grounds aur categories par bane law ki sakhti July 2022 mein dikhi. Ek unmarried aurat, jo lagbhag 22 hafte pregnant thi, ne Delhi High Court se abortion ki permission maangi. 20 se 24 hafte wale rules mein single aurton ka naam nahi tha, aur 15 July ko High Court ne use interim relief dene se mana kar diya. Court ne kaha ki woh "cannot go beyond the Statute", yaani law se aage nahi ja sakta [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

21 July 2022 ko Supreme Court ne dakhal diya. Usne High Court ka order modify kiya aur kaha ki agar AIIMS Delhi ka Medical Board ise safe paaye, to woh pregnancy end kar sakti hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Do courts aur ek medical board: ek aurat ko woh decision paane mein itna sab laga, jiski saaf permission Act ke shabdon mein nahi thi. Unmarried aurton aur September 2022 ke ruling par hamara explainer uska case end tak follow karta hai.

## Autonomy Constitution mein hai, Act mein abhi nahi

Access badhane ke liye Supreme Court ko MTP Act se aage jaakar Constitution tak jaana pada. September 2022 ke judgment mein court ne Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009) par bharosa kiya, jisne aurat ki reproductive autonomy ko maana tha. Saath hi nau judges ke privacy wale faisle K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) par bhi, jisne abortion ke statutory right ko Article 21 ke tahat reproductive choices ke right se joda [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Court ne kaha ki reproductive autonomy, dignity aur privacy ek unmarried aurat ko bhi, married aurat ki tarah, "the right of choice on whether or not to bear a child" deti hain, yaani bachcha paida karna hai ya nahi, yeh chunne ka haq [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

2021 mein jab Parliament ne Act amend kiya, tab government ne kaha tha ki isse aurton ko "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" milega [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Phir bhi Act ka har decision aaj bhi doctor ki opinion se hokar hi guzarta hai.

Agar law sach mein rights par tika hota, to clinic counter par kya badalta? Pehla sawaal hota "Kya yeh tumhara decision hai?", na ki "Kaunsa ground lagu hota hai?" Aurat ki wajahein uski apni rehtin, unhe kisi mental-health clause mein fit nahi karna padta. Aur jo doctor personally abortion ke khilaf hai, woh opinion dene se mana karke chupchaap uske raaste band nahi kar paata.

Jab tak law nahi badalta, practical lesson simple hai. Jaldi jao. Registered doctor ke paas jao. Saaf batao ki tum yeh pregnancy kyun continue nahi kar sakti. Law ke presumptions ko sahi se use karo, toh "doctor ki opinion" sunne mein jitna lagta hai, law usse kahin zyada support deta hai.

abortion-pills-without-doctor-risks.en:
Consider a message a 21-year-old in Pune might send her best friend at 2 am: "Took the kit yesterday. Still bleeding a lot. Is this normal?" Nobody in that chat knows how many weeks pregnant she was, whether the pregnancy was in her uterus, or how much bleeding is too much. The tablets in that kit are good medicine. What is missing is everything a doctor puts around them.

## Myth: the kit is a home remedy

The myth runs like this: the kit comes in a box like any other strip of tablets, friends have used it, so it must be safe to take alone. The first half of that is true. India's Health Ministry guidelines (2023) say the mifepristone-misoprostol combination succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

The second half is not. The same guidelines approve the pills only up to nine weeks (63 days), prescribed by a qualified doctor at a clinic linked to an approved abortion facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Most kits are not taken that way. In 2015, an estimated 11.5 million medication abortions took place outside any health facility, 87% of them with a ready-made combipack [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. A combipack is a prescription medicine packed for convenience. It is not a home remedy.

## What the guidelines actually require

Before prescribing, a doctor confirms that you are pregnant and works out how many weeks it has been since the first day of your last period, because the pills are approved only up to nine weeks [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The doctor also looks for signs of a pregnancy outside the uterus, which needs urgent hospital care, not a kit [[nhs-ectopic]], and tells you which bleeding and pain are expected and which are not. And the clinic must have a referral link to an approved facility, so there is somewhere to go if something goes wrong [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

The law also says who may end a pregnancy: a registered medical practitioner, at a place approved under the MTP Act. Since 2002, an abortion by anyone else, or at an unapproved place, is punishable with two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. That reaches anyone who plays abortion provider without being a registered doctor, from a quack to an "experienced" neighbour. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Warning signs that mean hospital, now

Some bleeding and cramping is expected after abortion pills. These are not:

- bleeding that soaks through pad after pad, or large clots
- fever, or foul-smelling discharge
- severe pain in the belly that keeps getting worse
- dizziness or fainting

Any of these can mean an incomplete abortion, heavy blood loss or infection, the same complications the WHO lists for unsafe abortion [[who-abortion]], and each needs a hospital without delay. Pain low down on one side, or pain in the tip of the shoulder, can signal an ectopic pregnancy, one growing outside the uterus, usually in a fallopian tube [[nhs-ectopic]]. It needs urgent hospital care, not more tablets, and if the tube ruptures it is an emergency [[nhs-ectopic]]. See a doctor soon, too, if there is no bleeding at all after the pills or the pregnancy symptoms do not fade: the pregnancy may be continuing, or may be in the wrong place.

Go to the nearest government hospital or call 112. Tell the doctor exactly what you took and when; the doctor needs it to treat you. Do not take more tablets to "finish it", and do not wait for morning out of shame.

## How late or unsupervised use goes wrong

The calendar is the first trap. The nine weeks are counted from the first day of the last period. A woman who counts from the night she had sex, or from the day her period was due, believes she is less far along than she is. Without a check, nobody corrects her.

The second trap is silence. Across six states surveyed in 2015 (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh), 4-16% of women receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications, including infection of the uterus, perforation, sepsis and shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. That is a share of women already in care, not of all abortions. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 15.6% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion reported complications, and 89.7% of them sought treatment [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Seeking care is normal. Arriving late is what turns a treatable problem into a dangerous one.

The stakes are steep. The WHO says deaths from safe abortion are negligible, under 1 per 100,000, but exceed 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. UNFPA India estimates that unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths in India, with close to eight women dying every day from related causes and young women aged 15-19 at the highest risk [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Getting pills the safe way

Start early, and start with a registered doctor or a government hospital. If you are 18 or older, your own consent is the only one the MTP Act requires [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. A doctor who reveals your abortion to anyone not authorised by law can be jailed for up to a year, fined, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Missing the nine-week window does not close the legal door. Up to 20 weeks, one doctor's opinion is enough where continuing the pregnancy would risk your life or gravely injure your physical or mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]; the abortion is then done at a government hospital or approved facility rather than on an outpatient prescription. If you are under 18, a guardian must consent in writing [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]], and the doctor must report the pregnancy to the police, because the POCSO Act treats any sexual activity with someone under 18 as an offence, though your name can be kept out of that report if you and your guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The pills are not the danger. Taking them alone, late or blind is.
abortion-pills-without-doctor-risks.hg:
Socho, Pune ki ek 21 saal ki ladki raat ke 2 baje apni best friend ko aisa message bhej sakti hai: "Kal kit li thi. Abhi bhi bahut bleeding ho rahi hai. Kya yeh normal hai?" Us chat mein kisi ko nahi pata ki woh kitne hafte pregnant thi, pregnancy uske uterus mein thi ya nahi, ya kitni bleeding zyada hoti hai. Us kit ki tablets achhi dawa hain. Kami hai un sab cheezon ki jo ek doctor unke aas-paas rakhta hai.

## Myth: kit ghar ka nuskha hai

Myth kuch aisa hai: kit baaki tablets ki strip ki tarah ek dibbe mein aati hai, doston ne use kiya hai, toh akele lena bhi safe hi hoga. Iska pehla hissa sach hai. India ki Health Ministry ki guidelines (2023) kehti hain ki mifepristone-misoprostol combination shuruaati abortions mein 95-99% cases mein kaamyaab hota hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Doosra hissa sach nahi hai. Wahi guidelines in pills ko sirf 9 hafte (63 din) tak approve karti hain, aur woh bhi ek qualified doctor ke prescription par, aise clinic mein jo kisi approved abortion facility se juda ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Zyada tar kits is tarah nahi li jaati. 2015 mein lagbhag 11.5 million medication abortions kisi bhi health facility ke bahar hue, aur unmein se 87% mein ready-made combipack use hua [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Combipack ek prescription wali dawa hai jise suvidha ke liye pack kiya gaya hai. Yeh ghar ka nuskha nahi hai.

## Guidelines asal mein kya maangti hain

Prescription dene se pehle doctor confirm karta hai ki tum pregnant ho aur hisaab lagata hai ki tumhare last period ke pehle din se kitne hafte hue, kyunki pills sirf 9 hafte tak approved hain [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Doctor yeh bhi dekhta hai ki kahin pregnancy uterus ke bahar toh nahi, kyunki uske liye kit nahi, turant hospital care chahiye [[nhs-ectopic]], aur samjhata hai ki kaunsi bleeding aur dard expected hai aur kaunsa nahi. Aur clinic ka kisi approved facility se referral link hona zaroori hai, taaki kuch galat ho toh jaane ki jagah ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Law yeh bhi batata hai ki pregnancy kaun khatam kar sakta hai: ek registered medical practitioner, MTP Act ke tahat approved jagah par. 2002 se, agar abortion koi aur kare, ya bina approval wali jagah par ho, toh 2 se 7 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ki saza hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Yeh har us insaan par lagu hota hai jo registered doctor na hote hue abortion provider ban baithta hai, jhola-chhaap se lekar "tajurbe wali" padosan tak. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Warning signs jinka matlab hai abhi hospital

Abortion pills ke baad kuch bleeding aur cramps expected hain. Yeh nahi:

- aisi bleeding jo ek ke baad ek pad bhigo de, ya khoon ke bade thakke
- bukhaar, ya badbudaar discharge
- pet mein tez dard jo badhta hi jaaye
- chakkar aana ya behosh hona

Inmein se koi bhi incomplete abortion, bahut zyada khoon behne ya infection ka sign ho sakta hai, wahi complications jo WHO unsafe abortion ke liye batata hai [[who-abortion]], aur har ek mein bina der kiye hospital jaana zaroori hai. Pet ke neeche ek taraf dard, ya kandhe ke sire mein dard, ectopic pregnancy ka sign ho sakta hai, yaani aisi pregnancy jo uterus ke bahar, aksar fallopian tube mein, badh rahi ho [[nhs-ectopic]]. Iske liye aur tablets nahi, turant hospital care chahiye, aur agar tube phat jaaye toh yeh emergency hai [[nhs-ectopic]]. Agar pills ke baad bilkul bleeding na ho, ya pregnancy ke symptoms khatam na hon, toh bhi jaldi doctor ko dikhao: ho sakta hai pregnancy abhi bhi chal rahi ho, ya galat jagah par ho.

Sabse nazdeeki sarkari hospital jao ya 112 par call karo. Doctor ko saaf batao ki tumne kya liya aur kab; ilaaj ke liye doctor ko yeh jaanna zaroori hai. "Kaam poora karne" ke liye aur tablets mat lo, aur sharm ki wajah se subah ka intezaar mat karo.

## Der se ya bina nigrani ke lene par kya galat hota hai

Pehla jaal calendar hai. 9 hafte last period ke pehle din se gine jaate hain. Jo aurat us raat se ginti hai jab sex hua, ya us din se jab period aana tha, woh samajhti hai ki pregnancy asal se kam hafte ki hai. Bina check ke koi uski galti theek nahi karta.

Doosra jaal chuppi hai. 2015 mein jin chhe states mein survey hua (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu aur Uttar Pradesh), wahan abortion ke baad care le rahi 4-16% aurton ka ilaaj serious complications ke liye ho raha tha, jaise uterus ka infection, perforation, sepsis aur shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Yeh un aurton ka hissa hai jo pehle se care mein thi, saare abortions ka nahi. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications batayi, aur unmein se 89.7% ne ilaaj karwaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ilaaj ke liye jaana normal hai. Der se pahunchna hi ek theek ho sakne wali problem ko khatarnak bana deta hai.

Daav bahut bada hai. WHO kehta hai ki safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hoti hai, 100,000 mein 1 se bhi kam, lekin jahan unsafe abortion aam hai, wahan yeh 100,000 mein 200 se zyada hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. UNFPA India ka estimate hai ki India mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah unsafe abortion hai, isse judi wajahon se har din lagbhag aath aurton ki maut hoti hai, aur 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko sabse zyada khatra hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Pills ka safe raasta

Jaldi shuru karo, aur registered doctor ya sarkari hospital se shuru karo. Agar tum 18 ya usse zyada ki ho, toh MTP Act sirf tumhari apni consent maangta hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Jo doctor tumhara abortion kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne permission nahi di, use ek saal tak ki jail, jurmana, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

9 hafte ki window nikal jaane se legal darwaza band nahi hota. 20 hafte tak ek doctor ki opinion kaafi hai, agar pregnancy jaari rakhne se tumhari jaan ko khatra ho ya tumhari physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan pahunche [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]; tab abortion outpatient prescription ke bajaye sarkari hospital ya approved facility mein hota hai. Agar tum 18 se kam ki ho, toh guardian ki likhit consent zaroori hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]], aur doctor ko pregnancy ki report police ko deni hoti hai, kyunki POCSO Act ke tahat 18 se kam umr ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity offence hai, lekin agar tum aur tumhare guardian kahein, toh us report mein tumhara naam daalna zaroori nahi hota [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Khatra pills mein nahi hai. Khatra unhe akele, der se ya andhere mein lene mein hai.

abortion-privacy-family-police-answered.en:
Imagine a 23-year-old in Lucknow, unmarried, seven weeks pregnant and living with her parents. She has saved a clinic's number under a fake name. What stops her from calling is a list of questions: will they want a husband's or a father's signature, will they phone home, will the police come? Each has a legal answer, and most of the answers are on her side.

Most abortions in India never reach an official record. The Health Ministry recorded 701,415 abortions in 2014-15, against a research estimate of 15.6 million in 2015, and about 11.5 million of those were medication abortions done outside health facilities [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. A chemist's counter can feel more private than a clinic. In law, it is the other way round: the duty of secrecy binds the doctor, not the chemist. What follows is general information, not legal advice.

## Do I need anyone's permission?

If you are 18 or older, no. Under the MTP Act, an adult woman's own consent is the only consent an abortion needs; a guardian's written consent is required only if she is under 18 or mentally ill [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The Act gives no role to a husband, a partner, parents or in-laws.

What the law does require is a doctor's opinion. Up to 20 weeks, one registered doctor must agree that continuing the pregnancy would risk your life or gravely injure your physical or mental health; from 20 to 24 weeks, two doctors must agree and you must fall in a listed category [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. That opinion is about your health, not your family's approval. Our plain-words guide to the MTP Act explains each week limit, and our data story on husbands and mothers-in-law shows where families still reach into the decision.

## Can the doctor or hospital tell my family, or the police?

Not your family. Since 2021, Section 5A of the MTP Act bars a registered medical practitioner from revealing the name or other particulars of a woman whose pregnancy was ended, except to a person authorised by law. Breaking it can mean up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. For an adult, being her husband or parent does not make someone "authorised by law". The section names doctors, so it is fair to ask a clinic who else will see your file.

The police are a different question. An abortion done by a registered doctor within the Act's conditions is legal, so there is no crime for them to look into. Outside the Act it is different: Section 88 of the BNS still punishes causing a miscarriage, and it expressly covers a woman who causes her own [[gazette-bns-2023]]. That is one more reason to go to a registered doctor.

For an adult having a legal abortion, the main exception is rape. If you tell a hospital the pregnancy came from rape, Section 397 of the BNSS obliges it to treat you free and to inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Your abortion does not have to wait for any police case: the Supreme Court said in 2022 that no FIR or court finding is needed before a woman relies on the rape ground [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## I'm unmarried: will they ask questions?

They may ask medical questions; they cannot make marriage a condition. Since 2021 the contraceptive-failure ground covers "any woman or her partner", not only a married woman or her husband [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. On 29 September 2022 the Supreme Court held that shutting unmarried or single women out of the 20-24 week window would violate the right to equality [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]:

> "The rights of reproductive autonomy, dignity, and privacy under Article 21 give an unmarried woman the right of choice on whether or not to bear a child, on a similar footing of a married woman."

The court built this on the nine-judge privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017), which tied the right to an abortion under the MTP Act to the constitutional right to make reproductive choices [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].
