A clinic that insists on a husband or a marriage certificate is asking for something the law does not. Our explainer on the 2022 ruling for unmarried women tells the story of the case itself.

## I'm under 18: what must be reported, and can my name stay out?

Two extra rules apply. A guardian must give written consent [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. And because any sexual act with a person under 18 is an offence under POCSO, the doctor must report the pregnancy to the police; failing to report can mean up to 6 months in prison or a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

What can stay private is your identity. Since September 2022, a doctor ending a minor's pregnancy need not disclose her name or personal details in that police report if she and her guardian ask, and need not reveal them in any criminal case that follows [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. You have to ask: say it at the first visit. Minors are one of the categories allowed an abortion up to 24 weeks [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Our explainer on POCSO's reporting rule sets out what this fix leaves unsolved.

## What if my privacy is breached?

A doctor who reveals your abortion to someone not authorised by law commits an offence under Section 5A [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Write down who told whom, what and when, keep screenshots, and take them to the police.

If the pregnancy followed rape and someone publishes your name or anything that could identify you, that is a separate crime: Section 72 of the BNS punishes it with up to 2 years in prison and a fine, unless you authorise it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. For a child, POCSO bars any media report from revealing her name, address, photograph, family, school or neighbourhood [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Section 72 is rarely invoked. In July-December 2024, the first six months of the BNS, police across India registered just 11 cases under it [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A complaint is how that number changes.
abortion-privacy-family-police-answered.hg:
Socho, Lucknow ki ek 23 saal ki ladki. Shaadi nahi hui, saat hafte ki pregnancy hai, aur woh mummy-papa ke saath rehti hai. Usne ek clinic ka number phone mein fake naam se save kar rakha hai. Par call karne se pehle kai sawaal use rok lete hain: kya woh husband ya papa ka sign maangenge, kya ghar phone karenge, kya police aayegi? Har sawaal ka legal jawaab hai, aur zyada tar jawaab uske haq mein hain.

India mein zyada tar abortions kabhi kisi official record tak pahunchte hi nahi. Health Ministry ne 2014-15 mein sirf 701,415 abortions darj kiye, jabki ek research ke andaaze se 2015 mein 15.6 million abortions hue. Inmein se kareeb 11.5 million hospital ya clinic ke bahar dawaiyon se hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Chemist ka counter clinic se zyada private lag sakta hai, lekin kanoon mein baat ulti hai: raaz rakhne ki zimmedari doctor par hai, chemist par nahi. Aage di gayi jaankari general samajh ke liye hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya mujhe kisi ki permission chahiye?

Agar tum 18 ya usse badi ho, toh nahi. MTP Act mein adult aurat ki apni consent hi kaafi hai; guardian ki likhit consent sirf tab chahiye jab ladki 18 se kam ho ya mentally ill ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Is kanoon mein husband, partner, parents ya sasural walon ka koi role nahi hai.

Haan, doctor ki raay zaroori hai. 20 hafte tak ek registered doctor ko maanna hoga ki pregnancy jaari rakhne se tumhari jaan ko khatra hai, ya physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan hoga. 20 se 24 hafte ke beech do doctors ki raay chahiye, aur tumhara rules mein likhi kisi category mein hona zaroori hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Yeh raay tumhari health ke baare mein hai, family ki manzoori ke baare mein nahi. MTP Act par hamari aasaan guide har hafte ki limit samjhaati hai, aur husbands aur saas par hamari data story dikhati hai ki family aaj bhi is faisle mein kahan-kahan dakhal deti hai.

## Kya doctor ya hospital mere ghar walon ko, ya police ko bata sakta hai?

Ghar walon ko nahi. 2021 se MTP Act ka Section 5A registered doctor ko us aurat ka naam ya koi aur detail batane se rokta hai jiska abortion hua hai, siwaay us insaan ke jise kanoon ijaazat deta ho. Rule todne par ek saal tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Adult aurat ke case mein, husband ya parent hone bhar se koi "authorised by law" nahi ban jaata. Yeh section doctors ka naam leta hai, isliye clinic se poochna theek hai ki tumhari file aur kaun-kaun dekhega.

Police ka sawaal alag hai. Registered doctor ke haathon, MTP Act ki sharton ke andar hua abortion legal hai, yaani police ke liye jaanch karne layak koi jurm hi nahi hai. Act ke bahar baat badal jaati hai: BNS ka Section 88 aaj bhi miscarriage karwane ko jurm maanta hai, aur saaf likhta hai ki khud apna miscarriage karne wali aurat bhi isme aati hai [[gazette-bns-2023]]. Registered doctor ke paas jaane ki yeh ek aur wajah hai.

Adult aurat ke legal abortion mein sabse badi exception rape hai. Agar tum hospital ko batati ho ki pregnancy rape se hui hai, toh BNSS ke Section 397 ke tahat hospital ko tumhara free ilaaj karna hoga aur police ko khabar deni hogi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Tumhare abortion ko kisi police case ka intezaar nahi karna padta: Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki rape wale ground ke liye na FIR chahiye, na court ka faisla [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## Meri shaadi nahi hui hai: kya woh sawaal poochenge?

Health se jude sawaal pooch sakte hain, par shaadi ko shart nahi bana sakte. 2021 se contraceptive failure (jaise condom ya pill fail hona) wala ground "any woman or her partner" par laagu hota hai, sirf married woman ya uske husband par nahi [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court ne kaha ki unmarried ya single auraton ko 20-24 hafte wali window se bahar rakhna barabari ke haq ke khilaaf hoga [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]:

> "The rights of reproductive autonomy, dignity, and privacy under Article 21 give an unmarried woman the right of choice on whether or not to bear a child, on a similar footing of a married woman."

Yaani bachcha paida karna hai ya nahi, yeh chunne ka haq unmarried aurat ka bhi utna hi hai jitna married aurat ka. Court ne yeh baat 2017 ke Puttaswamy faisle par tikaayi, jisme privacy par nau judges ki bench ne MTP Act ke tahat abortion ke haq ko reproductive choices ke constitutional haq se joda tha [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Jo clinic husband ya marriage certificate maangne par ad jaaye, woh aisi cheez maang raha hai jo kanoon nahi maangta. Unmarried auraton ke liye 2022 ke faisle par hamara alag explainer poora case batata hai.

## Meri umar 18 se kam hai: kya report hoga, aur kya mera naam chhupa reh sakta hai?

Yahan do rules aur judte hain. Guardian ki likhit consent chahiye [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Aur kyunki POCSO mein 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual act jurm hai, doctor ko pregnancy police ko report karni hogi; report na karne par 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Jo chhupa reh sakta hai, woh hai tumhari pehchaan. September 2022 se, minor ka abortion karne wale doctor ko police report mein uska naam ya personal details likhna zaroori nahi, agar ladki aur uske guardian aisa kahein. Aage ke kisi criminal case mein bhi doctor ko pehchaan batane ki zaroorat nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yeh tumhe khud maangna hoga: pehli visit mein hi keh do. Rules mein minors un categories mein hain jinhe 24 hafte tak abortion ki ijaazat hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. POCSO ke reporting rule par hamara explainer batata hai ki yeh hal kin baaton ko ab bhi nahi suljhaata.

## Agar meri privacy toot jaaye, toh main kya karun?

Jo doctor tumhare abortion ki baat kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise kanoon ne ijaazat nahi di, woh Section 5A ke tahat jurm karta hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Likh lo ki kisne, kise, kya aur kab bataya, screenshots sambhal kar rakho, aur police ke paas jao.

Agar pregnancy rape se hui aur koi tumhara naam ya pehchaan batane wali koi bhi baat publish kar de, toh yeh alag jurm hai: BNS ka Section 72 iske liye 2 saal tak ki jail aur fine ki saza rakhta hai, jab tak tumne likh kar ijaazat na di ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Bachchon ke case mein POCSO kisi bhi media report mein bachche ka naam, address, photo, family, school ya mohalla batane par rok lagata hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Section 72 bahut kam use hota hai. BNS ke pehle chhah mahine, yaani July se December 2024 mein, poore India mein police ne iske tahat sirf 11 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh number tabhi badlega jab log complaint karenge.

abortion-stigma-india-silence-risk.en:
Imagine a 27-year-old in Meerut, married, with a two-year-old son. She is pregnant again and does not want to be, and the only word her family has for what she is thinking is "paap", a sin. So she says nothing, buys tablets from a chemist in another neighbourhood, and when the bleeding will not slow on the second night, she waits for morning so that nobody asks questions. What she wanted was legal. What put her at risk was the silence around it.

## Legal for over 50 years, still whispered

India's Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act came into force on 1 April 1972 [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. It grew out of a government committee, set up in 1964, which reported in 1966 that the old law was "too restrictive" and should be liberalised [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]]. Yet for almost half a century the law carried its own stigma: its contraceptive-failure ground covered only "any married woman or her husband", as if unmarried women did not have sex [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

When Parliament amended the law in 2021, the government said the changes would ensure "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" for women. Even that took time: the Lok Sabha passed the bill on 17 March 2020, the Rajya Sabha only on 16 March 2021 [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]].

At home, many families still speak of abortion only in whispers, as a sin or a disgrace, and many young women grow up knowing the word but not that the act is legal. That gap between law and belief is what stigma means here: something lawful, treated as shameful, and therefore hidden.

## What stigma does to the numbers

Stigma hides abortion even from the people who count it. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), women reported that just 2.9% of their last pregnancies in the previous five years had ended in abortion [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A national study estimated that one third of all pregnancies in 2015 ended in induced abortion [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. The two measure different things in different years, but a gap that wide is what heavy under-reporting looks like.

Deaths hide too. The WHO says maternal deaths from unsafe abortion are often misclassified and under-reported because of stigma; even so, about 8% of maternal deaths worldwide in 2009-2020 were linked to abortion [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. In its 2023 guidelines, India's Health Ministry still puts unsafe abortion at 8% of maternal deaths, using cause-of-death data from 2001-03 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]], and UNFPA India estimates that close to 8 women die every day from causes related to unsafe abortion [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. When the government's own figure rests on data more than 20 years old, the silence is in the system too.

Deaths from safe abortion are negligible, under 1 per 100,000 abortions, but exceed 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common, the WHO says [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Shame does not cause those deaths by itself. It pushes women towards the conditions that do: secrecy, the wrong provider and delay.

## From 'paap' to the chemist counter

When something feels shameful, people choose the option where nobody looks at them. In NFHS-5, 26.2% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion had it at home, 26.9% said they did it themselves, rising to 30.0% in rural areas, and only 20.3% went to a public facility [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The pills are not the villain. Prescribed by a qualified doctor, the mifepristone-misoprostol combination succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions up to nine weeks [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The danger lies in what secrecy strips away: nobody checks how far along the pregnancy is or whether it is ectopic, nobody explains which bleeding is normal, and when something goes wrong, shame makes a woman wait. One step further, secrecy leads to the unqualified provider, though an abortion by anyone who is not a registered doctor, or at an unapproved place, carries two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. The quack's business runs on the same silence.

## Stigma inside the clinic

Stigma also wears a white coat. Picture the scenes that keep women away: a receptionist asking an unmarried woman where her husband is, a doctor asking a mother of two why she didn't think before, a clinic insisting that a husband or parent sign.

None of this is required by law (what follows is general information, not legal advice). An adult woman's own consent is the only consent the MTP Act needs [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Since 2021, the contraceptive-failure ground covers "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], and in 2022 the Supreme Court held that unmarried and single women have the same access as married women, including between 20 and 24 weeks [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. And a doctor who gossips commits a crime: under Section 5A, a registered doctor who reveals a woman's abortion to anyone not authorised by law faces up to a year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

A clinic that moralises does not prevent an abortion. It moves it: to a chemist, to a later week, to a worse provider.

## How to talk about it at home

Stigma breaks the way it was built, one conversation at a time. If someone in your family is pregnant and does not want to be, the most protective thing you can say is six words long: "It's legal. Let's see a doctor." In the Meerut house, those words would have changed the second night. Then:

- Use plain words: "abortion" or "ending a pregnancy", not "paap" or "galti".
- Don't ask her to justify it. Ask what she needs: a ride, money, company, privacy.
- Offer to go with her to a government hospital or an approved clinic, and to the follow-up.
- Learn the danger signs (very heavy bleeding, fainting, fever, severe pain) so you can say "hospital, now" without a debate.
- Keep it to yourself. It is her story to tell.

Silence has a male side too. In NFHS-5, 35.1% of men aged 15-49 agreed that "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A husband, brother or friend who treats an unplanned pregnancy as a shared problem breaks two silences at once. If it weighs on her, or on you, afterwards, Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]] is the Health Ministry's free counselling line, open round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
abortion-stigma-india-silence-risk.hg:
Socho, Meerut ki ek 27 saal ki shaadishuda aurat, jiska do saal ka beta hai. Woh phir se pregnant hai aur yeh pregnancy nahi chahti, lekin jo woh soch rahi hai uske liye uske ghar mein ek hi shabd hai: "paap". Isliye woh kuch nahi kehti, doosre mohalle ke chemist se goliyan khareed leti hai, aur doosri raat jab bleeding kam hi nahi hoti, tab bhi subah tak intezaar karti hai taaki koi sawaal na pooche. Jo woh chahti thi, woh legal tha. Jisne use khatre mein daala, woh thi uske aas-paas ki chuppi.

## 50 saal se zyada samay se legal, phir bhi phusphusahat mein

India ka Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act 1 April 1972 ko laagu hua [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Yeh 1964 mein bani ek sarkari committee se nikla tha, jisne 1966 ki apni report mein kaha tha ki purana kanoon "too restrictive", yaani bahut sakht, hai aur use naram kiya jaana chahiye [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]]. Phir bhi lagbhag aadhi sadi tak kanoon ke andar khud ek stigma baitha raha: contraceptive failure wala ground sirf "any married woman or her husband" par laagu hota tha, jaise unmarried auratein sex karti hi na hon [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Jab 2021 mein Parliament ne kanoon badla, toh sarkar ne kaha ki in badlaavon se auraton ko "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" milegi. Yeh badlaav bhi dheere aaya: Lok Sabha ne bill 17 March 2020 ko paas kiya, aur Rajya Sabha ne kahin jaakar 16 March 2021 ko [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]].

Ghar mein aaj bhi kai families abortion ki baat sirf phusphusa kar karti hain, paap ya badnaami ki tarah, aur kai ladkiyan yeh shabd toh jaanti hain, par yeh nahi jaantin ki yeh legal hai. Kanoon aur soch ke beech ka yahi faasla yahan stigma ka matlab hai: jo cheez legal hai, use sharam ki baat maana jaata hai, aur isliye chhupaya jaata hai.

## Stigma numbers ke saath kya karta hai

Stigma abortion ko unse bhi chhupa deta hai jo ginti karte hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein auraton ne bataya ki survey se pehle ke paanch saalon mein unki pichhli pregnancies mein se sirf 2.9% abortion par khatam hui [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Wahin ek national study ka andaaza hai ki 2015 mein India ki saari pregnancies mein se ek-tihaai induced abortion par khatam hui [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Dono alag cheezein, alag saalon mein naapte hain, lekin itna bada faasla wahi hai jo bahut kam reporting mein dikhta hai.

Maut bhi chhup jaati hai. WHO kehta hai ki unsafe abortion se hui maternal deaths aksar galat category mein darj hoti hain aur stigma ki wajah se kam report hoti hain; phir bhi duniya bhar mein 2009-2020 ki kareeb 8% maternal deaths abortion se judi thi [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. India ki Health Ministry apni 2023 ki guidelines mein aaj bhi unsafe abortion ko 8% maternal deaths ki wajah batati hai, aur iske liye 2001-03 ka cause-of-death data use karti hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. UNFPA India ka andaaza hai ki unsafe abortion se judi wajahon se roz kareeb 8 auratein marti hain [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Jab sarkar ka apna aankda 20 saal se zyada purane data par tika ho, toh chuppi system mein bhi hai.

WHO ke mutabik safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hai, har 100,000 abortions par 1 se bhi kam, lekin jahan unsafe abortion aam hai wahan yeh 200 per 100,000 se zyada hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Sharam akele in mauton ki wajah nahi hai. Lekin woh auraton ko unhi halaat ki taraf dhakelti hai jo jaan leti hain: chhupana, galat provider aur der.

## 'Paap' se chemist ke counter tak

Jab koi cheez sharam ki lagti hai, toh log wahi raasta chunte hain jahan koi unhe dekhe nahi. NFHS-5 mein, jin auraton ki pichhli pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.2% ka abortion ghar par hua, 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone khud kiya, gaon mein yeh 30.0% tha, aur sirf 20.3% public facility gayin [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Goliyan villain nahi hain. Qualified doctor ke prescription par mifepristone-misoprostol combination nau hafte tak ke early abortions mein 95-99% baar kaamyaab hota hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Khatra us cheez mein hai jo chhupane se chhin jaati hai: koi check nahi karta ki pregnancy kitne hafte ki hai ya ectopic toh nahi, koi nahi batata ki kaun si bleeding normal hai, aur jab kuch gadbad hoti hai, toh sharam aurat ko intezaar karwaati hai. Ek kadam aage, chuppi jhola-chhaap tak le jaati hai, jabki agar abortion registered doctor ke alawa koi aur kare, ya unapproved jagah par ho, toh karne wale ko do se saat saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Jhola-chhaap ka dhandha isi chuppi par chalta hai.

## Clinic ke andar stigma

Stigma white coat bhi pehenta hai. Woh scenes socho jo auraton ko door rakhte hain: receptionist ka ek unmarried ladki se poochna ki husband kahan hai, doctor ka do bachchon ki maa se poochna ki pehle kyun nahi socha, clinic ka zid karna ki husband ya parent sign karein.

Kanoon inmein se kuch nahi maangta (aage ki baatein general jaankari hain, legal advice nahi). MTP Act mein adult aurat ki apni consent hi kaafi hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 2021 se contraceptive failure wala ground "any woman or her partner" par laagu hota hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], aur 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki unmarried aur single auraton ko bhi married auraton jitni hi access hai, 20 se 24 hafte ke beech bhi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Aur jo doctor gossip karta hai, woh jurm karta hai: Section 5A ke tahat, jo registered doctor kisi aurat ka abortion kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise kanoon ne ijaazat nahi di, use ek saal tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Jo clinic lecture deta hai, woh abortion rokta nahi. Bas use kahin aur dhakel deta hai: chemist ke paas, aage ke hafton mein, kisi badtar provider ke paas.

## Ghar par iske baare mein baat kaise karein

Stigma jaise bana tha, waise hi tootega: ek-ek baatcheet se. Agar tumhare ghar mein koi pregnant hai aur yeh pregnancy nahi chahti, toh sabse zyada bachane wali baat bas itni si hai: "Yeh legal hai. Chalo doctor ko dikhate hain." Meerut wale ghar mein yahi chand shabd us doosri raat ko badal dete. Phir:

- Seedhe shabd use karo: "abortion" ya "pregnancy khatam karna", "paap" ya "galti" nahi.
- Usse safai mat maango. Poocho use kya chahiye: koi le jaane wala, paise, saath, ya privacy.
- Sarkari hospital ya approved clinic tak, aur follow-up par bhi, saath chalne ki offer do.
- Danger signs (bahut zyada bleeding, behoshi, bukhaar, tez dard) yaad rakho, taaki bina behas ke keh sako: "abhi hospital chalo".
- Baat apne tak rakho. Yeh uski kahani hai, wahi batayegi.

Chuppi ka ek mardana pehlu bhi hai. NFHS-5 mein 15-49 saal ke 35.1% mardon ne maana ki "contraception is women's business and a man should not have to worry about it", yaani contraception auraton ka kaam hai aur mard ko iski fikr nahi karni chahiye [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jo husband, bhai ya dost unplanned pregnancy ko saanjhi problem maanta hai, woh ek saath do chuppiyan todta hai. Agar baad mein yeh bojh use, ya tumhe, bhaari lage, toh Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call karo [[tele-manas]]; yeh Health Ministry ki free counselling line hai jo din-raat khuli rehti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

after-24-weeks-medical-board-courts.en:
Consider a hypothetical. A 19-year-old college student in Indore is raped by a man she knows. She tells no one, and months later a scan shows she is 25 weeks pregnant. One week earlier, the law had a route for her. Now it has a Medical Board built for a different problem, and the courts. Our plain-words guide to the MTP Act covers the earlier stages; this piece is about the wall at week 24. It is general information, not legal advice.

## What exactly happens after 24 weeks?

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act closes its gates in order: one doctor's opinion up to 20 weeks, then two doctors, and only for listed categories of women, up to 24 [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

After 24 weeks, the Act keeps one planned route. Since 2021 there is no upper limit at all when an abortion is needed because a Medical Board has diagnosed a substantial foetal abnormality [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Separately, a doctor may end a pregnancy at any stage when that is immediately necessary to save the woman's life [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

At week 25, then, the legal question is no longer "Why can't you continue?" but "What did the scan find?" A pregnancy from rape, with no foetal abnormality and no immediate threat to her life, has no route in the Act.

## Who sits on a Medical Board, and how fast must it act?

Every state and union territory must set up Medical Boards. Each must include at least a gynaecologist, a paediatrician and a radiologist or sonologist [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

The rules set a clock. A board must give its opinion within three days of receiving the request. If it approves, the abortion must be carried out, with safety precautions and counselling, within five days of the request [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

Under the Act, its job is narrow: to decide whether the foetus has a substantial abnormality. The woman's age, her reasons and how the pregnancy began are not its question.

Two practical points. These clocks are written for requests on the ground of a substantial foetal abnormality [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. And to find the board, ask the gynaecology department of the district hospital or the nearest government medical college.

## Why does a rape survivor past 24 weeks have to go to court?

Because the 2021 exemption covers only foetal abnormalities. Rule 3B, notified on 12 October 2021, lists survivors of sexual assault, rape or incest, and minors, among seven categories of women eligible up to 24 weeks [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

The Act also presumes that the anguish of a pregnancy caused by rape is a grave injury to her mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. But that presumption is written for the first two gates. At week 25 it has nothing left to open. Unless her life is at immediate risk, a rape survivor or a minor past 24 weeks has no route in the statute and must petition a High Court or the Supreme Court [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Parliament knew this kind of case. When the Rajya Sabha passed the amendment, the government noted that courts had been receiving petitions for abortions beyond the old 20-week limit [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]], both for foetal abnormalities and for pregnancies from sexual violence [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. After almost a year between the Lok Sabha vote on 17 March 2020 and the Rajya Sabha's on 16 March 2021 [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]], the amendment removed the upper limit for one of those two groups. For the other, it moved the deadline from 20 weeks to 24.

## What does a court petition involve?

A petition asks judges to allow what the Act does not. Expect four things.

**A lawyer.** If the family cannot pay, Legal Services Authorities provide free legal aid [[nalsa]].

**Doctors' evidence.** Expect the court to ask doctors whether ending the pregnancy is safe. In a 2022 case within the 24-week limit, the Delhi High Court refused interim relief to an unmarried woman about 22 weeks pregnant; on 21 July 2022 the Supreme Court modified that order and allowed her to end the pregnancy if a Medical Board at AIIMS Delhi found it safe [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**Anonymity.** Ask for it from the first filing. The woman in that case appears in the law reports only as "X".

**Time, and no guarantee.** Every day spent drafting, listing and hearing is a day added to the pregnancy, and the court may still say no.

## How can families avoid reaching this point?

Late discovery can have ordinary causes: a girl hides a pregnancy out of fear, no one recognises it, or the family fears what a hospital visit will set off.

That last fear is real for minors. Every pregnancy in a girl under 18 must be reported to the police under POCSO. The Supreme Court observed in 2022 that this leaves a pregnant minor and her guardian choosing between a registered doctor, with possible criminal proceedings, and an unqualified provider [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The same judgment said the doctor need not reveal the girl's identity or personal details in that report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Two more facts remove reasons to delay. To use the rape ground, a woman needs no FIR and no proof in court [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. And a doctor who reveals her name or details to anyone not authorised by law faces up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

The rest happens at home. A girl who expects anger is more likely to hide a missed period; one who expects help is more likely to speak up. Tell her before anything happens: if something ever happens to your body, come to us, and we will not blame you. Then act within days, not weeks.

Whatever she decides, help exists. Since November 2023 a Nirbhaya Fund scheme offers minor girls made pregnant by rape shelter, medical and maternity care, legal aid, counselling and education support under one roof [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]]. NALSA's 2018 scheme sets compensation of Rs 3 lakh to Rs 4 lakh for a pregnancy resulting from rape, with limits 50% higher for a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].
after-24-weeks-medical-board-courts.hg:
Ek hypothetical sochiye. Indore mein 19 saal ki ek college student ke saath uske ek jaan-pehchaan wale ne rape kiya. Usne kisi ko nahi bataya, aur mahino baad ek scan se pata chalta hai ki woh 25 hafte pregnant hai. Ek hafta pehle tak law mein uske liye raasta tha. Ab bacha hai ek Medical Board jo kisi aur problem ke liye bana hai, aur courts. MTP Act ko plain words mein samjhane wala hamara explainer pehle ke stages cover karta hai; yeh story 24 hafte wali deewar ke baare mein hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 24 hafte ke baad asal mein kya hota hai?

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act ke gate ek-ek karke band hote hain: 20 hafte tak ek doctor ki opinion, phir 24 hafte tak do doctors, aur woh bhi sirf rules ki list wali aurton ke liye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

24 hafte ke baad Act mein bas ek planned raasta bachta hai. 2021 se aise abortion ki koi upper limit nahi hai jiski zaroorat isliye pade ki Medical Board ne foetus mein substantial abnormality diagnose ki hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Iske alawa, agar aurat ki jaan bachane ke liye turant pregnancy khatam karna zaroori ho, to doctor kisi bhi stage par aisa kar sakta hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Yaani 25ve hafte mein legal sawaal badal jaata hai. Ab sawaal yeh nahi ki "Aap continue kyun nahi kar sakti?" Sawaal yeh hai ki "Scan mein kya nikla?" Agar pregnancy rape se hai, foetus mein koi abnormality nahi, aur aurat ki jaan ko turant khatra nahi, to Act mein koi raasta nahi.

## Medical Board mein kaun hota hai, aur use kitni jaldi opinion deni hoti hai?

Har state aur union territory ko Medical Boards banane hote hain. Har board mein kam se kam ek gynaecologist, ek paediatrician aur ek radiologist ya sonologist hona chahiye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Rules mein ghadi bhi tay hai. Request milne ke teen din ke andar board ko apni opinion deni hoti hai. Agar board haan kahe, to request ke paanch din ke andar abortion ho jaana chahiye, poori safety precautions aur counselling ke saath [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

Act ke hisaab se board ka kaam narrow hai: bas yeh dekhna ki foetus mein substantial abnormality hai ya nahi. Aurat ki umar, uski wajahein, aur pregnancy kaise hui, yeh board ka sawaal hi nahi hai.

Do practical baatein. Yeh ghadi substantial foetal abnormality ke ground wali requests ke liye likhi gayi hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Aur board dhoondhne ke liye district hospital ke gynae department mein poochhiye, ya paas ke government medical college mein.

## Rape survivor ko 24 hafte ke baad court kyun jaana padta hai?

Kyunki 2021 wali chhoot sirf foetal abnormalities ke liye hai. 12 October 2021 ko notify hue Rule 3B mein saat categories ki aurtein hain jo 24 hafte tak abortion karwa sakti hain. Inme sexual assault, rape ya incest ki survivors aur minors bhi shaamil hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

Act yeh bhi maanta hai ki rape se hui pregnancy ki anguish aurat ki mental health par gambhir chot hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Lekin yeh presumption sirf pehle do gates ke liye likha gaya hai. 25ve hafte mein iske paas kholne ko koi darwaza nahi bachta. Jab tak uski jaan ko turant khatra na ho, 24 hafte ke baad rape survivor ya minor ke liye statute mein koi raasta nahi hai, aur use High Court ya Supreme Court mein petition daalni padti hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Parliament aise cases ko jaanti thi. Jab Rajya Sabha ne amendment pass kiya, tab government ne khud bataya tha ki courts mein purani 20 hafte ki limit [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]] ke baad abortion ke liye petitions aa rahi thin, kuch foetal abnormality ki wajah se aur kuch sexual violence se hui pregnancies ki wajah se [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Lok Sabha ne bill 17 March 2020 ko pass kiya aur Rajya Sabha ne 16 March 2021 ko, yaani qareeb ek saal baad [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Aakhir mein in do groups mein se ek ke liye upper limit poori tarah hata di gayi. Doosre ke liye deadline bas 20 se 24 hafte hui.

## Court petition mein kya-kya hota hai?

Petition mein judges se woh permission maangi jaati hai jo Act nahi deta. Chaar cheezon ke liye taiyaar rahiye.

**Lawyer.** Agar family fees nahi de sakti, to Legal Services Authorities free legal aid deti hain [[nalsa]].

**Doctors ki opinion.** Court doctors se poochega ki pregnancy end karna safe hai ya nahi. 2022 ke ek case mein, jo 24 hafte ki limit ke andar ka tha, Delhi High Court ne qareeb 22 hafte pregnant ek unmarried aurat ko interim relief dene se mana kar diya tha; 21 July 2022 ko Supreme Court ne woh order modify kiya aur kaha ki agar AIIMS Delhi ka Medical Board ise safe paaye, to woh pregnancy end kar sakti hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

**Naam chhupana.** Pehli filing se hi iski maang kijiye. Us case ki aurat law reports mein sirf "X" ke naam se jaani jaati hai.

**Time lagega, aur koi guarantee nahi.** Drafting, listing aur hearing ka har din pregnancy ka bhi ek aur din hai, aur court phir bhi mana kar sakta hai.

## Families is point tak pahunchne se kaise bachein?

Der se pata chalne ki wajahein bilkul aam bhi ho sakti hain: ladki darr ke maare pregnancy chhupa leti hai, ya kisi ka dhyaan hi nahi jaata, ya family darti hai ki hospital gaye to na jaane kya-kya shuru ho jaayega.

Minors ke case mein yeh aakhri darr sach hai. 18 se kam umar ki ladki ki har pregnancy ki khabar POCSO ke tahat police ko deni hoti hai. Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha tha ki isse pregnant minor aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi raaste bachte hain: registered doctor ke paas jaayein aur shayad criminal proceedings mein phansein, ya kisi unqualified provider ke paas jaayein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Usi judgment ne kaha ki agar ladki aur uske guardian kahein, to doctor ko police report mein ladki ki identity ya personal details dene ki zaroorat nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Do aur facts der karne ki wajah khatam karte hain. Rape ground use karne ke liye aurat ko na FIR chahiye, na court mein kuch prove karna hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Aur agar doctor uska naam ya details kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne authorise nahi kiya, to doctor ko ek saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Baaki kaam ghar par hota hai. Jis ladki ko daant ka darr hai, uske missed period ki baat chhupane ke chances zyada hain; jise madad ki ummeed hai, uske bata dene ke chances zyada hain. Kuch hone se pehle hi usse keh dijiye: "Agar kabhi tumhari body ke saath kuch bhi ho, to hamare paas aana. Hum tumhe blame nahi karenge." Phir dinon mein kadam uthaiye, hafton mein nahi.

Woh jo bhi decide kare, madad maujood hai. November 2023 se Nirbhaya Fund ki ek scheme rape se pregnant hui minor ladkiyon ko ek hi chhat ke neeche shelter, medical aur maternity care, legal aid, counselling aur education support deti hai [[mwcd-pocso-victim-support-scheme-2023]]. NALSA ki 2018 ki scheme mein rape se hui pregnancy ke liye Rs 3 lakh se Rs 4 lakh tak ka compensation hai, aur minor ke liye limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

after-abortion-care-warning-signs-guide.en:
Imagine a 24-year-old in Pune. A gynaecologist prescribed abortion pills at six weeks; she took them on Saturday, and by Monday she is back at her desk, still bleeding, unsure whether this is normal and too embarrassed to ask. This guide is what someone should have told her.

In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 15.6% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion reported complications; 89.7% of them sought treatment, 70.6% of it in the private sector [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Abortion itself is rarely the danger: deaths from safe abortion are negligible, under 1 per 100,000 abortions, but exceed 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common, the WHO says [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. The difference lies in who provides the abortion and how fast problems are treated. Your own doctor's instructions come first.

## What is normal in the days after

Bleeding and cramps mean the abortion is working, not that something is damaged. With pills, bleeding is usually heavier than a period while the pregnancy passes, sometimes with clots, then settles into lighter bleeding or spotting that can come and go for a few weeks. After a procedure, it is usually lighter [[who-abortion]].

On the day you take them, the tablets can cause short-lived fever, chills, nausea or diarrhoea [[nhm-cac]]; tiredness and tender breasts are common too. Use pads rather than tampons or a cup, so you can see how much you are bleeding, and ask the doctor, not the chemist, which painkiller to take.

A home pregnancy test can stay positive for some weeks after a complete abortion, because the hormone takes time to clear. A positive test alone does not prove the abortion failed; the follow-up visit settles that. Your period should return within weeks. If it does not, or you still feel pregnant, go back.

## Danger signs that cannot wait

Go to the nearest government hospital, or call 112, if you notice any of these [[who-abortion]]:

- bleeding that soaks through pads very quickly, or gets heavier instead of lighter;
- large clots, dizziness, fainting or a racing heart;
- fever or chills that begin after the day of the tablets, or carry on beyond it;
- severe pain in the abdomen that painkillers do not touch, especially on one side;
- foul-smelling discharge from the vagina;
- no bleeding at all after the pills, or pregnancy symptoms that do not fade.

These can mean an incomplete abortion, an infection, or an ectopic pregnancy (one growing outside the womb) that nobody detected. Each can become life-threatening. In a 2015 survey of six states, 4-16% of patients receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications such as infection of the uterus, perforation, sepsis and shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Tell the doctor exactly what you took, how much and when, including tablets bought without a prescription: doctors cannot treat what they do not know. Do not take more tablets, and do not wait it out for fear of being judged. UNFPA India estimates that close to 8 women die every day from causes related to unsafe abortion [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## The follow-up visit: what it should check

The mifepristone-misoprostol combination, approved in India for pregnancies of up to nine weeks, succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. So a few do not complete, and the follow-up visit exists to catch them. Keep it even if you feel fine. A good one should:

- confirm the abortion is complete, from your symptoms and an examination, with an ultrasound or blood test if there is doubt;
- check for infection and ask how much you are still bleeding;
- start the contraception you choose, if you want it [[nhm-cac]];
- ask how you are feeling, and answer your questions about sex, work and exercise.

In NFHS-5, 26.9% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion said they had ended it themselves [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. If you took pills without seeing a doctor, you need this check more, not less: nobody may have confirmed how far along you were or ruled out an ectopic pregnancy. A government hospital can still do that now.

## Contraception after an abortion

Fertility comes back fast: you can ovulate, and get pregnant, before your next period arrives [[nhm-cac]]. In NFHS-5, an unplanned pregnancy was the main reason for 47.6% of abortions [[nfhs5-india-2021]], and one abortion does nothing to prevent the next. Most methods, including the pill, the injectable and the Copper-T, can start at the abortion or at the follow-up visit; ask which timing suits yours [[nhm-cac]].

In typical use, WHO counts fewer than 1 pregnancy per 100 women in the first year with an IUD such as the Copper-T, about 4 with the injectable, about 7 with the pill and about 13 with male condoms [[who-fp]]. Only condoms also cut the risk of sexually transmitted infections. If one breaks meanwhile, emergency contraception works up to 5 days after sex, sooner is better [[who-ec]].

## Feelings, privacy and where to talk

There is no correct way to feel. Many women feel relief; some feel sad, guilty or numb; many feel several of these in the same week. Low mood that does not lift, or any thought of harming yourself, needs help now: call Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]], the Health Ministry's free counselling line, open round the clock [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

You do not owe anyone an explanation. If you are 18 or older, your own consent is the only one the MTP Act requires, so you can go to the follow-up alone [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Since 2021, Section 5A of the Act bars a registered doctor from revealing your name or other particulars to anyone not authorised by law, on pain of up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. A husband, parent or mother-in-law is not such a person.

If you are under 18, doctors must report the pregnancy to the police under POCSO, so they cannot promise complete secrecy; since 2022, though, you and your guardian can ask for your name to be kept out of that report [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. And if anyone at a clinic lectures you instead of treating you, ask for another doctor or go elsewhere. A lecture is not part of the treatment.
after-abortion-care-warning-signs-guide.hg:
Socho, Pune ki ek 24 saal ki ladki. Gynaecologist ne chhe hafte ki pregnancy par use abortion pills di. Usne Saturday ko goliyan li, aur Monday ko woh office mein apni desk par wapas hai: bleeding abhi bhi ho rahi hai, samajh nahi aa raha ki yeh normal hai ya nahi, aur kisi se poochne mein sharam aa rahi hai. Yeh guide woh sab hai jo kisi ko use pehle hi bata dena chahiye tha.

NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein, jin auraton ki pichhli pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications bataye; inmein se 89.7% ilaaj ke liye gayin, aur us ilaaj ka 70.6% private sector mein hua [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Khatra aksar abortion khud nahi hota. WHO ke mutabik safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hai, har 100,000 abortions par 1 se bhi kam, lekin jahan unsafe abortion aam hai wahan yeh 200 per 100,000 se zyada ho jaati hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Farak is baat ka hai ki abortion kaun karta hai, aur problem hone par ilaaj kitni jaldi milta hai. Tumhare apne doctor ki salah sabse pehle aati hai.

## Pehle kuch dinon mein kya normal hai

Bleeding aur cramps ka matlab hai ki abortion kaam kar raha hai, yeh nahi ki andar kuch kharab ho gaya. Goliyon se, jab pregnancy bahar nikalti hai, bleeding aam taur par period se zyada hoti hai, kabhi-kabhi clots ke saath. Phir yeh halki bleeding ya spotting mein badal jaati hai, jo kuch hafton tak aati-jaati reh sakti hai. Procedure ke baad bleeding aam taur par kam hoti hai [[who-abortion]].

Jis din tum goliyan leti ho, us din thodi der ke liye bukhaar, kapkapi, ulti jaisa mann ya dast ho sakte hain [[nhm-cac]]; thakaan aur breasts mein dard bhi aam baat hai. Tampon ya cup ki jagah pads use karo, taaki dikhe ki bleeding kitni ho rahi hai. Aur kaun sa painkiller lena hai, yeh chemist se nahi, doctor se poocho.

Complete abortion ke baad bhi ghar wala pregnancy test kuch hafton tak positive aa sakta hai, kyunki hormone ko body se nikalne mein waqt lagta hai. Sirf positive test se yeh saabit nahi hota ki abortion fail ho gaya; yeh follow-up visit mein pata chalta hai. Tumhara period kuch hafton mein laut aana chahiye. Agar na aaye, ya ab bhi pregnant jaisa lage, toh doctor ke paas wapas jao.

## Danger signs jinke liye ruk nahi sakte

Inmein se kuch bhi ho toh sabse nazdeek sarkari hospital jao, ya 112 par call karo [[who-abortion]]:

- aisi bleeding jo pads ko bahut jaldi-jaldi bhigo de, ya kam hone ki jagah badhti jaaye;
- bade clots, chakkar, behoshi ya dil ka tezi se dhadakna;
- bukhaar ya kapkapi jo goliyon wale din ke baad shuru ho, ya us din ke baad bhi chalti rahe;
- pet mein itna tez dard ki painkiller se bhi na jaaye, khaaskar ek taraf;
- vagina se badbudaar discharge;
- goliyon ke baad bilkul bleeding na hona, ya pregnancy ke lakshan khatam na hona.

In signs ka matlab incomplete abortion, infection, ya aisi ectopic pregnancy (jo womb ke bahar badh rahi ho) ho sakta hai jise kisi ne pakda hi nahi. Inmein se har ek jaanleva ban sakti hai. 2015 mein chhe states ke ek survey mein, post-abortion care le rahe patients mein se 4-16% ka ilaaj serious complications ke liye ho raha tha, jaise uterus ka infection, perforation, sepsis aur shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Doctor ko saaf-saaf batao ki tumne kya liya, kitna aur kab, bina prescription khareedi goliyan bhi. Jo baat doctor ko pata hi nahi, uska ilaaj woh nahi kar sakte. Aur goliyan mat lo, aur judge hone ke darr se ghar baith kar intezaar mat karo: UNFPA India ka andaaza hai ki unsafe abortion se judi wajahon se roz kareeb 8 auratein marti hain [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Follow-up visit: ismein kya check hona chahiye

Mifepristone-misoprostol combination, jo India mein nau hafte tak ki pregnancy ke liye approved hai, early abortions mein 95-99% baar kaamyaab hota hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Yaani kuch abortions poore nahi hote, aur follow-up visit unhi ko pakadne ke liye hai. Theek mehsoos karo tab bhi jao. Ek achhi follow-up visit mein:

- tumhare symptoms aur examination se confirm ho ki abortion poora hua, aur shak ho toh ultrasound ya blood test ho;
- infection ka check ho, aur poocha jaaye ki bleeding ab kitni hai;
- tum jo contraception chuno, agar chaho toh, woh shuru ho [[nhm-cac]];
- poocha jaaye ki tum kaisa mehsoos kar rahi ho, aur sex, kaam aur exercise ke baare mein tumhare sawaalon ke jawaab milein.

NFHS-5 mein, jin auraton ki pichhli pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone pregnancy khud khatam ki [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Agar tumne bina doctor ko dikhaye goliyan li, toh yeh check tumhare liye aur bhi zaroori hai: ho sakta hai kisi ne confirm hi nahi kiya ki pregnancy kitne hafte ki thi, ya woh ectopic toh nahi thi. Sarkari hospital mein yeh ab bhi ho sakta hai.

## Abortion ke baad contraception

Fertility jaldi laut aati hai: agle period se pehle hi ovulation ho sakta hai, aur tum pregnant ho sakti ho [[nhm-cac]]. NFHS-5 mein 47.6% abortions ki main wajah unplanned pregnancy thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]], aur ek abortion agli unplanned pregnancy ko nahi rokta. Pill, injectable aur Copper-T samet zyada tar methods abortion ke time ya follow-up visit par shuru ho sakte hain; poocho ki tumhare method ke liye sahi time kya hai [[nhm-cac]].

Aam istemaal mein, WHO ke hisaab se har 100 auraton mein pehle saal mein IUD jaise Copper-T se 1 se bhi kam pregnancy hoti hai, injectable se kareeb 4, pill se kareeb 7 aur male condom se kareeb 13 [[who-fp]]. Sirf condom hi sexually transmitted infections ka risk bhi kam karta hai. Agar is beech condom phat jaaye, toh emergency contraception sex ke 5 din baad tak kaam karti hai, jitni jaldi utna behtar [[who-ec]].

## Feelings, privacy aur kisse baat karein

Mehsoos karne ka koi ek sahi tareeka nahi hai. Kai auraton ko rahat milti hai; kuch ko dukh, guilt ya khaalipan lagta hai; aur kai ko ek hi hafte mein yeh sab. Agar mood utha hi nahi, ya khud ko nuksaan pahunchane ka koi bhi khayal aaye, toh abhi madad lo: Tele-MANAS ko 14416 par call karo [[tele-manas]], yeh Health Ministry ki free counselling line hai jo din-raat khuli rehti hai [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

Tum kisi ko safai dene ke liye majboor nahi ho. Agar tum 18 ya usse badi ho, toh MTP Act mein sirf tumhari apni consent chahiye, isliye follow-up par tum akeli ja sakti ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 2021 se, Act ka Section 5A registered doctor ko tumhara naam ya koi aur detail kisi aise insaan ko batane se rokta hai jise kanoon ne ijaazat nahi di; rule todne par ek saal tak ki jail, fine ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Husband, parent ya saas aise insaan nahi hain.

Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh POCSO ke tahat doctor ko pregnancy police ko report karni hoti hai, isliye woh poori secrecy ka vaada nahi kar sakte. Lekin 2022 se tum aur tumhare guardian maang sakte ho ki us report mein tumhara naam na likha jaaye [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Aur agar clinic mein koi ilaaj ki jagah lecture dene lage, toh doosre doctor ke liye kaho ya kahin aur jao. Lecture ilaaj ka hissa nahi hai.

blamed-for-daughters-sex-selection-myth.en:
Consider a scene many Indian families will recognise. A woman gives birth to her second daughter. Within days the sympathy turns into advice: eat this, fast on that day, try the powder a relative swears by, and next time "get it checked". Nobody asks what her husband ate. Every remark rests on one assumption: her body decided, and decided wrongly.

The assumption is false, and it is not harmless. It turns a preference for sons into a project with a woman at the centre of it. In a 2014 ICRW-UNFPA survey in seven states, 81% of women and 76% of men said it was very important to have at least one son [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. When a family wants a son that much and believes the mother decides, she becomes the problem to be fixed.

## Myth: the mother decides whether it's a boy or a girl

The myth comes in many forms. She "only gives girls". Her diet was wrong, her prayers weak, her timing off. Some families buy powders or follow rituals that promise a son. Others decide she must simply keep trying until one arrives.

More women than men in that survey called a son very important. So the pressure on a mother can come from other women in the family as much as from men. That does not make the myth truer; it shows how long it has gone unchallenged.

## Truth: what actually sets a baby's sex

Every egg carries an X chromosome. Every sperm carries either an X or a Y. If an X-carrying sperm fertilises the egg, the baby typically develops as a girl (XX); if a Y-carrying sperm does, typically as a boy (XY). The sex is settled at that moment, by whichever sperm gets there first. It is chance.

So if any cell "decides", it is the father's sperm, and he does not choose either. Nothing a woman eats, prays for or does can change which sperm reaches the egg. Each pregnancy is a fresh draw: two daughters do not make a son "due". (Some people are born with intersex variations. That is biology too, and nobody's fault.)

Left alone, nature produces slightly more boys than girls, about 105 for every 100 girls. India's ratio at birth was about 108 in NFHS-5 (2019-21) [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. The gap between those two numbers is not biology.

## Where the myth leads: pressure, scans, abortions

If the mother is "responsible" for daughters, the family believes she can be made to correct it: another pregnancy, then an illegal test, then an abortion she may not want.

NFHS-5 caught a sliver of this. Of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion, 2.1% openly named a female foetus as the main reason; among the larger states, the share was highest in Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) and Punjab (4.2%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sex selection is a crime, so women have every reason not to tell a surveyor. The real share is almost certainly far higher.

About 460,000 girls in India went "missing" at birth every year between 2013 and 2017, UNFPA reported in 2020. Sex selection accounts for about two thirds of India's missing girls, and excess deaths of girls after birth for about one third [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. The myth does not stop at the scan. It follows the daughters who are born.

## What the law says about a woman forced into it

The Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act bans sex selection, before or after conception, and the misuse of prenatal tests to find a foetus's sex [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. No one, including the person doing a scan, may tell a pregnant woman, her relatives or anyone else the sex of the foetus "by words, signs or in any other manner" [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Anyone who seeks sex selection faces up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 50,000, and up to five years and Rs 1 lakh for a repeat offence. But the Act presumes that a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives, does not punish a woman who was forced, and makes the husband or relative liable for abetment [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

In other words, the law has already rejected the myth. It assumes the pressure comes from the family, not from her.

Two more protections matter. An adult woman's own consent is the only consent an abortion needs [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. And causing a woman to miscarry without her consent is punishable with up to ten years, or life, in prison under Section 89 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [[gazette-bns-2023]].

To report a clinic offering sex determination, go to the district Appropriate Authority, the health officials who enforce the Act. A person can also take a complaint to court after giving that authority at least 15 days' notice [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

## Words to use when the blame starts

Some lines that help, said plainly and early:

- "The baby's sex comes from the sperm, by chance. Nobody's body chooses it, not mine and not his."
- "Two daughters don't mean a son is due. Every pregnancy is a new chance either way."
- "Asking for a test to find out the baby's sex is a crime for whoever asks. I won't do it."

If you are watching this happen to a sister-in-law, a sister or a friend, speak to her alone first, then stand beside her when the family raises it. If she is being pushed towards a test or an abortion she does not want, the Women Helpline and the One Stop Centres run under the government's Mission Shakti scheme can help [[wcd-mission-shakti]]; in danger, call 112.

A family that believes the mother decides will always have someone to blame. The truth leaves them only their own preference to answer for.
blamed-for-daughters-sex-selection-myth.hg:
Ek scene sochiye jo kai Indian families pehchaanengi. Ek aurat apni doosri beti ko janam deti hai. Kuch hi dinon mein hamdardi salah mein badal jaati hai: yeh khao, us din vrat rakho, woh powder try karo jiski ek rishtedaar kasam khaati hai, aur agli baar "check karwa lena". Koi nahi poochta ki uske pati ne kya khaya tha. Har baat ke neeche ek hi soch hai: faisla uski body ne kiya, aur galat kiya.

Yeh soch galat hai, aur harmless bhi nahi. Yeh bete ki chahat ko ek project bana deti hai, jiske beech mein ek aurat khadi hai. 2014 mein saat states mein hue ICRW-UNFPA survey mein 81% aurton aur 76% mardon ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]]. Jab family ko beta itna chahiye ho aur use lagta ho ki faisla maa karti hai, toh wahi aurat woh "problem" ban jaati hai jise theek karna hai.

## Myth: ladka hoga ya ladki, maa decide karti hai

Yeh myth kai roop mein aata hai. Woh "sirf ladkiyan deti hai". Uska khana galat tha, uski prarthana kamzor thi, uski timing gadbad thi. Kuch families aise powders khareedti hain ya aisi rasmein karti hain jo bete ka vaada karti hain. Kuch tay kar leti hain ki use bas tab tak koshish karte rehna hai jab tak beta na aa jaaye.

Us survey mein mardon se zyada aurton ne beta hona bahut zaroori bataya. Isliye maa par pressure family ki doosri aurton se bhi utna hi aa sakta hai jitna mardon se. Isse myth sach nahi ho jaata; isse bas yeh dikhta hai ki ise kitne lambe samay se kisi ne challenge nahi kiya.

## Sach: bachche ka sex asal mein kya tay karta hai

Har egg mein X chromosome hota hai. Har sperm mein ya toh X hota hai ya Y. Agar X wala sperm egg ko fertilise karta hai, toh baby typically ladki (XX) ke roop mein develop hota hai; agar Y wala karta hai, toh typically ladke (XY) ke roop mein. Sex usi pal tay ho jaata hai, us sperm se jo pehle pahunchta hai. Yeh chance hai.

Toh agar koi cell "decide" karta bhi hai, toh woh pita ka sperm hai, aur pita bhi ise choose nahi karta. Aurat kya khaati hai, kya dua maangti hai ya kya karti hai, isse yeh nahi badalta ki kaun sa sperm egg tak pahunchega. Har pregnancy ek nayi baazi hai: do betiyon ke baad beta "due" nahi ho jaata. (Kuch log intersex variations ke saath paida hote hain. Woh bhi biology hai, aur usmein bhi kisi ki galti nahi.)

Agar kuch na chheda jaaye, toh nature ladkiyon se thode zyada ladke paida karti hai, har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 105 ladke. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India ka ratio at birth lagbhag 108 tha [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. In do numbers ke beech ka fark biology nahi hai.

## Myth kahan le jaata hai: pressure, scan, abortion

Agar betiyon ke liye maa "zimmedaar" hai, toh family maanti hai ki use yeh "sudharne" par majboor kiya ja sakta hai: ek aur pregnancy, phir ek illegal test, phir ek abortion jo shayad woh chahti hi nahi.

NFHS-5 ne iska ek chhota sa hissa pakda. Jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 2.1% ne khul kar kaha ki main wajah pet mein ladki thi; bade states mein yeh share sabse zyada Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) aur Punjab (4.2%) mein tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sex selection crime hai, isliye aurton ke paas surveyor ko yeh na batane ki poori wajah hai. Asli share almost pakka isse kahin zyada hai.

UNFPA ne 2020 mein bataya ki 2013 se 2017 ke beech India mein har saal lagbhag 460,000 ladkiyan janam ke waqt "missing" hui. India ki missing ladkiyon mein se lagbhag do-tihaai ke peeche sex selection hai, aur lagbhag ek-tihaai ke peeche janam ke baad ladkiyon ki zyada maut [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Myth scan par khatam nahi hota. Woh un betiyon ka bhi peecha karta hai jo paida ho jaati hain.

## Majboor ki gayi aurat ke baare mein law kya kehta hai

Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act sex selection par ban lagata hai, conception se pehle bhi aur baad bhi, aur foetus ka sex jaanne ke liye prenatal tests ke galat istemaal par bhi [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Koi bhi, scan karne wala bhi, pregnant aurat, uske rishtedaaron ya kisi aur ko foetus ka sex "by words, signs or in any other manner", yaani bol kar, ishaare se ya kisi bhi tarah, nahi bata sakta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Jo bhi sex selection karwana chahe, use teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 50,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai, aur dobara karne par paanch saal tak ki jail aur Rs 1 lakh tak ka fine. Lekin Act yeh maan kar chalta hai ki pregnant aurat ko uske pati ya rishtedaaron ne majboor kiya tha. Jis aurat ko majboor kiya gaya, use woh saza nahi deta, aur pati ya rishtedaar ko abetment ka zimmedaar maanta hai [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Matlab, law is myth ko pehle hi reject kar chuka hai. Woh maanta hai ki pressure family se aata hai, aurat se nahi.

Do aur protections kaam ki hain. Adult aurat ki apni consent hi woh akeli consent hai jo abortion ke liye chahiye [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Aur kisi aurat ka uski consent ke bina miscarriage karwana Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 89 ke under crime hai, jiski saza das saal tak ki jail ya umrakaid tak ho sakti hai [[gazette-bns-2023]].

Sex determination offer karne wale clinic ki report karni ho, toh district Appropriate Authority ke paas jaaiye, yaani un health officials ke paas jo yeh Act lagu karte hain. Koi bhi insaan us authority ko kam se kam 15 din ka notice dene ke baad court mein complaint bhi kar sakta hai [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

## Jab blame shuru ho, toh kya kahein

Kuch lines jo kaam aati hain, saaf-saaf aur jaldi boli jaayein:

- "Bachche ka sex sperm se aata hai, chance se. Kisi ki body ise choose nahi karti, na meri, na unki."
- "Do betiyon ka matlab yeh nahi ki ab beta due hai. Har pregnancy mein dono ka chance naye sire se hota hai."
- "Bachche ka sex pata karne ke liye test maangna, maangne wale ke liye crime hai. Main yeh nahi karungi."

Agar yeh aapki bhabhi, behen ya kisi dost ke saath hota dikh raha hai, toh pehle usse akele mein baat kijiye, phir jab family yeh baat uthaye toh uske saath khade rahiye. Agar us par test ya aise abortion ka pressure hai jo woh nahi chahti, toh Women Helpline aur sarkar ki Mission Shakti scheme ke under chalne wale One Stop Centres madad kar sakte hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]]; khatre mein ho toh 112 par call kijiye.

Jo family maanti hai ki faisla maa karti hai, uske paas blame karne ke liye hamesha koi na koi hoga. Sach unke paas sirf unki apni chahat chhodta hai, jiska jawab unhe khud dena hoga.

contraceptive-failure-abortion-ground-in.en:
Imagine a 22-year-old in Pune, unmarried, whose condom broke. Six weeks later the test is positive. She has two fears: that abortion is only for married women, and that a doctor will make her prove how distressed she is. The first fear was never fully true, but for 50 years the law gave it a foothold; since 2021 it has none. The second is answered by one sentence in the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, about exactly her situation: a contraceptive that failed.

## The clause written in 1971

Abortion in India is not available on request. Today, up to 20 weeks, one registered doctor must form an opinion, in good faith, that continuing the pregnancy would risk the woman's life or gravely injure her physical or mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. So what counts as grave injury to mental health?

For one situation, the 1971 Act answered in advance:

> "Where any pregnancy occurs as a result of failure of any device or method used by any married woman or her husband for the purpose of limiting the number of children, the anguish caused by such unwanted pregnancy may be presumed to constitute a grave injury to the mental health of the pregnant woman." [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]

"May be presumed" is the phrase that matters. The doctor needs no psychiatric diagnosis or proof of distress; the law lets the doctor assume the harm. In a law that refuses abortion on request, that turns "my method failed and I do not want this pregnancy" into a recognised legal ground.

## Fifty years of 'married woman or her husband'

The 1971 clause pictured a family-planning programme, not a person: a wife and husband limiting the size of their family. An unmarried woman whose condom broke was outside it [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

She could still get an abortion on the general health ground, which applied to every pregnant woman. What she lacked was the presumption, so she depended more on how an individual doctor judged her. For half a century, the shortcut was reserved for wives.

## 2021: any woman, any partner

The 2021 amendment rewrote it to cover a method "used by any woman or her partner for the purpose of limiting the number of children or preventing pregnancy" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Three changes in one line: woman, not wife; partner, not husband; and "preventing pregnancy", which covers someone who has no children and wanted none yet.

What this means at a clinic:

- Up to 20 weeks, one registered doctor's opinion is enough, whatever her marital status [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].
- "Her partner" gives him no veto: an adult woman's own consent is the only consent the law asks for [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. His signature is not needed.
- A doctor who reveals her name or details to anyone not authorised by law faces up to a year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].
- Past 20 weeks, failure alone is not enough. Up to 24 weeks, the 2021 rules list seven eligible categories, such as survivors of rape, minors and women whose marital status changes; contraceptive failure is not among them [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Since 2022, unmarried women have the same access to that window as married women [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

If she is under 18, a guardian must consent in writing [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Because any sexual activity with a minor is an offence under POCSO, the doctor must also report the pregnancy to the police [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]], though the Supreme Court has said the report need not reveal her identity if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

## Failure is ordinary, so why do so few name it?

Contraceptive failure is not a moral failing. It is arithmetic. In typical use, about 13 in 100 women relying on the external condom get pregnant within a year, about 7 on the pill and about 20 using withdrawal; with no method, about 85. Implants and IUDs bring it below 1 in 100 [[who-fp]]. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 9.5% of married women relied on condoms, 5.1% on the pill and 10.3% on traditional methods such as withdrawal [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yet when NFHS-5 asked women for the main reason for their abortion, only 3.6% named contraceptive failure, against 47.6% who named an unplanned pregnancy [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Three things help explain the gap. The survey asks for one main reason, and a pregnancy after a failed method is also unplanned, so many women may give the broader answer. Many unplanned pregnancies involve no method at all: 66.7% of married women used one, which leaves about a third using none [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. And naming a failure means admitting to using contraception, in a country where 19.6% of men agreed that women who use it may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The law takes the opposite view: a failed method is a reason, not a confession.

## Before it comes to abortion: the 120-hour window

Deal with a broken condom the same day if you can. Emergency contraception works by delaying ovulation and can be used up to five days (120 hours) after unprotected sex; sooner is better. A copper IUD fitted by a trained provider is the most effective option. Emergency contraception is not abortion, will not end an established pregnancy and does not protect against infections [[who-ec]].

If there is any chance of HIV exposure, see a doctor urgently: PEP must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]].

If the period is late, test and see a registered doctor early. Under Health Ministry guidelines, abortion pills can be used up to nine weeks, with 95-99% success in early abortions, on a qualified doctor's prescription [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Do not take them on a chemist's say-so.

It took Indian law 50 years to admit that unmarried women use contraception too, and that it fails for them as well. A reader needs only two numbers: five days for emergency contraception, and 20 weeks for the law's presumption.
contraceptive-failure-abortion-ground-in.hg:
Imagine kijiye, Pune ki ek 22 saal ki unmarried ladki hai, jiska condom phat gaya. Chhe hafte baad test positive aata hai. Use do darr hain: ki abortion sirf shaadishuda aurton ke liye hai, aur ki doctor use saabit karne ko kahega ki woh kitni pareshaan hai. Pehla darr kabhi poori tarah sach nahi tha, lekin 50 saal tak law ne use ek zameen di; 2021 se woh zameen bhi nahi bachi. Doosre darr ka jawab Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act ki ek line mein hai, jo theek uski situation ke baare mein hai: ek contraceptive jo fail ho gaya.

## 1971 mein likhi gayi line

India mein abortion on request nahi milta. Aaj 20 hafte tak, ek registered doctor ko good faith mein yeh opinion banani hoti hai ki pregnancy jaari rakhne se aurat ki jaan ko risk hai, ya uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan hoga [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Toh mental health ko gambhir nuksaan kise maana jaaye?

Ek situation ke liye 1971 ke Act ne jawab pehle hi de diya tha:

> "Where any pregnancy occurs as a result of failure of any device or method used by any married woman or her husband for the purpose of limiting the number of children, the anguish caused by such unwanted pregnancy may be presumed to constitute a grave injury to the mental health of the pregnant woman." [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]

Seedhe shabdon mein: agar kisi shaadishuda aurat ya uske pati ka device ya method, jo bachchon ki ginti seemit rakhne ke liye use kiya gaya tha, fail ho jaaye, toh us unwanted pregnancy ki takleef ko aurat ki mental health ke liye gambhir nuksaan maana ja sakta hai.

"May be presumed", yaani "maana ja sakta hai", yahi asli baat hai. Doctor ko na kisi psychiatric diagnosis ki zaroorat hai, na distress ke saboot ki; law doctor ko nuksaan maan lene deta hai. Jo law abortion on request nahi deta, usmein yeh line "mera method fail hua aur mujhe yeh pregnancy nahi chahiye" ko ek maana hua legal ground bana deti hai.

## 50 saal tak 'married woman or her husband'

1971 ki line kisi insaan ki nahi, ek family-planning programme ki tasveer thi: pati-patni jo apne parivaar ka size seemit kar rahe hain. Jis unmarried aurat ka condom phata, woh isse bahar thi [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Woh phir bhi general health ground par abortion karwa sakti thi, jo har pregnant aurat par lagu tha. Uske paas bas yeh presumption nahi tha, isliye woh is par zyada nirbhar thi ki koi ek doctor use kaise judge karta hai. Aadhi sadi tak yeh shortcut sirf biwiyon ke liye reserved raha.

## 2021: koi bhi aurat, koi bhi partner

2021 ke amendment ne ise badal kar aise method ko cover kiya jo "used by any woman or her partner for the purpose of limiting the number of children or preventing pregnancy" ho, yaani koi bhi aurat ya uska partner, bachche seemit karne ya pregnancy rokne ke liye use kare [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Ek line mein teen badlaav: biwi nahi, aurat; pati nahi, partner; aur "preventing pregnancy", jo us ladki ko bhi cover karta hai jiske koi bachche nahi aur jo abhi koi bachcha chahti bhi nahi thi.

Clinic mein iska matlab:

- 20 hafte tak ek registered doctor ki opinion kaafi hai, chahe aurat shaadishuda ho ya nahi [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].
- "Her partner" likhne se partner ko veto nahi milta: adult aurat ki apni consent hi woh akeli consent hai jo law maangta hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Partner ka signature nahi chahiye.
- Jo doctor aurat ka naam ya details kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne permission nahi di, use ek saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].
- 20 hafte ke baad sirf failure kaafi nahi. 24 hafte tak ke liye 2021 ke rules saat categories list karte hain, jaise rape survivors, minors aur woh aurtein jinka marital status badal jaaye; contraceptive failure inmein nahi hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. 2022 se unmarried aurton ko is window tak wahi access hai jo shaadishuda aurton ko hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Agar ladki 18 se kam hai, toh guardian ki written consent chahiye [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Kyunki POCSO ke under minor ke saath koi bhi sexual activity offence hai, isliye doctor ko pregnancy ki report police ko bhi karni hoti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Haalanki Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki agar ladki aur uska guardian kahein, toh us report mein uski pehchaan batana zaroori nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

## Failure aam baat hai, toh itne kam log iska naam kyun lete hain?

Contraceptive failure koi naitik galti nahi. Yeh seedha hisaab hai. Typical use mein external condom par nirbhar 100 mein se lagbhag 13 aurtein ek saal ke andar pregnant ho jaati hain, pill par lagbhag 7 aur withdrawal par lagbhag 20; bina kisi method ke lagbhag 85. Implants aur IUDs ise 100 mein 1 se neeche le aate hain [[who-fp]]. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 9.5% shaadishuda aurtein condom par, 5.1% pill par aur 10.3% withdrawal jaise traditional methods par nirbhar thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Phir bhi jab NFHS-5 ne aurton se unke abortion ki main wajah poochi, toh sirf 3.6% ne contraceptive failure ka naam liya, jabki 47.6% ne unplanned pregnancy batayi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Is fark ko teen baatein samjhati hain. Survey sirf ek main wajah poochta hai, aur fail hue method ke baad hui pregnancy bhi unplanned hi hoti hai, isliye kai aurtein shayad bada jawab chun leti hain. Kai unplanned pregnancies mein koi method tha hi nahi: 66.7% shaadishuda aurtein koi method use kar rahi thi, yaani lagbhag ek-tihaai kuch bhi use nahi kar rahi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Aur failure ka naam lene ka matlab hai yeh maanna ki aap contraception use kar rahi thi, us desh mein jahan 19.6% mardon ne maana ki contraception use karne wali aurtein "badchalan" ho sakti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Law ulta sochta hai: fail hua method ek wajah hai, koi confession nahi.

## Abortion tak pahunchne se pehle: 120 ghante ki window

Condom phate toh ho sake toh usi din kuch kijiye. Emergency contraception ovulation ko delay karke kaam karta hai, aur unprotected sex ke paanch din (120 ghante) baad tak liya ja sakta hai; jitni jaldi, utna behtar. Kisi trained provider ka lagaya copper IUD sabse effective option hai. Emergency contraception abortion nahi hai, pehle se ho chuki pregnancy ko khatam nahi karta, aur infections se nahi bachata [[who-ec]].

Agar HIV exposure ka zara bhi chance ho, toh turant doctor se miliye: PEP jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye, aur exposure ke 72 ghante ke andar hi [[who-pep]].

Period late ho, toh test kijiye aur jaldi kisi registered doctor se miliye. Health Ministry ki guidelines ke hisaab se abortion pills nau hafte tak use ho sakti hain, aur early abortions mein 95-99% kaamyaab rehti hain, lekin qualified doctor ke prescription par [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Chemist ke kehne bhar se inhe mat lijiye.

Indian law ko yeh maanne mein 50 saal lag gaye ki unmarried aurtein bhi contraception use karti hain, aur unke liye bhi woh fail hota hai. Aapko sirf do numbers yaad rakhne hain: emergency contraception ke liye paanch din, aur law ke presumption ke liye 20 hafte.

disability-abortion-law-consent-autonomy.en:
When Parliament passed India's abortion law in 1971, it had a word for some adult women: "lunatic". For them, the decision about their own pregnancy went to a guardian [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Today the abortion rules give some disabled women more time, and another law makes it a crime to end a disabled woman's pregnancy without her express consent. Between the two sits a question many families never say aloud: when does protecting a disabled woman turn into deciding for her?

## The words the law used, and still uses

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971 said that the pregnancy of a woman under 18, or of an adult woman who "is a lunatic", could be ended only with her guardian's written consent [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. A 2002 amendment replaced "lunatic" with "mentally ill person". The guardian's written consent stayed [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

The 2021 abortion rules still use the outdated term "mental retardation" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Such words are not just old-fashioned. In the consent rule, the label "mentally ill person" still decides whose "yes" the system listens for.

## Who consents for whom

If a woman is 18 or older, her own consent is the only one the MTP Act asks for. A guardian steps in only if she is under 18 or a "mentally ill person" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Physical disability is not on that list: a wheelchair user, a blind woman or a Deaf woman consents for herself.

The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 adds a hard line. Under Section 92(f), anyone who carries out or directs a procedure that ends a disabled woman's pregnancy without her express consent faces six months to five years in prison. The only exception: a severe case of disability, with a registered doctor's opinion and the guardian's consent [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]].

Read together, the message is clear: a guardian's signature is a narrow exception, not a shortcut around the woman. (This is general information, not legal advice.)

A protection is only as strong as the complaints that reach it. In 2024, the first year national crime data counted them, police across India registered just 56 cases under the whole RPwD Act, for all offences [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Rule 3B: disability as a 24-week category

Up to 20 weeks, any woman can end a pregnancy on one registered doctor's opinion, if a legal ground applies. Between 20 and 24 weeks, the law allows it only for categories named in the rules, with two doctors agreeing [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. The rules notified on 12 October 2021 name seven such categories, and two concern disability: women with major physical disabilities, and mentally ill women [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Our plain-words MTP Act guide lists all seven.

The extra weeks matter because barriers stack up. Take a hypothetical: a Deaf woman in a small town whose family does the talking at every clinic. Nobody explains her test result in sign language. By the time she understands she is pregnant, and decides, weeks have passed.

When a pregnancy follows rape, the law presumes its anguish gravely injures the woman's mental health, a legal ground for abortion [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. In 2022 the Supreme Court said no FIR or proof in court is needed first [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Raping a woman with a mental or physical disability is aggravated rape under Section 64(2)(k) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS): at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Suchita Srivastava and reproductive autonomy

One foundation of "reproductive autonomy" in Indian law is a case about a disabled woman. Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009) concerned a woman with an intellectual disability who became pregnant after an alleged rape while living in a government-run welfare institution. Thirteen years later, the Supreme Court put it plainly:

> "In Suchita Srivastava (supra) this Court explicitly recognized the concept of reproductive autonomy." (Supreme Court, 2022)

In 2017, the nine-judge privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India built on it, tying the right to an abortion under the MTP Act to the constitutional right to make reproductive choices under Article 21. In September 2022, the Court relied on both judgments to widen abortion access [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

So a principle the Supreme Court now applies to every woman was shaped by a disabled woman's case. It would be a strange law that applied it to everyone except women like her.

## Rights to insist on at a hospital

Start with consent: an adult with a physical disability signs for herself. If she communicates through sign language, writing or an assistant, ask the doctor to speak with her that way.

Next, privacy. Since 2021, a doctor who reveals the name or details of a woman who had an abortion, to anyone not authorised by law, faces up to a year in prison [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

If there was sexual violence, police must record a disabled survivor's complaint at her home or a place she chooses, with an interpreter or special educator, and the recording must be videographed [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

On paper, these are strong rights. In practice, the record is thin. In a 2018 report on 17 cases of sexual violence against disabled women and girls, Human Rights Watch found that police and court officials ignored the accommodations the law required in 15. In 16, the survivors and their families did not know the law's disability-specific protections existed [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].
