The numbers are patchy too. India's 2011 Census counted 26.8 million people with disabilities, 2.21% of the population, against a WHO-World Bank global estimate of 15%. In 2018, Human Rights Watch noted that neither the National Family Health Survey nor national crime data broke figures down by disability [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Police data now show one narrow slice: of 29,536 rape cases registered in 2024, only 144 were recorded under the aggravated charge for raping a disabled woman. Uttar Pradesh recorded 3; Bihar recorded none [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Those figures show how rarely police use the charge, not how often the crime happens. Nobody can say how many disabled women became pregnant after rape, or lost a decision about a pregnancy.

If you are her family, the test is simple: did she say yes, in her own way? If anyone, a hospital included, says otherwise, legal services authorities give free legal aid [[nalsa]].
disability-abortion-law-consent-autonomy.hg:
1971 mein jab Parliament ne India ka abortion law paas kiya, tab us law mein kuch adult aurton ke liye ek shabd tha: "lunatic", yaani "pagal". Aisi aurat ki pregnancy ka faisla uske guardian ke haath mein chala jaata tha [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Aaj abortion ke rules kuch disabled aurton ko zyada time dete hain, aur ek doosra law kehta hai ki disabled aurat ki saaf consent ke bina uska abortion karna crime hai. In dono ke beech ek sawaal hai jo kai families kabhi zor se nahi poochti: disabled aurat ki hifazat kab uske badle faisla lene mein badal jaati hai?

## Law ne kaun se shabd use kiye, aur ab bhi karta hai

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, 1971 kehta tha ki 18 se kam umar ki ladki ka, ya us adult aurat ka jo "lunatic" ho, abortion sirf guardian ki written consent se ho sakta hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 2002 ke amendment ne "lunatic" ki jagah "mentally ill person" likha. Lekin guardian ki written consent wali shart bani rahi [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

2021 ke abortion rules mein aaj bhi "mental retardation" jaisa purana aur insulting term hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Aaj ise intellectual disability kehte hain. Aise shabd sirf purane nahi hain. Consent wale rule mein "mentally ill person" ka label aaj bhi tay karta hai ki system kiski "haan" sunega.

## Kaun kiske liye consent deta hai

Agar aurat 18 ya usse badi hai, toh MTP Act sirf uski apni consent maangta hai. Guardian tabhi aata hai jab woh 18 se kam ki ho ya "mentally ill person" ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Physical disability is list mein hai hi nahi. Jo aurat wheelchair use karti hai, jo dekh nahi sakti, ya jo sun nahi sakti, woh kisi bhi doosri adult aurat ki tarah apni consent khud deti hai.

Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 yahan ek sakht line kheenchta hai. Section 92(f) ke under, jo bhi disabled aurat ki saaf consent ke bina uska abortion kare ya karwaye, use chhe mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai. Chhoot sirf ek hai: severe disability ka case ho, registered doctor ki raay ho, aur guardian ki consent ho [[gazette-rpwd-act-2016]].

Dono laws ko saath padhiye, toh message saaf hai: guardian ka signature ek chhoti si chhoot hai, aurat ko side karke faisla lene ka shortcut nahi. (Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.)

Koi bhi protection utni hi strong hoti hai jitni complaints us tak pahunchti hain. 2024 mein, pehli baar national crime data ne in cases ko gina, aur poore India mein police ne poore RPwD Act ke under, har tarah ke offence mila kar, sirf 56 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Rule 3B: disability, 24 hafte wali category mein

20 hafte tak koi bhi aurat ek registered doctor ki raay par abortion karwa sakti hai, agar law mein di gayi koi wajah lagu hoti ho. 20 se 24 hafte ke beech yeh sirf rules mein likhi categories ki aurton ke liye hai, aur do doctors ka agree karna zaroori hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 12 October 2021 ko notify hue rules mein aisi saat categories hain, aur unmein se do disability se judi hain: serious physical disability wali aurtein, aur mentally ill aurtein [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Saaton categories hamare MTP Act wale plain-words guide mein hain.

Yeh extra hafte isliye matter karte hain kyunki rukawatein ek ke upar ek judti jaati hain. Ek hypothetical lijiye: ek chhote shehar mein ek aurat jo sun nahi sakti, aur har clinic mein uski taraf se family hi baat karti hai. Koi use sign language mein uski test report nahi samjhata. Jab tak woh samajhti hai ki woh pregnant hai, aur faisla karti hai, kai hafte nikal chuke hote hain.

Agar pregnancy rape se hui hai, toh law maan kar chalta hai ki iska dard aurat ki mental health ko gambhir chot pahunchata hai, aur yeh abortion ki ek legal wajah hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki iske liye pehle na FIR chahiye, na court mein saboot [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Aur mental ya physical disability wali aurat ka rape Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64(2)(k) mein aggravated rape hai: kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment, jo baaki poori zindagi ki jail tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Suchita Srivastava case aur reproductive autonomy

Indian law mein "reproductive autonomy", yaani bachcha paida karne ya na karne ka faisla khud lene ka haq, ki ek neev ek disabled aurat ka case hai. Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration (2009) ek aisi aurat se juda tha jinhe intellectual disability thi, aur jo ek sarkari welfare institution mein rehte hue alleged rape ke baad pregnant hui thi. Terah saal baad Supreme Court ne saaf shabdon mein kaha:

> "In Suchita Srivastava (supra) this Court explicitly recognized the concept of reproductive autonomy." (Supreme Court, 2022)

2017 mein nau judges ki bench ne privacy ke bade faisle, K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, mein isi case ko aage badhaya. Court ne abortion ke legal haq ko Article 21 ke under reproductive choices lene ke constitutional haq se joda. September 2022 mein Supreme Court ne in dono faislon ke sahaare abortion ka raasta aur chauda kiya [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Yaani jo principle Supreme Court aaj har aurat par laagu karta hai, woh ek disabled aurat ke case se bana. Ajeeb law hoga jo yeh haq sabko de, sivaay un aurton ke jo uske jaisi hain.

## Hospital mein kin baaton par tike rahein

Pehli baat, consent. Physical disability wali adult aurat apna sign khud karti hai. Agar woh sign language, likh kar, ya kisi assistant ki madad se baat karti hai, toh doctor se kahiye ki usi tareeke se usse baat kare.

Doosri baat, privacy. 2021 se, agar koi doctor abortion karwane wali aurat ka naam ya details kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne permission nahi di, toh use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Agar sexual violence hua hai, toh police ko disabled survivor ki complaint uske ghar par ya uski chuni hui jagah par darj karni hogi, interpreter ya special educator ke saath, aur poori recording ka video banna chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Kaagaz par yeh strong rights hain. Zameen par haalat kamzor hai. 2018 mein Human Rights Watch ne disabled aurton aur ladkiyon ke saath sexual violence ke 17 cases par ek report di. 15 cases mein police aur court officials ne woh arrangements nahi kiye jo law ke hisaab se disability ke liye zaroori the. 16 cases mein survivors aur unki families ko pata hi nahi tha ki law mein disability ke liye khaas protections hain [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]].

Numbers bhi adhoore hain. Census 2011 ne 26.8 million logon ko disabled gina, yaani population ka 2.21%, jabki WHO-World Bank ka global estimate 15% hai. 2018 mein Human Rights Watch ne bataya tha ki na National Family Health Survey, na national crime data, disability ke hisaab se alag numbers deta hai [[hrw-invisible-victims-2018]]. Ab police data mein ek chhoti si jhalak milti hai: 2024 mein rape ke 29,536 cases darj hue, aur unmein se sirf 144 disabled aurat ke rape wali aggravated dhara mein darj hue. Uttar Pradesh mein aise sirf 3 cases the, aur Bihar mein ek bhi nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh numbers batate hain ki police yeh charge kitna kam lagati hai, yeh nahi ki yeh crime kitna hota hai. Koi nahi bata sakta ki kitni disabled aurtein rape ke baad pregnant hui, ya kitni aurton se pregnancy ka faisla chheen liya gaya.

Agar aap uski family se hain, toh test seedha hai: kya usne apne tareeke se "haan" kaha? Agar koi, chahe hospital hi kyun na ho, iske ulta kahe, toh legal services authorities se free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]].

emergency-pill-not-abortion-pill.en:
Imagine two purchases made in the same low voice at a chemist's counter in Patna. One customer wants "the pill for after" because a condom broke last night. Another wants "the kit" because her period is three weeks late. To many young Indians these sound like one medicine in two strengths. They are not. One works before a pregnancy exists. The other ends a pregnancy that does. Confusing them wastes the days that both the body and the law are counting.

## Myth: one pill, two names

The confusion has reasons. Both medicines are taken after sex, both are about not having a baby, and both are usually bought quietly, with no explanation offered or asked for. Most abortion pills in India are not taken in a clinic at all. In 2015, an estimated 11.5 million abortions were done with pills outside any health facility, and 87% of those used a ready-made "combipack" of mifepristone and misoprostol [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Two small packets, no conversation attached: it is easy to file both under one word, "the pill". That word hides two medicines running on two different clocks.

## What emergency contraception actually does

Emergency contraception (EC) stops a pregnancy from starting. EC pills work mainly by delaying ovulation, so that no egg is released for sperm to meet. They can be used up to five days (120 hours) after unprotected sex, and they work better the sooner they are taken. They cannot end a pregnancy that is already established. A copper IUD fitted by a trained provider within the same five days is the most effective emergency contraception of all. None of these protects against sexually transmitted infections [[who-ec]].

EC exists because contraception fails in ordinary ways: a condom splits, a pill is forgotten, "safe days" are miscounted, or sex is forced. With typical use, about 13 in every 100 couples relying on condoms have a pregnancy within a year; for the pill the figure is about 7, and for withdrawal about 20 [[who-fp]]. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 9.5% of currently married women in India reported using condoms and 5.1% the pill, while 10.3% relied on traditional methods [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For unmarried couples, the same failures happen with even fewer people to ask.

## What an abortion pill actually does

The abortion pill is a combination of two medicines, mifepristone and misoprostol, and it does the opposite job: it ends a pregnancy that already exists. India's Health Ministry guidelines (2023) approve the combination up to 9 weeks (63 days), report that it succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions, and allow a qualified doctor to prescribe it at a clinic linked to an approved abortion facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Two details matter. The nine weeks are counted from the first day of the last period, not from the day of sex. And before prescribing, a doctor confirms that there is a pregnancy and how far along it is, because the pills are approved only inside that limit [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The doctor also looks for signs of a pregnancy outside the uterus (an ectopic pregnancy), which needs urgent hospital care, not a kit [[nhs-ectopic]]. The kit is not a stronger morning-after pill, and it is not approved as contraception.

> EC runs on a clock that starts at sex. The abortion pill runs on a clock that starts at your last period. Neither clock waits.

## Why confusing them is dangerous

The mix-up can fail people in three ways.

The first is false comfort. EC taken after a pregnancy has begun will not end it [[who-ec]]. A woman who believes the morning-after pill "handled it" may stop counting, and by the time her period is clearly late, part of the nine-week window for pills has gone.

The second is misplaced guilt. Someone who believes EC is "a small abortion" may skip a medicine that only delays ovulation, miss the five-day window, and face the very pregnancy she feared. India had an estimated 48.1 million pregnancies in 2015; nearly half were unintended, and one third ended in induced abortion [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Not all of those could have been prevented, but a pill taken in time prevents some.

The third is the reverse error: treating the abortion kit as a backup for a broken condom, and swallowing a pregnancy-ending medicine without knowing whether there is a pregnancy, how many weeks it has run, or where it is. Those are exactly the questions the doctor's check exists to answer.

Consider a hypothetical. A 19-year-old in Bhopal waits four days out of embarrassment before buying an EC pill. When her period does not come, she waits another month, sure the pill "is still working". By the time she sees a doctor, she is past the nine weeks for which pills are approved on an outpatient prescription. She can still have a legal abortion, but now it must happen at a government hospital or approved facility.

## After unprotected sex: the hours that matter

Within five days, and the sooner the better: take EC, or ask a doctor or government health centre about a copper IUD, which can then stay in as regular contraception [[who-ec]].

If your next period is late, take a pregnancy test. If it is positive and you do not want to continue, see a registered doctor early, not a chemist's counter. Pills are approved only inside the nine weeks [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. After that, the law still allows abortion up to 20 weeks on one doctor's opinion where continuing would risk a woman's life or gravely injure her physical or mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Since 2021, the law's contraceptive-failure ground covers "any woman or her partner", so unmarried women can rely on it too [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

EC is a backup, not a method; needing it once is a reason to ask a doctor about a regular one. And if anyone calls the morning-after pill an abortion, tell them what it actually does: it delays the release of an egg. It cannot end what has already begun.
emergency-pill-not-abortion-pill.hg:
Socho, Patna mein ek chemist ki dukaan par ek hi dabi awaaz mein do cheezein khareedi ja rahi hain. Ek customer ko "baad wali goli" chahiye, kyunki kal raat condom phat gaya. Doosri ko "kit" chahiye, kyunki uska period teen hafte late hai. Bahut se young Indians ko yeh ek hi dawa ke do strength lagte hain. Aisa nahi hai. Ek pregnancy shuru hone se pehle kaam karti hai. Doosri shuru ho chuki pregnancy ko khatam karti hai. Dono ko ek samajhne mein woh din barbaad hote hain jinhe body bhi gin rahi hai aur law bhi.

## Myth: ek goli, do naam

Is confusion ki wajah hai. Dono dawaiyan sex ke baad li jaati hain, dono ka matlab hai bachcha na hona, aur dono aksar chupke se khareedi jaati hain, bina kisi explanation ke: na koi deta hai, na koi poochta hai. India mein zyada tar abortion pills kisi clinic mein li hi nahi jaati. 2015 mein lagbhag 11.5 million abortions kisi bhi health facility ke bahar pills se hue, aur unmein se 87% mein mifepristone aur misoprostol ka ready-made "combipack" use hua [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Do chhote packets, saath mein koi baat-cheet nahi: dono ko ek hi shabd mein daal dena aasaan hai, "the pill". Yeh ek shabd do alag dawaiyon ko chhupa deta hai, jinki ghadiyan bilkul alag chalti hain.

## Emergency contraception asal mein kya karti hai

Emergency contraception (EC) pregnancy ko shuru hone se rokti hai. EC pills mainly ovulation ko delay karke kaam karti hain, taaki koi egg release hi na ho jisse sperm mil sake. Inhe unprotected sex ke 5 din (120 ghante) baad tak liya ja sakta hai, aur jitni jaldi li jaayein, utna better kaam karti hain. Jo pregnancy pehle se established hai, use yeh khatam nahi kar sakti. Trained provider dwara unhi 5 dinon ke andar lagaya gaya copper IUD sabse effective emergency contraception hai. Inmein se koi bhi sexually transmitted infections se nahi bachata [[who-ec]].

EC isliye hai kyunki contraception roz-marra ke tareekon se fail hota hai: condom phat jaata hai, pill bhool jaati hai, "safe days" galat gine jaate hain, ya sex zabardasti hota hai. Typical use mein, condom par bharosa karne wale har 100 couples mein se lagbhag 13 ko ek saal ke andar pregnancy ho jaati hai; pill ke liye yeh figure lagbhag 7 hai, aur withdrawal ke liye lagbhag 20 [[who-fp]]. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein India ki currently married aurton mein se 9.5% ne condom aur 5.1% ne pill use karna bataya, jabki 10.3% traditional methods par nirbhar thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Unmarried couples ke saath bhi yahi failures hote hain, bas unke paas poochne ke liye log aur bhi kam hote hain.

## Abortion pill asal mein kya karti hai

Abortion pill do dawaiyon ka combination hai, mifepristone aur misoprostol, aur iska kaam bilkul ulta hai: yeh pehle se maujood pregnancy ko khatam karti hai. India ki Health Ministry ki guidelines (2023) is combination ko 9 hafte (63 din) tak approve karti hain, kehti hain ki shuruaati abortions mein yeh 95-99% cases mein kaamyaab hota hai, aur ek qualified doctor ise aise clinic mein likh sakta hai jo kisi approved abortion facility se juda ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Do baatein important hain. Yeh 9 hafte last period ke pehle din se gine jaate hain, sex wale din se nahi. Aur prescription dene se pehle doctor confirm karta hai ki pregnancy hai bhi ya nahi aur kitne hafte ki hai, kyunki pills sirf usi limit ke andar approved hain [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Doctor yeh bhi dekhta hai ki kahin pregnancy uterus ke bahar (ectopic pregnancy) toh nahi, kyunki uske liye turant hospital care chahiye, kit nahi [[nhs-ectopic]]. Kit koi "strong morning-after pill" nahi hai, aur contraception ke liye approved bhi nahi hai.

> EC ki ghadi sex se shuru hoti hai. Abortion pill ki ghadi tumhare last period se. Dono mein se koi ghadi rukti nahi.

## Dono ko ek samajhna khatarnak kyun hai

Yeh confusion teen tarah se nuksaan kar sakta hai.

Pehla hai jhootha sukoon. Pregnancy shuru hone ke baad li gayi EC use khatam nahi karegi [[who-ec]]. Jo aurat maan leti hai ki morning-after pill ne "sab sambhal liya", woh ginna band kar sakti hai, aur jab tak period saaf taur par late hota hai, tab tak pills ki 9 hafte wali window ka kuch hissa nikal chuka hota hai.

Doosra hai galat guilt. Jo ladki ya aurat maanti hai ki EC "chhota abortion" hai, woh ek aisi dawa chhod sakti hai jo sirf ovulation ko delay karti hai, 5 din ki window miss kar sakti hai, aur phir usi pregnancy ka saamna kar sakti hai jiska use darr tha. 2015 mein India mein lagbhag 48.1 million pregnancies hui; unmein se lagbhag aadhi unintended thi, aur ek-tihaai induced abortion par khatam hui [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Inmein se sab ko roka nahi ja sakta tha, lekin waqt par li gayi goli kuch ko zaroor rokti hai.

Teesra hai ulti galti: abortion kit ko phate condom ka backup samajhna, aur pregnancy khatam karne wali dawa nigal lena, bina yeh jaane ki pregnancy hai bhi ya nahi, kitne hafte ki hai, ya kahan hai. Doctor ka check thik inhi sawaalon ka jawab dene ke liye hota hai.

Ek hypothetical lo. Bhopal ki ek 19 saal ki ladki sharm ki wajah se chaar din rukti hai, phir EC pill khareedti hai. Jab period nahi aata, toh woh ek mahina aur intezaar karti hai, is yakeen mein ki pill "abhi bhi kaam kar rahi hai". Jab tak woh doctor ke paas pahunchti hai, woh un 9 hafton se aage nikal chuki hoti hai jinke liye pills outpatient prescription par approved hain. Legal abortion ab bhi ho sakta hai, lekin ab use kisi sarkari hospital ya approved facility mein hi karwana padega.

## Unprotected sex ke baad: woh ghante jo maayne rakhte hain

5 din ke andar, aur jitni jaldi utna behtar: EC lo, ya kisi doctor ya sarkari health centre se copper IUD ke baare mein poocho, jo baad mein regular contraception ki tarah lagi reh sakti hai [[who-ec]].

Agar agla period late ho, toh pregnancy test karo. Agar positive aaye aur tum pregnancy aage nahi badhana chahti, toh jaldi kisi registered doctor ke paas jao, chemist ke counter par nahi. Pills sirf 9 hafte ke andar approved hain [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Uske baad bhi law 20 hafte tak ek doctor ki opinion par abortion ki ijazat deta hai, agar pregnancy jaari rakhne se aurat ki jaan ko khatra ho ya uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan pahunche [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2021 se law ka contraceptive-failure wala ground "any woman or her partner" par lagu hota hai, yaani unmarried aurtein bhi is par bharosa kar sakti hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

EC ek backup hai, method nahi; ek baar iski zaroorat padi, toh yeh doctor se kisi regular method ke baare mein poochne ka signal hai. Aur agar koi morning-after pill ko abortion kahe, toh use batao ki yeh asal mein kya karti hai: yeh egg ke release ko delay karti hai. Jo shuru ho chuka hai, use yeh khatam nahi kar sakti.

find-safe-legal-abortion-provider-india.en:
Imagine a 20-year-old in Patna, six weeks pregnant, typing "abortion clinic near me" into her phone at midnight. The results mix a government hospital, private nursing homes and numbers promising a "safe kit, home delivery". On a screen they look alike. In law, and in what can go wrong, they are not. This guide is general information, not legal advice.

## Who is allowed to perform an abortion

India's Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act allows only a registered medical practitioner to end a pregnancy, and only at a place approved under the Act [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. A chemist, a compounder, a clinic assistant or a self-styled "doctor" is not a registered medical practitioner, however confident they sound.

Since the 2002 amendment, an abortion by anyone who is not a registered medical practitioner, or at a place not approved under the Act, is punishable with 2 to 7 years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. The danger is not theoretical: in 2015, an estimated 0.8 million abortions in India, 5% of the total, used methods other than pills or surgery that researchers judged probably unsafe [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

## Finding an approved facility, public or private

Start with a government hospital: the gynaecology department of a district hospital or a medical college. It is also where you would be sent if anything went wrong.

Private clinics and nursing homes need approval. Since 2002, District Level Committees of three to five members, chaired by the Chief Medical Officer or District Health Officer, approve private abortion facilities [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. So the CMO's office is the place to ask whether a clinic is approved, and an approved clinic should be able to show you its approval.

Early pregnancies have a third door. The Health Ministry's guidelines approve the mifepristone-misoprostol combination for pregnancies of up to nine weeks (63 days), with a 95-99% success rate in early abortions, and let a qualified doctor prescribe it at a clinic linked to an approved abortion facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The pills are legal from a doctor who has assessed you and has a hospital to send you to, not from a counter. The same guidelines treat abortion care as a package: counselling, the abortion, a follow-up and contraception [[nhm-cac]].

Many women never reach these doors. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), among women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion, 52.9% had it in the private sector, 20.3% in the public sector and 26.2% at home; 26.9% said they did it themselves, 30.0% in rural areas, and a doctor performed only 54.8% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A home abortion with pills is not automatically unsafe, but every step away from a doctor removes a safety check.

## Questions to ask before you pay

A legitimate clinic will answer these without irritation:

- Is the doctor who will see me a registered medical practitioner, and what is the registration number?
- Is this a government hospital, or is the place approved for MTP? Can I see the approval?
- How will you confirm how many weeks pregnant I am, and that the pregnancy is in the womb?
- Which method do you suggest, pills or a procedure, and why for me?
- What is the full cost, including medicines and the follow-up visit?
- If I bleed heavily at night, whom do I call and where do I go?
- Who will see my records?

The week count matters because the law is built on it. Up to 20 weeks, an abortion needs the opinion of one registered doctor; from 20 to 24 weeks, it needs two doctors and one of the categories of women listed in the rules [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. A provider who never asks how far along you are is skipping a check that both medicine and the law depend on.

## Red flags: the quack's script

Walk out if you hear any of these:

- "No need to examine you, just take this kit." Pills handed over without asking your dates or ruling out an ectopic pregnancy.
- "No need to come back." A real provider plans the follow-up.
- "Guaranteed, and no bleeding." Bleeding is how a medication abortion works, and no method succeeds every time.
- "Come after hours, cash only, no papers." Without records there is no accountability, and nothing to show the next doctor if you need one.
- "Want to know if it's a boy or a girl?" Under the PCPNDT Act, no one may tell a pregnant woman or her relatives the sex of the foetus "by words, signs or in any other manner" [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. A clinic willing to break that law is not one to trust with your body.

## Your rights inside the clinic

If you are 18 or older, your consent is the only one the MTP Act requires; a guardian's written consent is needed only if you are under 18 or mentally ill [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. No husband, parent or in-law has to sign, and marriage is not a condition: since 2021, the contraceptive-failure ground covers "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Your abortion is also confidential. Section 5A, added in 2021, makes it an offence for a registered doctor to reveal your name or other particulars to anyone not authorised by law, punishable with up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. If you are under 18, the doctor must still report the pregnancy to the police under POCSO, but since 2022 you and your guardian can ask for your name to be kept out of that report [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

If a clinic turns you away for being unmarried, demands a signature the law does not ask for, or pressures you, leave and go to a government hospital. And if you know of an unqualified person or an unapproved place offering abortions, tell the district CMO's office or the police. A quack's business survives on the same silence that sends women to the door.
find-safe-legal-abortion-provider-india.hg:
Socho, Patna ki ek 20 saal ki ladki, chhe hafte pregnant, aadhi raat ko phone par "abortion clinic near me" type kar rahi hai. Results mein sab mila-jula hai: ek sarkari hospital, kuch private nursing homes, aur kuch numbers jo "safe kit, home delivery" ka vaada karte hain. Screen par sab ek jaise dikhte hain. Kanoon ki nazar mein, aur jo galat ho sakta hai uski nazar se, bilkul nahi. Yeh guide general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Abortion karne ki ijaazat kise hai

India ka Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act pregnancy khatam karne ki ijaazat sirf registered medical practitioner ko deta hai, aur woh bhi sirf Act ke tahat approved jagah par [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Chemist, compounder, clinic ka assistant, ya khud ko "doctor" kehne wala, inmein se koi bhi registered medical practitioner nahi hai, chahe kitne bhi confidence se baat kare.

2002 ke amendment ke baad se, agar abortion koi aisa insaan kare jo registered medical practitioner nahi hai, ya kisi aisi jagah par ho jo Act ke tahat approved nahi, toh 2 se 7 saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Khatra sirf kitaabi nahi hai: 2015 mein India mein andaazan 0.8 million abortions, yaani kul ka 5%, goliyon ya surgery ke alawa aise tareekon se hue jinhe researchers ne shayad unsafe maana [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

## Approved jagah kaise dhoondhein, sarkari ya private

Shuruaat sarkari hospital se karo: district hospital ya medical college ka gynaecology department. Kuch galat hone par bhi tumhe wahin bheja jaata.

Private clinics aur nursing homes ko approval chahiye. 2002 se, teen se paanch members wali District Level Committees, jinke chairperson Chief Medical Officer (CMO) ya District Health Officer hote hain, private abortion facilities ko approve karti hain [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Isliye koi clinic approved hai ya nahi, yeh poochne ki sahi jagah CMO ka office hai, aur approved clinic ko apna approval dikhane mein koi dikkat nahi honi chahiye.

Early pregnancy ke liye ek teesra raasta bhi hai. Health Ministry ki guidelines mifepristone-misoprostol combination ko nau hafte (63 din) tak ki pregnancy ke liye approve karti hain. Early abortions mein yeh 95-99% baar kaamyaab hota hai, aur qualified doctor ise aise clinic se prescribe kar sakta hai jo kisi approved abortion facility se juda ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Matlab goliyan tab legal hain jab aisa doctor de jisne tumhe check kiya ho aur jiske paas zaroorat padne par bhejne ke liye hospital ho, counter se nahi. Yahi guidelines abortion care ko ek package maanti hain: counselling, abortion, follow-up aur contraception [[nhm-cac]].

Kai auratein in darwaazon tak pahunchti hi nahi. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein, jin auraton ki pichhli pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 52.9% ka abortion private sector mein, 20.3% ka public sector mein aur 26.2% ka ghar par hua. 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone khud kiya, gaon mein yeh 30.0% tha, aur sirf 54.8% abortions doctor ne kiye [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ghar par goliyon se hua abortion apne aap unsafe nahi hota, lekin doctor se har kadam door hone par ek safety check chhoot jaata hai.

## Paise dene se pehle yeh sawaal poocho

Sahi clinic in sawaalon ka jawaab bina chidhe dega:

- Jo doctor mujhe dekhenge, kya woh registered medical practitioner hain, aur unka registration number kya hai?
- Kya yeh sarkari hospital hai, ya yeh jagah MTP ke liye approved hai? Kya main approval dekh sakti hoon?
- Aap kaise confirm karenge ki main kitne hafte pregnant hoon, aur pregnancy womb ke andar hi hai?
- Aap kaun sa method suggest karte hain, goliyan ya procedure, aur mere liye wahi kyun?
- Dawaiyon aur follow-up visit samet poora kharcha kitna hai?
- Agar raat ko bahut bleeding ho, toh main kise call karun aur kahan jaun?
- Mere records kaun-kaun dekhega?

Hafton ki ginti isliye zaroori hai kyunki kanoon usi par bana hai. 20 hafte tak abortion ke liye ek registered doctor ki raay chahiye; 20 se 24 hafte ke beech do doctors ki raay chahiye, aur rules mein likhi auraton ki kisi category mein hona bhi zaroori hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Jo provider poochta hi nahi ki pregnancy kitne hafte ki hai, woh aisa check skip kar raha hai jis par medicine aur kanoon dono tike hain.

## Red flags: jhola-chhaap ki script

Inmein se kuch bhi suno toh uth kar chal do:

- "Check karne ki zaroorat nahi, bas yeh kit le lo." Yaani bina tumhari dates pooche ya ectopic pregnancy rule out kiye goliyan pakda dena.
- "Wapas aane ki zaroorat nahi." Sahi provider follow-up plan karta hai.
- "Guarantee hai, aur bleeding bhi nahi hogi." Medication abortion mein bleeding hi toh process hai, aur koi bhi method har baar kaamyaab nahi hota.
- "Clinic band hone ke baad aana, sirf cash, koi kaagaz nahi." Records nahi toh koi jawabdehi nahi, aur zaroorat padne par agle doctor ko dikhane ke liye bhi kuch nahi.
- "Jaanna hai ladka hai ya ladki?" PCPNDT Act ke tahat koi bhi pregnant aurat ya uske rishtedaaron ko foetus ka sex "by words, signs or in any other manner" nahi bata sakta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Jo clinic yeh kanoon todne ko taiyaar hai, us par apni body ka bharosa mat karo.

## Clinic ke andar tumhare haq

Agar tum 18 ya usse badi ho, toh MTP Act mein sirf tumhari apni consent chahiye; guardian ki likhit consent sirf tab chahiye jab tum 18 se kam ho ya mentally ill ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Husband, parents ya sasural walon ko sign nahi karna hota, aur shaadi koi shart nahi hai: 2021 se contraceptive failure wala ground "any woman or her partner" par laagu hota hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Tumhara abortion confidential bhi hai. 2021 mein jode gaye Section 5A ke tahat, registered doctor agar tumhara naam ya koi aur detail kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise kanoon ne ijaazat nahi di, toh yeh jurm hai, jiski saza ek saal tak ki jail, fine ya dono hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Agar tum 18 se kam ho, toh POCSO ke tahat doctor ko pregnancy police ko report karni hi hogi, lekin 2022 se tum aur tumhare guardian maang sakte ho ki us report mein tumhara naam na likha jaaye [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Agar koi clinic unmarried hone ki wajah se mana kare, aisa sign maange jo kanoon nahi maangta, ya tum par dabaav daale, toh wahan se niklo aur sarkari hospital jao. Aur agar tumhe kisi aise unqualified insaan ya unapproved jagah ke baare mein pata hai jahan abortion hota hai, toh district CMO ke office ya police ko batao. Jhola-chhaap ka dhandha usi chuppi par chalta hai jo auraton ko uske darwaaze tak bhejti hai.

india-abortion-count-15-million-hidden.en:
Two numbers describe abortion in India, and they are not even close. The Health Ministry recorded 701,415 abortions in 2014-15. A national research estimate for 2015, the most recent we could find, is 15.6 million [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Put side by side, the official record caught fewer than one abortion in twenty. Most of the rest were pill abortions outside any health facility, with drugs from chemists and informal vendors; others were done by private doctors outside registered facilities. The state never saw them.

## Two numbers that should match

Start with the official count. For 15 years, the Health Ministry's yearly figure stayed between 621,000 and 770,000 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Then the estimate. In 2018, researchers from the Guttmacher Institute, the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) in Mumbai and the Population Council published a national study in The Lancet Global Health. They estimated 15.6 million abortions in India in 2015, somewhere between 14.1 million and 17.3 million. That is 47.0 abortions for every 1,000 women aged 15-49 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

The gap is not a typing error. The official figure counts only abortions that facilities report. It leaves out private doctors who do not work in registered facilities, and it leaves out abortion pills sold without a prescription [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. In other words, it leaves out most of how India actually ends pregnancies.

## One pregnancy in three

The same study estimated 48.1 million pregnancies in India in 2015. One third ended in abortion. Nearly half were unintended, a rate of 70.1 unintended pregnancies per 1,000 women aged 15-49 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

That is not unusual by world standards. The WHO says around 73 million abortions take place worldwide each year, and 29% of all pregnancies end in one [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. India's one in three sits close to the world's three in ten. The problem is how little of it India's official records catch.

> Abortion in India is common. Counting it is what is rare.

## Where the missing abortions happen

Mostly, in a strip of tablets. About 11.5 million of the 15.6 million abortions in 2015 (73%) were done with pills outside any health facility. Only 3.4 million (22%) took place in a facility, and 73% of those were private [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Ready-made "combipacks" of mifepristone and misoprostol were used in 87% of the pill abortions outside facilities [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Another 0.8 million (5%) used other methods the researchers judged probably unsafe [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Women's own answers show part of this picture. Among women in NFHS-5 (2019-21) whose last pregnancy ended in abortion, 26.2% had it at home and 26.9% said they did it themselves, rising to 30.0% in rural areas. 52.9% went to the private sector and 20.3% to the public sector [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The pills themselves are approved and effective. Health Ministry guidelines say the mifepristone-misoprostol combination is approved up to nine weeks (63 days), works in 95-99% of early abortions, and can be prescribed by a qualified doctor at a clinic linked to an approved facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The trouble is the route. Most pill abortions in India happen without a prescription or medical advice, and little is known about what information women get, or whether they take the pills correctly [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Consider a hypothetical. A 26-year-old in Indore, seven weeks pregnant, buys a kit at a chemist's counter on a friend's advice and takes it at home. This time, nothing goes wrong. No clinic sees her, no register lists her, and the abortion does not exist for the state.

## Why surveys and registers miss them

Registers miss these abortions by design. Surveys miss them because many women do not tell. In NFHS-5, just 2.9% of women's last pregnancies in the five years before the survey were reported as ending in abortion: 4.0% in urban areas, 2.5% in rural areas [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The two numbers do not measure exactly the same thing. NFHS asks about each woman's last pregnancy, while the 2015 study modelled every pregnancy in one year. But abortion is heavily under-reported in household surveys. Picture the same woman from Indore three years later, with a surveyor at the door and her mother-in-law in the room. She may simply not mention it.

Getting a credible number took a dedicated effort: a survey of thousands of health facilities in six states, national sales data for abortion pills, and the earlier round of NFHS. More than a decade on, we could find no newer national estimate.

## What you cannot fix if you cannot count

Start with deaths. The Health Ministry's 2023 abortion care guidelines say unsafe abortion causes about 8% of maternal deaths. That share comes from Registrar General cause-of-death data for 2001-03 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. In 2022, UNFPA India called unsafe abortion the third leading cause of maternal deaths, with close to eight women dying every day from related causes and young women aged 15-19 at the highest risk [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. These are estimates built on old data, not counts.

Then injuries. In the six states surveyed in 2015, 4-16% of women receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications such as infection and sepsis [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. In NFHS-5, 15.6% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion reported complications; 89.7% of them sought treatment, 70.6% of it in the private sector [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

A country that cannot see its abortions cannot plan how many trained providers, approved clinics or medicines it needs. Nor can it enforce the law meant to keep unqualified providers away from women. Since 2002, an abortion by someone who is not a registered doctor, or at an unapproved place, can bring two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. That means little when the state sees fewer than one abortion in twenty.

For a woman, the practical message is simpler. A legal, early abortion with a doctor's prescription is both effective and private: since 2021, a doctor who reveals her name or details to anyone not authorised by law faces up to a year in prison [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. India's invisible abortions do not have to be unsafe ones.
india-abortion-count-15-million-hidden.hg:
India mein abortion ki tasveer do numbers se banti hai, aur dono mein zameen-aasmaan ka farak hai. Health Ministry ne 2014-15 mein 701,415 abortions record kiye. Lekin 2015 ka ek national research estimate, jo hamein mila sabse naya estimate hai, 15.6 million, yaani 1.56 crore abortions ka hai [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Dono ko saath rakho, toh official record mein bees mein se ek abortion bhi darj nahi hua. Baaki mein se zyada tar abortions kisi health facility ke bahar pills se hue, aur yeh pills chemists aur informal vendors se aayi; kuch abortions aise private doctors ne kiye jo registered facilities mein kaam nahi karte. Sarkar ne unhe kabhi dekha hi nahi.

## Do numbers jo match hone chahiye the

Pehle official count dekho. 15 saal tak Health Ministry ka saalana aankda 621,000 se 770,000 ke beech hi raha [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Ab estimate dekho. 2018 mein Guttmacher Institute, Mumbai ke International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) aur Population Council ke researchers ne The Lancet Global Health mein ek national study publish ki. Unke hisaab se 2015 mein India mein 15.6 million abortions hue, kahin 14.1 million se 17.3 million ke beech. Yaani 15-49 saal ki har 1,000 aurton par 47.0 abortions [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Yeh farak koi typing mistake nahi hai. Official figure sirf wahi abortions ginta hai jo facilities report karti hain. Ismein woh private doctors nahi aate jo registered facilities mein kaam nahi karte, aur woh pills bhi nahi aati jo bina prescription ke bikti hain [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Seedhe shabdon mein, India mein zyada tar abortions jis tarah hote hain, wahi is ginti se bahar hai.

## Har teen mein se ek pregnancy

Isi study ke mutabik 2015 mein India mein 48.1 million pregnancies hui. Unmein se ek-tihaai abortion par khatam hui. Lagbhag aadhi pregnancies unintended thi, yaani 15-49 saal ki har 1,000 aurton par 70.1 unintended pregnancies [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Duniya ke hisaab se yeh koi anokhi baat nahi hai. WHO ke mutabik duniya mein har saal lagbhag 73 million abortions hote hain, aur saari pregnancies mein se 29% abortion par khatam hoti hain [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. India ka "teen mein se ek" duniya ke "das mein se teen" ke kareeb hi hai. Problem yeh hai ki India ke official records iska kitna kam hissa pakad paate hain.

> India mein abortion aam baat hai. Use ginna aam baat nahi hai.

## Gaayab abortions kahan hote hain

Zyada tar, pills ki ek strip se. 2015 ke 15.6 million abortions mein se lagbhag 11.5 million (73%) kisi hospital ya clinic ke bahar pills se hue. Sirf 3.4 million (22%) kisi facility mein hue, aur unmein se bhi 73% private the [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Bahar pills se hue abortions mein se 87% mein mifepristone aur misoprostol ka ready-made "combipack" use hua [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Baaki 0.8 million (5%) abortions aise tareekon se hue jinhe researchers ne shayad unsafe maana [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Aurton ke apne jawab is tasveer ka ek hissa dikhate hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.2% ka abortion ghar par hua, aur 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone yeh khud kiya. Gaon mein yeh 30.0% tha. 52.9% private sector mein gayi aur 20.3% public sector mein [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh pills apne aap mein approved hain aur kaam bhi karti hain. Health Ministry ki guidelines kehti hain ki mifepristone-misoprostol ka combination 9 hafte (63 din) tak ke liye approved hai, shuruaati abortions mein 95-99% cases mein kaam karta hai, aur ise ek qualified doctor likh sakta hai, aise clinic mein jo kisi approved abortion facility se juda ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Problem raaste mein hai. India mein zyada tar pill abortions bina prescription ya doctor ki salah ke hote hain, aur aurton ko kya jaankari milti hai ya woh pills sahi tareeke se leti hain ya nahi, iske baare mein bahut kam pata hai [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Ek hypothetical lo. Indore ki 26 saal ki ek aurat saat hafte pregnant hai. Woh dost ke kehne par chemist se ek kit khareedti hai aur ghar par le leti hai. Is baar kuch galat nahi hota. Koi clinic use nahi dekhta, kisi register mein uska naam nahi aata, aur sarkar ke liye yeh abortion hua hi nahi.

## Survey aur register inhe kyun nahi pakad paate

Register in abortions ko apni banawat ki wajah se miss karte hain. Survey isliye miss karte hain kyunki kai aurtein batati hi nahi. NFHS-5 mein, survey se pehle ke paanch saalon mein aurton ki last pregnancies mein se sirf 2.9% abortion par khatam hui batayi gayi: shehri ilaakon mein 4.0%, gaon ke ilaakon mein 2.5% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Yeh dono numbers bilkul ek hi cheez nahi naapte. NFHS har aurat ki last pregnancy ke baare mein poochta hai, jabki 2015 ki study ne ek saal ki saari pregnancies ka hisaab lagaya. Phir bhi, ghar-ghar jaakar hone wale surveys mein abortion bahut kam bataya jaata hai. Indore wali usi aurat ko teen saal baad socho: darwaze par surveyor khada hai, aur kamre mein uski saas baithi hai. Ho sakta hai woh iska zikr hi na kare.

Ek bharosemand number nikaalne ke liye alag se badi mehnat karni padi: chhe states mein hazaaron health facilities ka survey, abortion pills ki desh bhar ki sales ka data, aur NFHS ke pichhle round ke aankde. Das saal se zyada beet gaye, phir bhi hamein isse naya koi national estimate nahi mila.

## Jo gin nahi sakte, use theek bhi nahi kar sakte

Pehle maut ki baat. Health Ministry ki 2023 ki abortion care guidelines kehti hain ki maternal deaths mein se lagbhag 8% unsafe abortion se hoti hain. Lekin yeh hissa Registrar General ke 2001-03 ke cause-of-death data se aata hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. 2022 mein UNFPA India ne kaha ki maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah unsafe abortion hai, isse judi wajahon se har din lagbhag aath aurton ki maut hoti hai, aur 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko sabse zyada khatra hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Yeh purane data par bane estimates hain, asli ginti nahi.

Phir complications. 2015 mein jin chhe states mein survey hua, wahan abortion ke baad care ke liye aayi 4-16% aurton ka ilaaj serious complications ke liye ho raha tha, jaise infection aur sepsis [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. NFHS-5 mein jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications batayi; unmein se 89.7% ne ilaaj karwaya, aur ilaaj ka 70.6% hissa private sector mein hua [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Jo desh apne abortions dekh hi nahi pata, woh yeh bhi plan nahi kar sakta ki use kitne trained providers, kitne approved clinics aur kitni dawaiyan chahiye. Na hi woh us law ko lagu kar sakta hai jo aurton ko unqualified providers se bachane ke liye bana hai. 2002 se, agar abortion koi aisa insaan kare jo registered doctor nahi hai, ya bina approval wali jagah par ho, toh 2 se 7 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Lekin jab sarkar bees mein se ek abortion bhi nahi dekh paati, toh is rule ka zyada matlab nahi bachta.

Ek aurat ke liye message isse simple hai. Doctor ke prescription par, jaldi aur legal tareeke se karwaya gaya abortion effective bhi hai aur private bhi: 2021 se, agar koi doctor uska naam ya details kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne permission nahi di, toh use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. India ke anadekhe abortions ka unsafe hona zaroori nahi hai.

india-abortion-law-timeline-1964-2022.en:
India did not legalise abortion in one stroke. It carved exceptions, one failure at a time, out of a crime older than the country itself. Each change on this timeline answered a specific problem: a law too harsh, girls disappearing before birth, unqualified providers, women turned away at 20 weeks. Read in order, the timeline also shows which problems are still waiting. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 1964-66: a committee calls the old law too restrictive

The modern law began with a government committee formed in 1964 (some accounts say 1965) and headed by Shantilal Shah. Its report, submitted in 1966, was blunt [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]]:

> "The committee considers the above provision too restrictive; and therefore recommends that it should be liberalised."

The law it judged too restrictive was the criminal code. Section 312 of the Indian Penal Code of 1860 punished anyone who caused a woman to miscarry, unless it was done in good faith to save her life, and it expressly covered a woman who caused her own miscarriage [[gazette-bns-2023]] [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. ThePrint's history of the law notes that the committee did not see abortion as a workable method of population control [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]].

## 1971-72: the MTP Act and its 20-week ceiling

Parliament's answer was the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, which received the President's assent on 10 August 1971 [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]] and came into force on 1 April 1972 [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. It did not repeal the crime. It created an exception that shields registered doctors who end a pregnancy within its conditions [[gazette-bns-2023]].

One registered doctor's opinion was enough up to 12 weeks; between 12 and 20 weeks, two had to agree. The contraceptive-failure ground covered only "any married woman or her husband", and a guardian had to consent for a girl under 18 or for a woman the Act called a "lunatic" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Three failures were written in from day one: a hard ceiling at 20 weeks, a law that pictured wives, and a decision that belonged to doctors.

## 1994-2008: a ban on sex selection, jail for quacks, and the pill

The next failure was one the 1971 law did not address: prenatal tests used to find and abort girls. The Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act of 1994 came into operation on 1 January 1996 [[mohfw-pndt-act-rules-2003]]. At first it barred only the person doing the test from telling a woman or her relatives the sex of the foetus; since a 2003 amendment, no one may reveal it "by words, signs or in any other manner" [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. The Health Ministry links that amendment, which also renamed the law and extended it to sex selection before conception, to a 2000 Supreme Court petition by CEHAT and others over slow implementation [[mohfw-pndt-act-rules-2003]]. It has not been enough: at least 9.0 million female births went "missing" between 2000 and 2019, Pew estimates [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

In 2002 the MTP Act turned on unsafe providers: an abortion by anyone other than a registered medical practitioner, or at an unapproved place, became punishable with two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment, and district committees could now approve private clinics. The same amendment replaced "lunatic" with "mentally ill person" [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

The same year brought the pill: mifepristone was approved in 2002 and misoprostol in 2006 for pregnancies up to seven weeks, and a combipack for up to nine weeks in December 2008 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2018]]. Just as the law tightened its grip on who and where, the pill moved abortion out of the clinic. Of an estimated 15.6 million abortions in 2015, 11.5 million (73%) were medication abortions outside any health facility [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

## 2021: court petitions force the first big rewrite

The 20-week ceiling kept sending women to judges, and the government itself cited petitions over foetal abnormalities and sexual violence. The Lok Sabha passed an amendment on 17 March 2020; the Rajya Sabha approved it only on 16 March 2021 [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. It took effect on 24 September 2021 [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]].

One doctor could now act up to 20 weeks, two up to 24 weeks for categories listed in rules, and a Medical Board could approve an abortion at any stage for a substantial foetal abnormality. "Any married woman or her husband" became "any woman or her partner", and Section 5A made it punishable, with up to a year in prison, for a doctor to reveal a woman's identity [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. We compare the old and new texts clause by clause in a separate explainer. The failure it left: unless her life is in danger, a rape survivor past 24 weeks still has no route but a court.

## 2022 and after: autonomy in the courts, not yet in the code

The rules for 20 to 24 weeks spoke of a "change of marital status". On 15 July 2022 the Delhi High Court refused interim relief to an unmarried woman about 22 weeks pregnant, saying it "cannot go beyond the Statute"; on 21 July the Supreme Court let her end the pregnancy if a Medical Board at AIIMS Delhi found it safe [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

On 29 September 2022, in X v. Principal Secretary, the court held that excluding unmarried women from that window violates Article 14. It grounded the right in reproductive autonomy, relying on Suchita Srivastava (2009) and the nine-judge privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017), which tied abortion to the right to make reproductive choices under Article 21. It also held that "rape" in the Act includes marital rape [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Our explainer on that ruling goes further.

Then Parliament re-enacted the old crime. When the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024 [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], its Section 88 copied Section 312 word for word, including the line about a woman who causes her own miscarriage [[gazette-bns-2023]]. Almost six decades after the Shah Committee called that law too restrictive, it is still the baseline, and the MTP Act is still an exception to it.

So the timeline ends with its own to-do list: autonomy that lives in a judgment but not in the statute, no route for survivors past 24 weeks, and a criminal ban that still names the woman herself.
india-abortion-law-timeline-1964-2022.hg:
India mein abortion ek jhatke mein legal nahi hua. Ek aise crime mein, jo desh se bhi purana hai, ek-ek failure ke baad exceptions kaate gaye. Is timeline ka har change kisi khaas problem ka jawab tha: bahut sakht law, paida hone se pehle gayab hoti betiyan, unqualified providers, aur 20 hafte par lauta di gayi women. Order mein padho, toh yeh bhi dikhta hai ki kaun si problems ab bhi wait kar rahi hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1964-66: ek committee purane law ko too restrictive kehti hai

Aaj ke law ki shuruaat ek government committee se hui, jo 1964 mein bani (kuch accounts 1965 kehte hain) aur jiske head Shantilal Shah the. 1966 mein submit hui uski report ne seedha kaha [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]]:

> "The committee considers the above provision too restrictive; and therefore recommends that it should be liberalised." (Shah Committee report, 1966)

Committee ne jis law ko too restrictive kaha, woh criminal law tha. 1860 ke Indian Penal Code ka Section 312 har us insaan ko saza deta tha jo kisi woman ka miscarriage cause kare, jab tak woh good faith mein uski jaan bachane ke liye na kiya gaya ho, aur yeh section saaf kehta tha ki jo woman khud apna miscarriage cause kare, woh bhi iske under aati hai [[gazette-bns-2023]] [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]]. ThePrint ki history ke mutabik committee abortion ko population control ka kaam ka tareeka nahi maanti thi [[theprint-abortion-law-history-2022]].

## 1971-72: MTP Act aur uski 20 hafte ki limit

Parliament ka jawab tha Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, jise 10 August 1971 ko President ki assent mili [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]] aur jo 1 April 1972 ko lagu hua [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Isne crime ko khatam nahi kiya. Isne ek exception banaya jo un registered doctors ko bachata hai jo iski conditions ke andar pregnancy end karte hain [[gazette-bns-2023]].

12 hafte tak ek registered doctor ki opinion kaafi thi; 12 se 20 hafte ke beech do doctors ko agree karna hota tha. Contraceptive-failure ground sirf "any married woman or her husband" ke liye tha, aur 18 se kam umar ki ladki ya jise Act "lunatic" kehta tha, uske liye guardian ki consent zaroori thi [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Pehle din se teen failures likhe hue the: 20 hafte ki hard limit, sirf wives ko dhyan mein rakhne wala law, aur ek decision jo doctors ke haath mein tha.

## 1994-2008: sex selection par ban, quacks ko jail, aur pill

Agla failure aisa tha jise 1971 ka law address hi nahi karta tha: prenatal tests se betiyon ka pata lagakar abortion karwana. 1994 ka Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques Act 1 January 1996 se lagu hua [[mohfw-pndt-act-rules-2003]]. Shuru mein yeh sirf test karne wale insaan ko woman ya uske rishtedaaron ko foetus ka sex batane se rokta tha; 2003 ke amendment ke baad koi bhi ise "by words, signs or in any other manner" reveal nahi kar sakta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Health Ministry us amendment ko, jisne law ka naam bhi badla aur use conception se pehle ke sex selection par bhi lagu kiya, CEHAT aur doosron ki 2000 ki Supreme Court petition se jodti hai, jo slow implementation ke khilaaf thi [[mohfw-pndt-act-rules-2003]]. Phir bhi yeh kaafi nahi raha: Pew ke estimate ke mutabik 2000 se 2019 ke beech kam se kam 9.0 million (90 lakh) female births "missing" ho gaye [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

2002 mein MTP Act ne unsafe providers par shikanja kasa: registered medical practitioner ke alawa koi aur abortion kare, ya bina approval wali jagah par ho, toh 2 se 7 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti thi, aur district committees ab private clinics ko approve kar sakti thi. Isi amendment ne "lunatic" ki jagah "mentally ill person" likha [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

Usi saal pill bhi aayi: mifepristone ko 2002 mein aur misoprostol ko 2006 mein 7 hafte tak ki pregnancy ke liye approval mila, aur December 2008 mein ek combipack ko 9 hafte tak ke liye [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2018]]. Jis waqt law yeh kas raha tha ki abortion kaun kare aur kahan, usi waqt pill ne abortion ko clinic se bahar pahuncha diya. 2015 mein andaazan 15.6 million abortions mein se 11.5 million (73%) medication abortions the jo kisi health facility ke bahar hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

## 2021: court petitions ne pehla bada rewrite karwaya

20 hafte ki limit women ko baar-baar judges ke paas bhejti rahi, aur government ne khud foetal abnormalities aur sexual violence wali petitions ka hawala diya. Lok Sabha ne amendment 17 March 2020 ko pass kiya; Rajya Sabha ne use 16 March 2021 ko jaakar approve kiya [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Yeh 24 September 2021 ko lagu hua [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]].

Ab ek doctor 20 hafte tak act kar sakta tha, rules mein listed categories ke liye do doctors 24 hafte tak, aur substantial foetal abnormality ho toh Medical Board kisi bhi stage par abortion approve kar sakta tha. "Any married woman or her husband" ban gaya "any woman or her partner", aur Section 5A ne doctor ke liye woman ki identity reveal karne par 1 saal tak ki jail ka rule banaya [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Purane aur naye text ko clause by clause humne ek alag explainer mein compare kiya hai. Jo failure bacha: jab tak jaan ko khatra na ho, 24 hafte ke baad rape survivor ke paas court ke alawa koi raasta nahi.

## 2022 aur uske baad: autonomy courts mein, code mein abhi nahi

20 se 24 hafte ke rules mein "change of marital status" ki baat thi. 15 July 2022 ko Delhi High Court ne lagbhag 22 hafte pregnant ek unmarried woman ko interim relief dene se mana kar diya, yeh kehkar ki woh "cannot go beyond the Statute"; 21 July ko Supreme Court ne use pregnancy end karne di, is shart par ki AIIMS Delhi ka Medical Board ise safe maane [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

29 September 2022 ko X v. Principal Secretary case mein court ne kaha ki unmarried women ko us window se bahar rakhna Article 14 ke khilaaf hai. Court ne is right ki jad reproductive autonomy mein batayi, aur Suchita Srivastava (2009) aur nine-judge privacy ruling K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) ka sahara liya, jisne abortion ko Article 21 ke under reproductive choices ke right se joda tha. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki is Act mein "rape" mein marital rape bhi aata hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Us ruling par hamara explainer aur detail mein jaata hai.

Phir Parliament ne purane crime ko dobara law mein likh diya. 1 July 2024 ko jab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li [[pib-new-criminal-laws-highlights-2024]], uske Section 88 ne Section 312 ko word for word copy kar liya, us line ke saath bhi ki jo woman khud apna miscarriage cause kare woh bhi iske under hai [[gazette-bns-2023]]. Shah Committee ke us law ko too restrictive kehne ke lagbhag chhe dashak baad bhi wahi law baseline hai, aur MTP Act ab bhi uska bas ek exception hai.

Toh timeline apni to-do list ke saath khatam hoti hai: autonomy jo ek judgment mein hai par statute mein nahi, 24 hafte ke baad survivors ke liye koi raasta nahi, aur ek criminal ban jo aaj bhi khud woman ko saza ke daayre mein rakhta hai.

marital-rape-abortion-law-2022-ruling.en:
Imagine a 26-year-old in Kanpur, married five years, who finds she is pregnant. She did not want this pregnancy and did not agree to the sex that caused it. At a police station, the law will not count it as rape: in criminal law, a husband cannot rape his adult wife. At a hospital, the same words let a doctor treat it as rape. Both answers are correct today.

## One word, two laws

Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says that sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A husband who forces sex on a wife living separately faces only 2 to 7 years under Section 67, far below the 10-year minimum for raping any other woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The Union government has defended it: in an October 2024 affidavit it told the Supreme Court that calling non-consensual sex within marriage rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]].

India's abortion law, the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, uses the same word. Since 2022, it means something different there.

## What the Supreme Court held in 2022

The case, X v. Principal Secretary, began with an unmarried woman about 22 weeks pregnant. But on 29 September 2022 the Supreme Court also settled a question about wives: "rape" in the MTP Act and its rules includes marital rape, so a wife pregnant from forced sex by her husband can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks as a survivor of rape [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The weeks matter. Up to 20 weeks, one doctor's opinion is enough if the pregnancy would gravely injure a woman's physical or mental health. From 20 to 24 weeks, abortion is allowed only for categories listed in the rules, with two doctors agreeing [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. The first of the seven categories, notified on 12 October 2021, is "survivors of sexual assault or rape or incest" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Before the ruling, a wife forced into pregnancy had no clear claim to it. Now she does.

## No FIR, no proof: how the rape presumption works

One sentence in the MTP Act does most of the work. When a pregnant woman alleges that her pregnancy was caused by rape, "the anguish caused by the pregnancy shall be presumed to constitute a grave injury to the mental health of the pregnant woman" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. That injury is a legal ground for ending a pregnancy.

The key word is "alleged". The Supreme Court said no FIR has to be registered, and no rape proved in court, before a woman can rely on it [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. That matters most for a wife: she cannot file a rape FIR against her husband, and the abortion law does not ask for one.

At the clinic, she tells the doctor the pregnancy came from sex she was forced into. She needs no signature from her husband: an adult woman's own consent is the only consent the MTP Act requires [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Nor may the doctor tell him: since 2021, Section 5A punishes revealing her name or details to anyone not authorised by law with up to a year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

If a clinic has not heard of the ruling, she or anyone with her can name it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Violence the crime data cannot see

Who commits sexual violence against married women in India? Overwhelmingly, husbands. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 82% of ever-married women aged 18-49 who had experienced sexual violence named their current husband and 14% a former husband. Across all ever-married women aged 18-49, 4.6% said a husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Very little of it reaches anyone: among women who had faced physical or sexual violence only from their current husband, just 11.3% had ever sought help. And 12.2% of men aged 15-49 said a husband has the right to use force to have sex if his wife refuses [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Police data cannot fill the gap: the law gives this violence nowhere to go. In NCRB's 2024 count of rape cases with a known offender, separated husbands share one column with friends, online friends and live-in partners "on pretext of marriage": 13,879 cases in all [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A husband who lives with his adult wife cannot appear in it. For most wives forced into pregnancy, the MTP Act, as the Supreme Court has read it, is the only Indian law that treats what happened to them as rape, and it asks for no proof.

## The pending challenge and what it could change

The exception predates the BNS: until July 2024 it was Exception 2 to Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code. On 9 September 2026 a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant posted the challenges to it for final hearing, saying it would decide whether the exception is valid and whether a husband can be prosecuted while it stands [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. As of 19 November 2026 there was no ruling; the bench said it would fix the final hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026, before the winter break [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

If the exception falls, a wife could file a rape complaint like any other woman, and police data could start recording what surveys have shown for years. If it survives, much turns on the second question: unless the court allows a prosecution anyway, wives keep this abortion route and must rely on cruelty and domestic violence laws for the rest. Either way, the 2022 ruling stands on its own: the court said its reading applies "solely for the purposes of the MTP Act" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

A wife need not wait for December to use it. Beyond the clinic, 985 One Stop Centres were operating across India in July 2026; between April 2015 and June 2026 they assisted over 15.20 lakh women [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].
marital-rape-abortion-law-2022-ruling.hg:
Sochiye, Kanpur ki ek 26 saal ki aurat. Shaadi ko paanch saal hue hain, aur ab use pata chalta hai ki woh pregnant hai. Woh yeh pregnancy nahi chahti thi, aur jis sex se yeh hui, uske liye usne haan bhi nahi kahi thi. Police station mein kanoon ise rape nahi maanta, kyunki criminal law kehta hai ki pati apni adult wife ka rape nahi kar sakta. Lekin hospital mein yahi baat kahe, toh doctor ise rape maan kar chal sakta hai. Aaj India mein yeh dono baatein ek saath sach hain.

## Ek shabd, do kanoon

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar wife 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex ya koi bhi sexual act rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Agar wife alag reh rahi ho aur pati zabardasti kare, toh Section 67 mein sirf 2 se 7 saal ki saza hai, jabki kisi aur aurat ke rape par kam se kam 10 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Union government ne is exception ka bachaav kiya hai. October 2024 ke ek affidavit mein usne Supreme Court se kaha ki shaadi ke andar bina consent ke sex ko rape kehna "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" hoga, yaani zaroorat se zyada sakht, aur jurm ke hisaab se bemel [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]].

India ka abortion law, yaani Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, bhi yahi shabd use karta hai: rape. Lekin 2022 se wahan iska matlab badal gaya hai.

## Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kya kaha

Case tha X v. Principal Secretary. Iski shuruaat ek unmarried aurat se hui thi, jo qareeb 22 hafte pregnant thi. Lekin 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court ne wives se juda sawaal bhi suljha diya. Court ne kaha ki MTP Act aur uske rules mein "rape" mein marital rape bhi shamil hai. Yaani pati ki zabardasti se pregnant hui wife, rape survivor ke taur par 24 hafte tak abortion kara sakti hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Yahan hafton ka hisaab bahut maayne rakhta hai. 20 hafte tak ek doctor ki raay kaafi hai, agar pregnancy jaari rakhne se aurat ki physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan ho. 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion sirf un auraton ka ho sakta hai jinki category rules mein likhi hai, aur iske liye do doctors ka raazi hona zaroori hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 12 October 2021 ko notify hue rules mein aisi saat categories hain, aur pehli hai "survivors of sexual assault or rape or incest" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Is faisle se pehle zabardasti pregnant hui wife ka is category par saaf haq nahi tha. Ab hai.

## Na FIR, na saboot: kanoon pehle se kya maan leta hai

MTP Act ka ek sentence sabse bada kaam karta hai. Agar pregnant aurat kehti hai ki pregnancy rape se hui hai, toh kanoon maan leta hai ki is pregnancy ki takleef uski mental health ke liye "grave injury", yaani gambhir chot hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Aur mental health ko gambhir chot, abortion ki ek legal wajah hai.

Yahan sabse zaroori shabd hai "kehti hai". Supreme Court ne kaha ki iske liye na FIR likhwana zaroori hai, na court mein rape saabit karna [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Wife ke liye yeh sabse zyada maayne rakhta hai. Woh pati ke khilaaf rape ki FIR likhwa hi nahi sakti, aur abortion law usse FIR maangta bhi nahi.

Clinic mein use bas doctor ko batana hai ki pregnancy zabardasti ke sex se hui hai. Pati ke signature nahi chahiye, kyunki MTP Act mein adult aurat ki apni consent hi kaafi hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Doctor pati ko bata bhi nahi sakta. 2021 se Section 5A ke tahat doctor aurat ka naam ya koi bhi detail kisi aise insaan ko nahi de sakta jise kanoon ne ijaazat na di ho. Aisa karne par ek saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Agar kisi clinic ko yeh faisla pata nahi hai, toh aurat ya uske saath aaya koi bhi insaan faisle ka naam bata sakta hai. Yeh jaankari general samajh ke liye hai, legal advice nahi.

## Crime data mein na dikhne wali hinsa

Shaadishuda auraton ke saath sexual violence kaun karta hai? Zyada tar maamlon mein pati. NFHS-5 (2019-21) survey mein 18 se 49 saal ki un auraton se baat hui jinki kabhi shaadi hui thi aur jinhone sexual violence jheli thi. Inmein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya, aur 14% ne pehle husband ka. 18 se 49 saal ki, kabhi bhi shaadishuda rahi sabhi auraton ko dekhein, toh 4.6% ne kaha ki mana karne ke baad bhi husband ne zabardasti sex kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Aisi baatein bahut kam bahar aati hain. Jin auraton ke saath physical ya sexual hinsa sirf current husband ne ki, unmein se sirf 11.3% ne kabhi madad maangi. Aur isi survey mein 15 se 49 saal ke 12.2% mardon ne kaha ki agar wife mana kare, toh husband ko zabardasti sex karne ka haq hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Police data yeh kami nahi bhar sakta, kyunki kanoon mein is hinsa ke liye koi jagah hi nahi hai. NCRB ne 2024 mein rape ke un cases ko gina jinmein accused jaan-pehchaan ka tha. Us ginti mein separated husbands ek hi column mein friends, online friends aur "on pretext of marriage" wale live-in partners ke saath rakhe gaye hain: kul 13,879 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo pati apni adult wife ke saath rehta hai, woh is ginti mein aa hi nahi sakta. Zabardasti pregnant hui zyada tar wives ke liye, Supreme Court ki is reading ke baad, MTP Act hi akela kanoon hai jo unke saath hui baat ko rape maanta hai, aur woh koi saboot bhi nahi maangta.

## Supreme Court mein pending case, aur isse kya badal sakta hai

Yeh exception BNS se purana hai: July 2024 tak yeh Indian Penal Code ke Section 375 ka Exception 2 tha. 9 September 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki aguvai wali teen judges ki bench ne ise challenge karne wale cases final hearing ke liye lagaye. Bench ne kaha ki woh do baatein tay karegi. Pehli, kya yeh exception sahi hai. Doosri, exception ke rehte kya pati par case chal sakta hai [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. 19 November 2026 tak koi faisla nahi aaya tha. Bench ne kaha ki woh winter break se pehle, 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko final hearing rakhegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Agar exception hatta hai, toh wife bhi baaki auraton ki tarah rape complaint kar sakegi, aur police data woh dikhana shuru kar sakta hai jo surveys saalon se dikha rahe hain. Agar exception bana rehta hai, toh bahut kuch doosre sawaal par tikega: jab tak court phir bhi case chalane ki ijaazat na de, wives ke paas yeh abortion wala raasta rahega, aur baaki har baat ke liye unhe cruelty aur domestic violence laws ka hi sahara lena hoga. Dono haalat mein 2022 ka faisla apni jagah rahega. Court ne saaf kaha tha ki uski yeh reading "solely for the purposes of the MTP Act" hai, yaani sirf MTP Act ke liye [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Is raaste ke liye December ka intezaar karne ki zaroorat nahi hai. Clinic ke bahar madad ke liye, July 2026 mein desh bhar mein 985 One Stop Centres chal rahe the; April 2015 se June 2026 ke beech inhone 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad ki [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

maternal-deaths-india-states-odisha-kera.en:
Picture two women pregnant in 2021-23, one in Kerala and one in Odisha. In Kerala, 30 women died of maternal causes for every 100,000 live births. In Odisha the figure was 153, the highest among India's major states [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. Same country, same three years, about five times the risk. India's national average hides that gap, and the newest bulletin shows it has not closed.

## The national number, and why it stalled

The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) counts women who die from pregnancy-related causes for every 100,000 live births. India's fell from 130 in 2014-16 to 88 in 2020-22, then stayed at 88 in 2021-23, with a 95% confidence range of 79 to 96 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. The bulletin published in May 2026 put 2022-24 at 87, with a range of 78 to 95 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. The two ranges almost coincide, so the one-point fall is within the margin of error. India is still above the Sustainable Development Goal target of below 70.

The national figure does not explain the plateau, but the state figures show where the ratios are highest. A national ratio is, in effect, all maternal deaths divided by all live births. States with high ratios pull it up, and it cannot fall far while they stand still, however well Kerala does.

## The state ladder: from 30 to 153

| State | 2021-23 | 2022-24 |
|---|---|---|
| Odisha | 153 | 124 |
| Chhattisgarh | 146 | 124 |
| Madhya Pradesh | 142 | 135 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 141 | 154 |
| Kerala | 30 | 24 |
| India | 88 | 87 |

The figures are maternal deaths per 100,000 live births [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]] [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. In 2021-23, Andhra Pradesh shared the lowest ratio with Kerala, at 30. In 2022-24, Tamil Nadu (25) sat just above Kerala (24) at the bottom.

Read the rows and one thing holds in both bulletins: the same four states occupy the top, at roughly five to six times the rate of the best performers. The tables do not say why. They count deaths, not what surrounds a pregnancy: how far away the nearest hospital that can manage an emergency is, how fast a woman can get there, and whether the care is good enough when she arrives.

## Lifetime risk: what 0.41% means

The MMR measures risk per birth. Lifetime risk adds up the danger across all of a woman's pregnancies: the chance that a girl entering her reproductive years will eventually die from a maternal cause. In 2021-23 it was 0.18% for India and 0.41% in both Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, more than double [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. In 2022-24, Uttar Pradesh's lifetime risk was 0.44% [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]].

Put 0.41% into a school. Picture the 1,000 girls of a large school in Lucknow or Bhopal. If the 2021-23 rates held through their lives, about four of them would die from a pregnancy-related cause. At the national rate, fewer than two would. These are not abstractions: each is a girl who could be sitting in that classroom now.

## Where unsafe abortion fits

Maternal deaths include women who die after an abortion. Nationally, the Health Ministry attributes about 8% of maternal deaths to unsafe abortion, using Registrar General cause-of-death data for 2001-03 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]], and UNFPA India calls it the third leading cause [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. The state ratios above count deaths, not their causes, so they cannot show abortion's share state by state.

The best clue is older. A study of 1.8 million pregnant women in nine poorer states covered by the Annual Health Survey found that 67% of abortions in 2007-2011 were unsafe, meaning done outside a health facility, without a skilled attendant, or at 20 weeks or later. The share ranged from 45.1% in Assam to 78.3% in Chhattisgarh [[bmjgh-yokoe-unsafe-abortion-2019]]. All four states at the top of the 2021-23 ladder were among those nine, and Chhattisgarh, second on the ladder, had the highest unsafe share.

That overlap is not proof that unsafe abortion explains their death rates. The study is more than a decade older than the ladder, it counted miscarriages along with induced abortions, and it predates both the wide use of abortion pills and the 2021 changes to the law. At most it raises a question the ladder cannot answer: whether the same gaps in care, too far, too late and too little trusted, shape both how women end pregnancies and whether they survive them.

## Reading state data with care

Three rules help. First, only major states get their own estimate in these bulletins; smaller states are pooled together [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]].

Second, state estimates are imprecise. In 2022-24, Chhattisgarh's 124 came with a 95% confidence range of 48 to 199, and Kerala's 24 with a range of 0 to 50 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. India's own range, 78 to 95, is far narrower, because a national estimate rests on a much larger sample.

Third, each bulletin pools three years, so consecutive bulletins share two of them, and ranks can still jump. Odisha's fall from 153 to 124, and Uttar Pradesh's rise from 141 to 154, both sit inside wide ranges. They are signals to watch, not verdicts.

What survives every caveat is the shape of the ladder. The same four states topped both bulletins, Kerala sat at the bottom of both, and in 2022-24 Uttar Pradesh's ratio was more than six times Kerala's [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. On that arithmetic, India is unlikely to get below 70 until the states at the top of the ladder move.
maternal-deaths-india-states-odisha-kera.hg:
