Do aurton ko socho jo 2021-23 mein pregnant thin, ek Kerala mein aur ek Odisha mein. Kerala mein har 100,000 live births par 30 aurton ki maternal causes se maut hui. Odisha mein yeh figure 153 tha, India ke major states mein sabse zyada [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. Ek hi desh, wahi teen saal, aur kareeb paanch guna khatra. India ka national average yeh gap chhupa leta hai, aur sabse naya bulletin dikhata hai ki yeh gap abhi band nahi hua.

## National number, aur woh atka kyun

Maternal mortality ratio (MMR) yeh ginta hai ki har 100,000 live births par kitni aurtein pregnancy se judi wajahon se marti hain. India ka MMR 2014-16 mein 130 se gir kar 2020-22 mein 88 par aaya, phir 2021-23 mein bhi 88 hi raha, 95% confidence range 79 se 96 ke saath [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. May 2026 mein chhape bulletin ne 2022-24 ke liye 87 bataya, range 78 se 95 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. Dono ranges lagbhag ek jaisi hain, isliye ek point ki giravat margin of error ke andar hai. India ab bhi Sustainable Development Goal ke 70 se neeche wale target se upar hai.

National figure yeh nahi batata ki giravat ruki kyun, lekin state figures dikhate hain ki ratio sabse zyada kahan hai. National ratio asal mein saari maternal deaths ko saare live births se bhaag dena hai. High ratio wale states ise upar kheenchte hain, aur jab tak woh wahin khade hain, yeh zyada neeche nahi aa sakta, Kerala chahe kitna bhi achha kare.

## State ladder: 30 se 153 tak

| State | 2021-23 | 2022-24 |
|---|---|---|
| Odisha | 153 | 124 |
| Chhattisgarh | 146 | 124 |
| Madhya Pradesh | 142 | 135 |
| Uttar Pradesh | 141 | 154 |
| Kerala | 30 | 24 |
| India | 88 | 87 |

Yeh figures har 100,000 live births par maternal deaths hain [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]] [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. 2021-23 mein Andhra Pradesh bhi Kerala ke saath 30 par sabse neeche tha. 2022-24 mein Tamil Nadu (25) sabse neeche wale Kerala (24) se theek upar tha.

Rows padho to dono bulletins mein ek baat nahi badalti: wahi chaar states top par hain, sabse achha karne walon se lagbhag paanch se chhe guna rate par. Tables yeh nahi batati ki aisa kyun hai. Woh mautein ginti hain, woh sab nahi jo pregnancy ke aas-paas hota hai: emergency sambhaal sakne wala sabse kareebi hospital kitni door hai, aurat wahan kitni jaldi pahunch sakti hai, aur pahunchne par ilaaj kaafi achha milta hai ya nahi.

## Lifetime risk: 0.41% ka matlab kya hai

MMR har birth par risk naapta hai. Lifetime risk ek aurat ki saari pregnancies ka khatra jod deta hai: yeh chance ki reproductive umar mein kadam rakhne wali ek ladki aage chal kar kisi maternal cause se maregi. 2021-23 mein yeh poore India ke liye 0.18% tha, aur Madhya Pradesh aur Uttar Pradesh dono mein 0.41%, yaani do guna se bhi zyada [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. 2022-24 mein Uttar Pradesh ka lifetime risk 0.44% tha [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]].

0.41% ko ek school mein rakh kar dekho. Lucknow ya Bhopal ke kisi bade school ki 1,000 ladkiyon ko socho. Agar 2021-23 ke rates unki poori zindagi bane rahein, to unmein se kareeb chaar kisi pregnancy se judi wajah se marengi. National rate par do se kam marengi. Yeh koi abstract number nahi hai: har ek woh ladki hai jo shayad abhi usi classroom mein baithi hai.

## Unsafe abortion kahan fit hota hai

Maternal deaths mein woh aurtein bhi shaamil hain jo abortion ke baad marti hain. National level par Health Ministry lagbhag 8% maternal deaths ko unsafe abortion se jodti hai, Registrar General ke 2001-03 ke cause-of-death data ke aadhaar par [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]], aur UNFPA India ise teesri sabse badi wajah kehta hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Upar diye state ratios mautein ginte hain, unki wajahein nahi, isliye woh state-wise abortion ka hissa nahi dikha sakte.

Sabse achha suraag purana hai. Annual Health Survey wale nau gareeb states mein 1.8 million pregnant aurton par hui ek study ne paaya ki 2007-2011 mein 67% abortions unsafe the, yaani health facility ke bahar hue, skilled attendant ke bina hue, ya 20 hafte ya uske baad hue. Yeh hissa Assam mein 45.1% se lekar Chhattisgarh mein 78.3% tak tha [[bmjgh-yokoe-unsafe-abortion-2019]]. 2021-23 ki ladder ke top ke chaaron states unhi nau mein the, aur ladder par doosre number wale Chhattisgarh mein unsafe hissa sabse zyada tha.

Yeh overlap is baat ka saboot nahi hai ki unsafe abortion hi un states ki maut ki daron ko samjhata hai. Study ladder se ek dashak se bhi zyada purani hai, usne induced abortions ke saath miscarriages bhi gine, aur woh abortion pills ke wide use aur 2021 ke law changes, dono se pehle ki hai. Zyada se zyada yeh ek aisa sawaal uthata hai jiska jawab ladder nahi de sakti: kya care ki wahi kamiyan, yaani bahut door, bahut der se aur bharose ke laayak nahi, dono baatein tay karti hain, ki aurtein pregnancy kaise khatam karti hain, aur pregnancy se zinda bach paati hain ya nahi.

## State data ko dhyaan se padhna

Teen rules kaam aate hain. Pehla, in bulletins mein sirf major states ka alag estimate milta hai; chhote states ko ek saath jod diya jaata hai [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]].

Doosra, state estimates sateek nahi hote. 2022-24 mein Chhattisgarh ke 124 ke saath 95% confidence range 48 se 199 tha, aur Kerala ke 24 ke saath 0 se 50 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. India ki apni range, 78 se 95, kahin zyada patli hai, kyunki national estimate kahin bade sample par tika hota hai.

Teesra, har bulletin teen saal ka data jodta hai, isliye lagatar do bulletins mein do saal common hote hain, aur phir bhi ranks uchhal sakti hain. Odisha ka 153 se 124 par girna, aur Uttar Pradesh ka 141 se 154 par chadhna, dono wide ranges ke andar hain. Yeh dhyaan rakhne wale signals hain, faisle nahi.

Har caveat ke baad jo bachta hai, woh ladder ki shakal hai. Dono bulletins mein wahi chaar states top par the, Kerala dono mein sabse neeche tha, aur 2022-24 mein Uttar Pradesh ka ratio Kerala ke chhe guna se bhi zyada tha [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. Is hisaab se India ka 70 se neeche pahunchna tab tak mushkil hai jab tak ladder ke top wale states aage nahi badhte.

medication-abortion-india-pill-revolutio.en:
The most common abortion in India involves no operating table, and often no doctor. It involves a strip of tablets. In 2015, an estimated 12.7 million of India's 15.6 million abortions, or 81%, were medication abortions; 2.2 million (14%) were surgical, and 0.8 million (5%) used other methods the researchers judged probably unsafe [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Nobody announced this change. It happened one chemist's counter at a time, while the law kept picturing a doctor and an approved clinic.

## From instruments to tablets

The pills are recent arrivals. Mifepristone was approved in India in 2002 and misoprostol in 2006, for ending pregnancies of up to seven weeks (49 days). In December 2008 the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation approved a combipack of the two for use up to nine weeks (63 days) [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2018]].

By 2015, seven years after that combipack, tablets were the main way Indian women ended pregnancies. The MTP Act was written in 1971, decades before any of these medicines were approved here, around a procedure performed by a registered doctor at an approved place [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The medicine changed faster than that picture did.

## The chemist counter as clinic

Most of these pills were never taken in a clinic. About 11.5 million abortions in 2015, 73% of the total, were medication abortions done outside health facilities, against 3.4 million (22%) inside them, 73% of those in private facilities [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Ready-made combipacks were used in 87% of the pill abortions outside facilities [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Women's own answers point the same way. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), two in three reported abortions used medicines. Among women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion, 26.2% had it at home and 26.9% said they performed it themselves, rising to 30.0% in rural areas; a doctor performed 54.8% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Consider a hypothetical. A 28-year-old schoolteacher in Nagpur, mother of two, finds her period is late. A clinic means half a day's leave and a waiting room full of people who know her. The chemist near the bus stand means five minutes. She chooses the five minutes. Whether it ends well depends on questions nobody at that counter asks: how many weeks since her last period, whether the pregnancy is in the uterus, and whether she knows which bleeding is normal and which is an emergency. The researchers behind the 2015 estimate noted that little is known about what information women get from chemists and informal vendors, or whether they take the pills correctly [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

## What the 2023 guidelines allow

The health system has already bent towards the pill. The Health Ministry's 2023 guidelines say the mifepristone-misoprostol combination is approved up to nine weeks, succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions, and can be prescribed by a qualified doctor at an outpatient clinic, provided that clinic has a referral link to an approved abortion facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. A woman does not need to be admitted anywhere. She needs a qualified prescriber and a safety net.

Outside that line, the law is blunt. Since 2002, an abortion by anyone who is not a registered medical practitioner, or at a place not approved under the Act, can bring two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, in force since 1 July 2024, still punishes causing a miscarriage outside the Act's protection with up to three years in prison (seven once she is "quick with child"), and it expressly includes a woman who causes her own [[gazette-bns-2023]]. The same tablets are lawful care when a registered doctor prescribes them within the Act, and fall outside its shelter when bought over the counter.

These sections are seldom used: police registered 15 cases under the MTP Act in 2024 [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. The law neither stops the pill market nor makes it safer. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Where it goes right, and where it goes wrong

When it goes right, a pill abortion is early, private and needs no instruments. The WHO puts deaths from safe abortion at under 1 per 100,000 abortions, against more than 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

The risks sit around the pill, not inside it. A doctor's check exists to catch a pregnancy past the nine-week limit [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]] or one growing outside the uterus, which needs urgent hospital care, not a kit [[nhs-ectopic]], and to tell a woman which symptoms mean hospital. Skip the check and those risks travel home with her. Across six states surveyed in 2015, 4-16% of women receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications such as infection, sepsis and shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. That is a share of women already in care, not of all abortions. In NFHS-5, 15.6% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion reported complications; 89.7% of them sought treatment, 70.6% of it in the private sector [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Even the best numbers here are a decade old or self-reported.

## Safer pills, not fewer

The tempting response is to treat the pill as the problem and squeeze its supply. That would not reduce the need for abortion. It risks pushing women towards the kind of "other methods" that made up 5% of abortions in 2015 and that researchers judged probably unsafe [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

The safer route uses the space the guidelines already open: more qualified doctors prescribing early, in ordinary outpatient clinics; chemists who send anyone asking for a kit to a registered doctor instead of handing it over in silence; plain-language information in every Indian language on how the weeks are counted and which warning signs mean hospital now; and post-abortion care that treats a bleeding woman as a patient, not a suspect.

For a reader, the lesson is simple. The pill is good medicine. What makes it safe is the check before it and the safety net after it, and both are a registered doctor's job.
medication-abortion-india-pill-revolutio.hg:
India mein sabse aam abortion mein na koi operation table hota hai, na aksar koi doctor. Hoti hai tablets ki ek strip. 2015 mein India ke lagbhag 15.6 million abortions mein se 12.7 million, yaani 81%, medication abortions the; 2.2 million (14%) surgical the, aur 0.8 million (5%) aise doosre tareekon se hue jinhe researchers ne shayad unsafe maana [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Kisi ne is badlav ka elaan nahi kiya. Yeh ek-ek chemist counter par hota gaya, jabki law ek doctor aur approved clinic ki tasveer hi dekhta raha.

## Instruments se tablets tak

Yeh pills naye hain. India mein mifepristone 2002 mein aur misoprostol 2006 mein approve hui, saat hafte (49 din) tak ki pregnancy khatam karne ke liye. December 2008 mein Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation ne dono ka ek combipack 9 hafte (63 din) tak ke use ke liye approve kiya [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2018]].

2015 tak, us combipack ke saat saal baad, tablets India mein pregnancy khatam karne ka sabse bada tareeka ban chuki thi. MTP Act 1971 mein likha gaya tha, in dawaiyon ke yahan approve hone se dashakon pehle, aur uski soch ek procedure ke aas-paas thi jo registered doctor kisi approved jagah par kare [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Dawa us tasveer se zyada tezi se badal gayi.

## Chemist ka counter hi clinic

Inmein se zyada tar pills kabhi kisi clinic mein li hi nahi gayi. 2015 mein lagbhag 11.5 million abortions, yaani kul ka 73%, health facilities ke bahar hue medication abortions the, jabki facilities ke andar sirf 3.4 million (22%) hue, aur unmein se bhi 73% private facilities mein [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Facilities ke bahar hue pill abortions mein se 87% mein ready-made combipack use hua [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Aurton ke apne jawab bhi yahi kehte hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein report hue har teen mein se do abortions dawaiyon se hue. Jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.2% ka abortion ghar par hua aur 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone yeh khud kiya; gaon mein yeh figure 30.0% tha. Doctor ne 54.8% abortions kiye [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Ek hypothetical lo. Nagpur ki ek 28 saal ki schoolteacher, do bachchon ki maa, dekhti hai ki uska period late hai. Clinic jaane ka matlab hai aadhe din ki chhutti aur ek waiting room jo jaan-pehchaan walon se bhara hai. Bus stand ke paas wala chemist matlab paanch minute. Woh paanch minute chunti hai. Sab theek hoga ya nahi, yeh un sawaalon par tika hai jo us counter par koi nahi poochta: last period ko kitne hafte hue, pregnancy uterus mein hai ya nahi, aur kya use pata hai ki kaunsi bleeding normal hai aur kaunsi emergency. 2015 ka estimate banane wale researchers ne bhi likha ki aurton ko chemists aur informal vendors se kya jaankari milti hai, ya woh pills sahi tareeke se leti hain ya nahi, iske baare mein bahut kam pata hai [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

## 2023 ki guidelines kya ijazat deti hain

Health system pehle hi pill ki taraf jhuk chuka hai. Health Ministry ki 2023 ki guidelines kehti hain ki mifepristone-misoprostol combination 9 hafte tak approved hai, shuruaati abortions mein 95-99% cases mein kaamyaab hota hai, aur ise ek qualified doctor outpatient clinic mein bhi likh sakta hai, bas us clinic ka kisi approved abortion facility se referral link hona chahiye [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Aurat ko kahin admit hone ki zaroorat nahi. Use chahiye ek qualified prescriber aur ek safety net.

Is line ke bahar law sakht hai. 2002 se, agar abortion koi aisa insaan kare jo registered medical practitioner nahi hai, ya Act ke tahat approved jagah ke bahar ho, toh 2 se 7 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 88, jo 1 July 2024 se lagu hai, Act ki protection ke bahar miscarriage karwane par aaj bhi 3 saal tak ki jail ki saza deta hai ("quick with child" hone par 7 saal tak), aur saaf likhta hai ki khud apna miscarriage karne wali aurat bhi ismein aati hai [[gazette-bns-2023]]. Wahi tablets registered doctor ke prescription par, Act ke andar, legal care hain, aur counter se bina prescription khareedne par Act ki chhatri se bahar ho jaati hain.

Yeh sections bahut kam use hote hain: 2024 mein police ne MTP Act ke tahat sirf 15 cases register kiye [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. Law na pill market ko rok pata hai, na use safe bana pata hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kahan sahi hota hai, aur kahan galat

Jab sab sahi hota hai, toh pill abortion jaldi hota hai, private hota hai aur ismein koi instrument nahi lagta. WHO ke mutabik safe abortion se maut 100,000 abortions mein 1 se bhi kam hoti hai, jabki jahan unsafe abortion aam hai, wahan yeh 100,000 mein 200 se zyada hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

Khatra pill ke andar nahi, uske aas-paas hai. Doctor ka check isliye hota hai ki 9 hafte ki limit se aage ki pregnancy pakdi ja sake [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]], ya uterus ke bahar badh rahi pregnancy, jiske liye kit nahi, turant hospital care chahiye [[nhs-ectopic]], aur aurat ko bataya ja sake ki kaunse symptoms ka matlab hai turant hospital. Check chhod do, toh yeh saare khatre uske saath ghar chale jaate hain. 2015 mein jin chhe states mein survey hua, wahan abortion ke baad care le rahi 4-16% aurton ka ilaaj infection, sepsis aur shock jaisi serious complications ke liye ho raha tha [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Yeh un aurton ka hissa hai jo pehle se care mein thi, saare abortions ka nahi. NFHS-5 mein jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications batayi; unmein se 89.7% ne ilaaj karwaya, aur ilaaj ka 70.6% hissa private sector mein hua [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yahan ke sabse achhe numbers bhi ya toh das saal purane hain ya aurton ke khud bataye hue.

## Kam pills nahi, zyada safe pills

Aasaan jawab lagta hai ki pill ko hi problem maan lo aur uski supply daba do. Isse abortion ki zaroorat kam nahi hogi. Ulta, aurtein un "doosre tareekon" ki taraf ja sakti hain jo 2015 mein 5% abortions mein use hue the aur jinhe researchers ne shayad unsafe maana [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

Zyada safe raasta wahi jagah use karta hai jo guidelines pehle se khol chuki hain: zyada qualified doctors jo jaldi, aam outpatient clinics mein prescription dein; aise chemists jo kit maangne wale ko chupchaap kit thamaane ke bajaye registered doctor ke paas bhejein; har Indian language mein seedhi-saadi jaankari ki hafte kaise gine jaate hain aur kaunse warning signs ka matlab hai turant hospital; aur abortion ke baad aisi care jo bleeding wali aurat ko patient samjhe, suspect nahi.

Padhne wale ke liye seekh simple hai. Pill achhi dawa hai. Use safe banata hai pehle ka check aur baad ka safety net, aur dono ek registered doctor ka kaam hain.

missing-girls-india-sex-selection-number.en:
The 45.8 million women and girls in UNFPA's count for India will not be found on any list. They are a gap: the difference between the population India has and the one it would have had if girls were as welcome as boys, before birth and after it. UNFPA measured that gap for 2020 [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. The other numbers in this debate measure different parts of the same gap, and confusion starts when they are treated as one.

## What 'missing' means

Nature sets the baseline: without interference, about 105 boys are born for every 100 girls [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. When many more boys than that are born, year after year, the shortfall of girls is counted as "missing".

UNFPA's count has two parts. Girls go missing before birth through gender-biased sex selection, which in practice means sex-selective abortion. They also go missing after birth, through excess deaths of girls, which UNFPA traces to what it calls postnatal sex selection [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. For India, one analysis cited by UNFPA found that sex selection accounts for about two thirds of the missing girls, and deaths after birth for about one third [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

The second part is easy to forget. A girl who survives birth can still end up in this count if, when she falls ill, she is taken to a doctor later than her brother would be, or not at all.

## 45.8 million: the stock

The 45.8 million is a stock, a total built up over about 50 years: girls never born, and girls and women who died because they were female [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. It is not the number lost in 2020, and it cannot be set against a single year's births.

India's 45.8 million is part of 142.6 million "missing" females worldwide. Only China's figure, 72.3 million, is larger [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Between them, the two countries hold most of the world's total.

A stock tells you how deep the hole is. It does not tell you whether the hole is still being dug. For that you need the flow.

## 9 million in 20 years: the flow

Pew Research Center estimated in 2022 that at least 9.0 million female births went missing in India between 2000 and 2019 because of female-selective abortions [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. That counts only the before-birth part, over 20 years.

The yearly flow is shrinking. Pew's estimate of girls missing at birth each year fell from about 480,000 in 2010 to 410,000 in 2019 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. UNFPA's estimate for 2013-2017 was about 460,000 a year [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. The sex ratio at birth moved the same way: about 111 boys per 100 girls in the 2011 census, about 109 in NFHS-4 (2015-16) and 108 in NFHS-5 (2019-21) [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

Slower is not stopped. At 108 against a natural 105, every estimate here still puts the yearly loss in the hundreds of thousands. Revealing a foetus's sex has been illegal since 1996 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]; our investigation of the PC-PNDT Act looks at why its enforcement is so hard to see.

## India and China: 90-95% of the world's gap

Sex selection at birth is concentrated in very few places. UNFPA estimates that 1.2 million to 1.5 million female births go missing worldwide every year because of gender-biased sex selection, and that China and India together account for about 90-95% of them [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Many societies prefer sons, but only a few turn that preference into missing girls on this scale. In India the preference runs deep. In a 2014 survey in seven Indian states, 81% of women and 76% of men said it was very important to have at least one son [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Consider a hypothetical couple who want two children at most, and whose families insist that one must be a son. If the first child is a girl, the second pregnancy carries all the pressure. That is the moment a scan, and a clinic willing to hint, turns a preference into a number in this story.

## Why the estimates differ

If you have seen 460,000, 410,000, 9 million and 45.8 million quoted for the same problem, they are not contradicting each other. They answer different questions, about different years.

| Number | What it counts | Period | Estimated by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45.8 million | Missing females in India, before and after birth | Built up to 2020 | UNFPA |
| 9.0 million | Missing female births in India | 2000-2019 | Pew |
| 460,000 a year | Missing female births in India | 2013-2017 average | UNFPA |
| 410,000 a year | Missing female births in India | 2019 | Pew |
| 1.2-1.5 million a year | Missing female births worldwide | Annual estimate | UNFPA |

Two more things move the answer. The first is the data. Pew's estimate rests on National Family Health Survey data, which show less skewed birth ratios than the official Sample Registration System, so its figures are smaller than some other scholars' [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. NFHS-5 put the sex ratio at birth at 929 girls per 1,000 boys for children born in the five years before its 2019-21 survey [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]; the Sample Registration System recorded 913 for 2019-21 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]], and 918 for 2022-24, its latest figure [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Build an estimate on the first source and you will find fewer missing girls than on the second. The two series should never be joined into one trend.

The second is the model. Every estimate compares what happened with what would have happened without discrimination. That baseline is itself an estimate, and small changes to it shift the totals.

The honest summary: the hole is tens of millions deep, the digging has slowed, and it has not stopped. When you share any of these numbers, share its year and its definition with it.
missing-girls-india-sex-selection-number.hg:
UNFPA ki India wali ginti ki 45.8 million aurtein aur ladkiyan kisi list mein nahi milengi. Woh ek gap hain: us population ke beech ka farak jo India ke paas hai, aur jo hoti agar ladkiyon ka bhi ladkon jitna swagat hota, janm se pehle bhi aur janm ke baad bhi. UNFPA ne yeh gap 2020 ke liye naapa [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Is bahas ke baaki numbers isi gap ke alag-alag hisse naapte hain, aur confusion tab shuru hota hai jab unhe ek hi cheez samajh liya jaata hai.

## 'Missing' ka matlab kya hai

Baseline nature tay karti hai: bina kisi dakhal ke, har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 105 ladke paida hote hain [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. Jab saal dar saal isse kahin zyada ladke paida hote hain, toh ladkiyon ki kami ko "missing" gina jaata hai.

UNFPA ki ginti ke do hisse hain. Ladkiyan janm se pehle missing hoti hain, gender-biased sex selection se, jiska practical matlab hai sex-selective abortion. Aur woh janm ke baad bhi missing hoti hain, ladkiyon ki un zyada mauton se, jinki jad UNFPA us cheez mein dekhta hai jise woh postnatal sex selection kehta hai [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. India ke liye, UNFPA ke quote kiye ek analysis ke mutabik missing ladkiyon mein se lagbhag do-tihaai sex selection ki wajah se hain, aur lagbhag ek-tihaai janm ke baad ki mauton ki wajah se [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Doosra hissa aasani se bhool jaata hai. Jo ladki janm le leti hai, woh bhi is ginti mein aa sakti hai, agar beemar padne par use doctor ke paas apne bhai se der se le jaaya jaaye, ya le jaaya hi na jaaye.

## 45.8 million: stock

45.8 million ek stock hai, yaani lagbhag 50 saal mein jama hua total: woh ladkiyan jo kabhi paida nahi hui, aur woh ladkiyan aur aurtein jinki maut isliye hui kyunki woh female thi [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Yeh 2020 mein khoyi ladkiyon ki ginti nahi hai, aur ise kisi ek saal ki births ke saamne nahi rakha ja sakta.

India ke 45.8 million, duniya bhar ki 142.6 million "missing" females ka hissa hain. Sirf China ka figure, 72.3 million, isse bada hai [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Dono desh milkar duniya ke total ka zyada tar hissa rakhte hain.

Stock batata hai ki gaddha kitna gehra hai. Yeh nahi batata ki gaddha abhi bhi khoda ja raha hai ya nahi. Uske liye flow dekhna padta hai.

## 20 saal mein 9 million: flow

Pew Research Center ne 2022 mein estimate kiya ki 2000 se 2019 ke beech India mein female-selective abortions ki wajah se kam se kam 9.0 million female births missing hui [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. Yeh sirf janm se pehle wala hissa ginta hai, 20 saal ka.

Saalana flow kam ho raha hai. Pew ke estimate mein har saal janm ke waqt missing hone wali ladkiyan 2010 mein lagbhag 480,000 se ghat kar 2019 mein 410,000 ho gayi [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. UNFPA ka 2013-2017 ka estimate lagbhag 460,000 saalana tha [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Sex ratio at birth bhi isi taraf badla: 2011 ki census mein har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 111 ladke, NFHS-4 (2015-16) mein lagbhag 109, aur NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 108 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

Dheema hona rukna nahi hai. Natural 105 ke saamne 108 par, yahan ka har estimate saalana nuksaan ko ab bhi laakhon mein rakhta hai. Foetus ka sex batana 1996 se illegal hai [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]; PC-PNDT Act par hamari investigation dekhti hai ki iska enforcement itna kam nazar kyun aata hai.

## India aur China: duniya ke gap ka 90-95%

Janm ke waqt sex selection bahut kam jagahon par simta hua hai. UNFPA ka estimate hai ki duniya mein har saal gender-biased sex selection ki wajah se 1.2 million se 1.5 million female births missing hoti hain, aur inmein se lagbhag 90-95% China aur India mein milkar hoti hain [[unfpa-swop-2020]].

Kai samaaj bete chahte hain, lekin sirf kuch hi samaaj is chahat ko itne bade paimaane par missing ladkiyon mein badalte hain. India mein yeh chahat gehri hai. 2014 mein saat Indian states ke ek survey mein 81% aurton aur 76% mardon ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Ek hypothetical couple socho jo zyada se zyada do bacche chahta hai, aur jiski families zid karti hain ki ek beta toh hona hi chahiye. Agar pehla baccha ladki hai, toh doosri pregnancy par saara dabaav aa jaata hai. Yahi woh pal hai jab ek scan, aur ishaara karne ko taiyaar ek clinic, ek chahat ko is story ke ek number mein badal deta hai.

## Estimates alag kyun hote hain

Agar tumne ek hi problem ke liye 460,000, 410,000, 9 million aur 45.8 million quote hote dekhe hain, toh yeh ek doosre ko kaat nahi rahe. Yeh alag sawaalon ke jawab hain, alag saalon ke.

| Number | Kya ginta hai | Period | Kisne estimate kiya |
|---|---|---|---|
| 45.8 million | India mein missing females, janm se pehle aur baad | 2020 tak jama hua | UNFPA |
| 9.0 million | India mein missing female births | 2000-2019 | Pew |
| 460,000 a year | India mein missing female births | 2013-2017 ka average | UNFPA |
| 410,000 a year | India mein missing female births | 2019 | Pew |
| 1.2-1.5 million a year | Duniya bhar mein missing female births | Saalana estimate | UNFPA |

Do aur cheezein jawab badal deti hain. Pehli hai data. Pew ka estimate National Family Health Survey ke data par tika hai, jo official Sample Registration System ke muqable kam skewed birth ratios dikhata hai, isliye Pew ke figures kuch doosre scholars se chhote hain [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. NFHS-5 ne 2019-21 ke survey se pehle ke paanch saalon mein paida hue bacchon ka sex ratio at birth har 1,000 ladkon par 929 ladkiyan bataya [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]]; Sample Registration System ne 2019-21 ke liye 913 record kiya [[srs-statistical-report-2023]], aur apne sabse naye figure mein 2022-24 ke liye 918 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Pehle source par estimate banao toh doosre ke muqable kam missing ladkiyan milengi. In dono series ko kabhi ek trend mein mat jodo.

Doosri cheez hai model. Har estimate yeh compare karta hai ki kya hua, aur discrimination na hota toh kya hota. Woh baseline khud ek estimate hai, aur usmein chhote badlav bhi totals ko khiska dete hain.

Imaandaar summary yeh hai: gaddha croron mein gehra hai, khudai dheemi hui hai, aur ruki nahi hai. Jab bhi inmein se koi number share karo, uske saath uska saal aur uski definition bhi share karo.

most-dangerous-abortions-india-unsafe-me.en:
The story India now tells about abortion is a story about pills. Of an estimated 15.6 million abortions in 2015, 12.7 million (81%) were medication abortions and 2.2 million (14%) were surgical [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. That leaves 0.8 million (5%) that were neither, done by other methods the researchers judged probably unsafe. This investigation is about those abortions: who still has them, what the law does, and what would end them. It does not describe the methods; the danger is the point, not the detail.

## 5%: the abortions pills did not replace

Five per cent sounds small. It is one abortion in twenty, and in 2015 it meant 0.8 million women [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. It remains the latest national estimate, so nobody can show whether the number has fallen.

Globally, the WHO says about 45% of all induced abortions are unsafe. A third of those happen in the least safe conditions, by untrained people using dangerous and invasive methods, and more than half of all unsafe abortions occur in Asia, mostly in south and central Asia [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. The Indian study did not sort its 0.8 million into WHO's tiers, so how many of them fall into that bottom tier is unknown.

## What 'probably unsafe' means

In the study, by the Guttmacher Institute, IIPS Mumbai and the Population Council, "other methods" meant anything that was neither medication nor surgery. "Probably" is an honest word, because nobody watches these abortions happen. What reaches hospitals is clearer.

In six states surveyed in 2015 (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh), 4-16% of patients receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications such as infection of the uterus, perforation, sepsis and shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Women who never reached a hospital are not in that figure.

The deaths are estimated, not counted. UNFPA India reported in 2022 that unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths in India, that close to eight women die each day from causes related to it, and that women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from its complications [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. The Health Ministry's own figure, about 8% of maternal deaths, still rests on cause-of-death data from 2001-03 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. A system that quotes numbers more than twenty years old is not watching closely.

The WHO puts the stakes plainly: deaths from safe abortion are negligible, under 1 per 100,000 abortions, but exceed 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

## Who ends up with untrained providers

No survey asks whether a woman's provider was trained. But the law and the data leave clear openings.

The minor. Every pregnancy in a girl under 18 must be reported to the police under POCSO. In 2022 the Supreme Court itself observed that this leaves a pregnant minor and her guardian two choices: a registered doctor and possible criminal proceedings, or an unqualified provider [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. UNFPA's finding that teenagers face the highest risk of dying sits uncomfortably close to that warning.

The woman far from a clinic. In nine poorer states covered by India's Annual Health Survey, 67% of abortions reported for 2007-2011 were classified as unsafe, from 45.1% in Assam to 78.3% in Chhattisgarh [[bmjgh-yokoe-unsafe-abortion-2019]]. "Unsafe" there meant outside a health facility, without a skilled attendant, or at 20 weeks or later; the count includes miscarriages, and the data predate the spread of pills. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 26.2% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion had it at home, and 26.9% said they ended it themselves, 30.0% in rural areas [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Home and self-managed do not mean unsafe, but they are beyond anyone's sight.

The wife whose family decides. In NFHS-5, 4.1% of women said the main reason for their abortion was that their husband or mother-in-law did not want the pregnancy [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey does not say where those abortions happened. When someone else makes the decision, she may not get to choose where, or by whom, it is done.

## What the law threatens, and whom it reaches

On paper, the law is severe. Since 2002, an abortion by anyone who is not a registered medical practitioner, or at a place not approved under the MTP Act, is punishable with two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, in force since 1 July 2024, punishes anyone who causes a miscarriage outside the MTP Act, and expressly includes a woman who causes her own [[gazette-bns-2023]].

In practice, it barely moves. Police across India registered 15 cases under the MTP Act in 2024, after 32 in 2022 and 30 in 2023 [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. The 0.8 million estimate is for 2015, so the years differ, but the scale does not: the threat almost never reaches the untrained provider.

What it does reach is fear. A law that names the woman herself, and a reporting rule that the Supreme Court says pushes girls towards unqualified providers, give those most at risk a reason to hide from doctors as well as police. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Bringing every woman to safe care

The tools already exist in Indian law. Up to nine weeks, a qualified doctor can prescribe abortion pills, which succeed in 95-99% of early abortions, at an ordinary outpatient clinic linked to an approved facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Since 2021, a doctor who reveals the name of a woman who had an abortion, except to someone authorised by law, faces up to a year in prison [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Since 2022, a doctor reporting a minor's pregnancy to the police need not give her name or details if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

What is missing is reach: trained, approved providers close to where women live; accurate information about pills, so the choice is never between a chemist's guess and an untrained hand; and post-abortion care where no one is shamed for what happened before she arrived.

Behind each of the 0.8 million is a moment when a registered doctor seemed more dangerous, or further away, than someone without training. Changing that moment is the work.
most-dangerous-abortions-india-unsafe-me.hg:
India mein abortion ki ab jo kahani sunai jaati hai, woh pills ki kahani hai. 2015 mein andaazan 15.6 million abortions mein se 12.7 million (81%) medication abortions the aur 2.2 million (14%) surgical [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Bache 0.8 million (5%), jo na pills se hue na surgery se, balki aise doosre methods se jinhe researchers ne "probably unsafe", yaani shayad unsafe, maana. Yeh investigation unhi abortions ke baare mein hai: aaj bhi kaun inse guzarta hai, law kya karta hai, aur inhe khatam kya karega. Ismein methods describe nahi kiye gaye; baat khatre ki hai, detail ki nahi.

## 5%: woh abortions jinhe pills replace nahi kar payi

Paanch percent chhota lagta hai. Yeh har bees mein se ek abortion hai, aur 2015 mein iska matlab tha 0.8 million aurtein [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Yahi aaj bhi sabse latest national estimate hai, isliye koi data se nahi dikha sakta ki yeh number kam hua ya nahi.

Duniya bhar mein WHO kehta hai ki lagbhag 45% induced abortions unsafe hote hain. Inmein se ek-tihaai sabse unsafe halaat mein hote hain, untrained logon ke haathon, khatarnak aur invasive methods se, aur saare unsafe abortions mein se aadhe se zyada Asia mein hote hain, zyada tar south aur central Asia mein [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. India wali study ne apne 0.8 million ko WHO ke tiers mein nahi baanta, isliye inmein se kitne us sabse neeche wale tier mein aate hain, yeh pata nahi.

## 'Shayad unsafe' ka matlab kya hai

Guttmacher Institute, IIPS Mumbai aur Population Council ki is study mein "other methods" ka matlab tha har woh tareeka jo na medication tha na surgery. "Probably" ek imaandaar shabd hai, kyunki in abortions ko hote hue koi nahi dekhta. Jo hospital tak pahunchta hai, woh zyada saaf dikhta hai.

2015 mein survey kiye gaye chhe states (Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu aur Uttar Pradesh) mein post-abortion care paane wale 4-16% patients ka serious complications ke liye ilaaj chal raha tha, jaise uterus ka infection, perforation, sepsis aur shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Jo aurtein kabhi hospital tak pahunchi hi nahi, woh is figure mein nahi hain.

Maut ke numbers andaaze hain, ginti nahi. UNFPA India ne 2022 mein bataya ki unsafe abortion India mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah hai, ki isse jude kaaranon se har din lagbhag aath aurtein marti hain, aur ki 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko iske complications se marne ka sabse zyada risk hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Health Ministry ka apna figure, ki lagbhag 8% maternal deaths iski wajah se hoti hain, aaj bhi 2001-03 ke cause-of-death data par tika hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Jo system bees saal se zyada purane numbers quote karta ho, woh dhyaan se nahi dekh raha.

WHO saaf batata hai ki kya daav par hai: safe abortion se maut na ke barabar hai, har 100,000 abortions par 1 se kam, lekin jahan unsafe abortion aam hai wahan yeh 200 per 100,000 se zyada ho jaati hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

## Untrained providers tak kaun pahunchta hai

Koi survey yeh nahi poochta ki aurat ka provider trained tha ya nahi. Lekin law aur data kuch saaf raaste dikhate hain.

Minor ladki. POCSO ke under 18 se kam umar ki ladki ki har pregnancy police ko report karni padti hai. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne khud kaha ki isse pregnant minor aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi raaste bachte hain: registered doctor ke paas jaayein aur criminal proceedings ka risk lein, ya kisi unqualified provider ke paas jaayein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. UNFPA ki yeh finding ki teenagers ko marne ka sabse zyada risk hai, is chetavani ke bahut kareeb baithti hai.

Clinic se door rehne wali aurat. India ke Annual Health Survey mein shaamil nau gareeb states mein 2007-2011 ke reported abortions mein se 67% unsafe classify hue, Assam mein 45.1% se lekar Chhattisgarh mein 78.3% tak [[bmjgh-yokoe-unsafe-abortion-2019]]. Wahan "unsafe" ka matlab tha health facility ke bahar, bina skilled attendant ke, ya 20 hafte ya uske baad; is ginti mein miscarriages bhi shaamil hain, aur yeh data pills ke failne se pehle ka hai. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin aurton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.2% ka abortion ghar par hua, aur 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone khud kiya, gaon mein 30.0% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ghar par ya khud karne ka matlab unsafe nahi hai, lekin yeh kisi ki nazar mein nahi aata.

Woh biwi jiske liye family faisla karti hai. NFHS-5 mein 4.1% aurton ne kaha ki abortion ki main wajah yeh thi ki unke pati ya saas yeh pregnancy nahi chahte the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey nahi batata ki woh abortions kahan hue. Jab faisla koi aur leta hai, toh ho sakta hai use yeh chunne ka mauka bhi na mile ki abortion kahan, aur kiske haathon ho.

## Law kya dhamki deta hai, aur kis tak pahunchta hai

Kagaz par law sakht hai. 2002 se, agar abortion koi aisa insaan kare jo registered medical practitioner nahi hai, ya MTP Act ke under approved na ki gayi jagah par ho, toh do se saat saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ka Section 88, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hai, MTP Act ke bahar miscarriage karwane wale har insaan ko saza deta hai, aur saaf taur par us aurat ko bhi shaamil karta hai jo khud apna miscarriage karwaye [[gazette-bns-2023]].

Asal mein law mushkil se hilta hai. Poore India mein police ne 2024 mein MTP Act ke under sirf 15 cases darj kiye, 2022 mein 32 aur 2023 mein 30 ke baad [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. 0.8 million wala estimate 2015 ka hai, isliye saal alag hain, lekin scale nahi badalta: yeh dhamki untrained provider tak shayad hi kabhi pahunchti hai.

Jis tak yeh pahunchti hai, woh hai darr. Ek law jo khud aurat ka naam leta hai, aur ek reporting rule jiske baare mein Supreme Court kehta hai ki woh ladkiyon ko unqualified providers ki taraf dhakelta hai, sabse zyada risk wale logon ko police ke saath-saath doctors se bhi chhupne ki wajah dete hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Har aurat ko safe care tak laana

Indian law mein auzaar pehle se maujood hain. Nau hafte tak ek qualified doctor abortion pills prescribe kar sakta hai, jo shuruaati abortions mein 95-99% cases mein kaamyaab hoti hain, kisi aam outpatient clinic se jo approved facility se juda ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. 2021 se, jo doctor abortion karwane wali aurat ka naam kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne authorise nahi kiya, use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2022 se, minor ki pregnancy police ko report karne wale doctor ko uska naam ya details dene ki zaroorat nahi, agar woh aur uska guardian aisa kahein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Kami pahunch ki hai: aurton ke ghar ke paas trained, approved providers; pills ke baare mein sahi jaankari, taaki choice kabhi chemist ke andaaze aur untrained haath ke beech na ho; aur aisi post-abortion care jahan pahunchne se pehle jo hua uske liye kisi ko sharminda na kiya jaaye.

In 0.8 million mein se har ek ke peechhe ek pal hai jab registered doctor kisi untrained insaan se zyada khatarnak, ya zyada door, laga. Us pal ko badalna hi asli kaam hai.

mtp-act-plain-words-weeks-doctors.en:
Ask whether abortion is legal in India and you will hear yes, no, or "only if you are married". The real answer is in the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, and it is not one right but a row of gates. Each covers a stretch of weeks, with its own number of doctors who must agree and its own list of reasons they may accept. Miss one deadline and the next gate is narrower. Here is the law since the 2021 amendment, in plain words: general information, not legal advice.

## Up to 20 weeks: one doctor's opinion

For the first 20 weeks, one registered medical practitioner can end a pregnancy, but only if that doctor forms the opinion, in good faith, that continuing it would risk the woman's life or gravely injure her physical or mental health, or that there is a substantial risk of a serious foetal abnormality [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

That sounds narrow, but two presumptions widen it. If a woman says the pregnancy was caused by rape, the anguish is presumed to be a grave injury to her mental health. A doctor may presume the same when a contraceptive used by "any woman or her partner" fails, words that since 2021 cover unmarried women too [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Weeks count from the first day of the last period, not from the day of sex, so a pregnancy is further along than the date of sex suggests. Early on, pills are an option: India's 2023 abortion-care guidelines say the mifepristone-misoprostol combination is approved up to nine weeks (63 days), can be prescribed by a qualified doctor, and succeeds in 95-99% of early abortions [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

An abortion must be done by a registered medical practitioner at a government hospital or an approved place; a District Level Committee approves private clinics. Anyone else, or anyone working from an unapproved place, risks two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

## 20 to 24 weeks: two doctors, seven categories

After week 20 the gate narrows twice. At least two registered doctors must agree, and the woman must belong to a category listed in the rules [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Rule 3B, notified on 12 October 2021, names seven [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]:

- survivors of sexual assault, rape or incest;
- minors;
- women whose marital status changes during the pregnancy, through widowhood or divorce;
- women with major physical disabilities;
- mentally ill women;
- cases of serious foetal malformation;
- women in humanitarian, disaster or emergency settings.

On paper, that list leaves out a single woman whose partner walks out at week 21. On 29 September 2022 the Supreme Court closed the gap: shutting out unmarried and single women would violate the right to equality in Article 14, so they get the same access as married women. It also held that "rape" in the Act includes marital rape, and that no FIR or court finding is needed to rely on it [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## After 24 weeks: Medical Boards, foetal abnormality only

Past 24 weeks there is no upper limit, but only for one reason: a substantial foetal abnormality diagnosed by a Medical Board. Every state and union territory must set up such a board, with at least a gynaecologist, a paediatrician and a radiologist or sonologist [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. The rules give the board three days to give its opinion; if it says yes, the abortion must be done within five days of the request [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

Now imagine a 15-year-old who was raped and does not realise she is pregnant until week 26. Hers is not a foetal-abnormality case, so the Act has no gate for her. The one exception at any stage is an emergency, when ending the pregnancy is immediately necessary to save her life. Otherwise her family must petition a High Court or the Supreme Court and wait for judges to decide [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

## Consent and confidentiality: the rules families get wrong

The first mistake is about whose signature counts. If the woman is 18 or older, her own consent is the only one the law asks for. A guardian's written consent is needed only if she is under 18 or mentally ill, and the Act nowhere asks for a husband's consent [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Some families decide anyway. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 4.1% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion said the main reason was that the husband or mother-in-law did not want it [[nfhs5-india-2021]]; our data story on who else is deciding follows that thread. Between a woman and her family, the law sides with her both ways: no one can end her pregnancy without her consent, and if she is an adult, no relative's signature can stop her.

The second mistake is assuming the doctor will tell. Since 2021, Section 5A bars a doctor from revealing the name or details of a woman whose pregnancy was ended, except to someone authorised by law, on pain of up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

One honest limit: with a girl under 18, the doctor must inform the police under POCSO, because any sexual activity below 18 is an offence. In 2022 the Supreme Court said the doctor need not give her name or personal details in that report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## What the law still does not give you

For all its gates, the MTP Act has never given Indian women abortion on request. At every stage a doctor's opinion opens the gate, not her own decision, as our myth-check on that rule explains. The Act is less a woman's right than a list of conditions under which a doctor may act.

Most abortions never reach a health facility at all: of an estimated 15.6 million in India in 2015, 11.5 million (73%) were medication abortions done outside any health facility [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

After week 24 the law leaves a hole for exactly the women the 2021 rewrite was meant to help: rape survivors and girls who find out late. Until Parliament closes it, their way out still runs through a lawyer and a courtroom.
mtp-act-plain-words-weeks-doctors.hg:
Kisi se bhi poochho ki India mein abortion legal hai ya nahi, toh jawab milega haan, nahi, ya "sirf shaadishuda auraton ke liye". Asli jawab Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act mein hai, aur woh ek seedha right nahi, balki gates ki ek line hai. Har gate hafton ke ek daayre ko cover karta hai, aur har gate par tay hai ki kitne doctors ko agree karna hoga aur kaun si wajah maani jayegi. Ek deadline miss hui, toh agla gate aur tang ho jata hai. Neeche 2021 ke amendment ke baad ka law hai, simple words mein. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 20 hafte tak: ek doctor ki opinion

Pehle 20 hafte tak ek registered medical practitioner pregnancy end kar sakta hai, lekin tabhi jab woh doctor good faith mein yeh opinion banaye ki pregnancy continue karne se woman ki jaan ko risk hai, ya uski physical ya mental health ko serious nuksaan hoga, ya phir foetus mein serious abnormality ka bada risk hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Sunne mein yeh strict lagta hai, lekin law do baatein pehle se maan leta hai jo is gate ko chauda kar deti hain. Agar woman kehti hai ki pregnancy rape se hui, toh maana jata hai ki is anguish se uski mental health ko grave injury ho rahi hai. Doctor yahi baat tab bhi maan sakta hai jab "any woman or her partner" ka contraceptive fail ho jaye, aur 2021 se in words mein unmarried women bhi aati hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Hafte last period ke pehle din se gine jaate hain, sex wale din se nahi, isliye pregnancy usse zyada aage hoti hai jitna sex ki date se lagta hai. Shuru ke hafton mein pills ek option hain: India ki 2023 abortion-care guidelines kehti hain ki mifepristone-misoprostol combination 9 hafte (63 din) tak approved hai, qualified doctor ise prescribe kar sakta hai, aur early abortions mein yeh 95-99% cases mein kaamyaab hota hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]].

Abortion registered medical practitioner hi karega, sarkari hospital ya approved jagah par; private clinics ko approval ek District Level Committee deti hai. Koi aur abortion kare, ya koi bina approval wali jagah par kare, toh 2 se 7 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

## 20 se 24 hafte: do doctors, saat categories

Week 20 ke baad gate do tarah se tang hota hai. Kam se kam do registered doctors ko agree karna hoga, aur woman ko rules mein likhi kisi category mein aana hoga [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 12 October 2021 ko notify hue Rule 3B mein saat categories hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]:

- sexual assault, rape ya incest ki survivors;
- minors;
- woh women jinka marital status pregnancy ke dauraan badal jaye, yaani pati ki maut ho jaye ya divorce ho jaye;
- major physical disabilities wali women;
- mentally ill women;
- foetus mein serious malformation ke cases;
- humanitarian crisis, disaster ya emergency wale halaat mein phansi women.

Kagaz par yeh list us single woman ko chhod deti hai jiska partner week 21 mein use chhod kar chala jaye. 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court ne yeh gap band kar diya: unmarried aur single women ko bahar rakhna Article 14, yaani equality ke right, ke khilaaf hai, isliye unhe bhi married women jaisa hi access milega. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki is Act mein "rape" mein marital rape bhi aata hai, aur iske liye FIR ya court ka faisla zaroori nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## 24 hafte ke baad: Medical Board, sirf foetal abnormality

24 hafte ke baad koi upper limit nahi hai, lekin sirf ek wajah ke liye: jab Medical Board foetus mein substantial abnormality diagnose kare. Har state aur union territory ko aisa board banana hai, jismein kam se kam ek gynaecologist, ek paediatrician aur ek radiologist ya sonologist ho [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Rules ke hisaab se board ko 3 din mein apni opinion deni hai, aur haan kehne par request ke 5 din ke andar abortion ho jaana chahiye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]].

Ab socho, ek 15 saal ki ladki ke saath rape hua aur use week 26 mein jaakar pata chalta hai ki woh pregnant hai. Uska case foetal abnormality ka nahi hai, isliye Act mein uske liye koi gate nahi. Kisi bhi stage par bas ek exception hai, emergency: jab uski jaan bachane ke liye pregnancy turant end karna zaroori ho. Warna uski family ko High Court ya Supreme Court mein petition daalni hogi aur judges ke faisle ka intezaar karna hoga [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

## Consent aur confidentiality: woh rules jin par families galat hoti hain

Pehli galti yeh hai ki signature kiska chahiye. Agar woman 18 ya usse badi hai, toh law sirf uski apni consent maangta hai. Guardian ki written consent tabhi chahiye jab woh 18 se kam ho ya mentally ill ho, aur Act mein pati ki consent ka zikr kahin nahi hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

Phir bhi kuch families decision khud le leti hain. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin women ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 4.1% ne kaha ki main wajah yeh thi ki pati ya saas yeh pregnancy nahi chahte the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]; ghar mein aur kaun decide kar raha hai, is par hamari data story yahi thread aage follow karti hai. Woman aur uski family ke beech, law dono taraf se woman ka saath deta hai: uski consent ke bina koi uski pregnancy end nahi kara sakta, aur agar woh adult hai, toh kisi rishtedaar ka signature use rok nahi sakta.

Doosri galti yeh sochna hai ki doctor ghar walon ko bata dega. 2021 se Section 5A doctor ko us woman ka naam ya details batane se rokta hai jiska abortion hua, siwaye us insaan ke jise law authorise karta hai; rule todne par 1 saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

Ek limit imaandari se batana zaroori hai: agar ladki 18 se kam hai, toh POCSO ke under doctor ko police ko inform karna hi hoga, kyunki 18 se kam umar mein koi bhi sexual activity offence hai. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki agar ladki aur uske guardian kahein, toh doctor ko us report mein uska naam ya personal details dene ki zaroorat nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## Law aaj bhi kya nahi deta

Itne gates ke baad bhi MTP Act ne Indian women ko kabhi "abortion on request" nahi diya. Har stage par gate doctor ki opinion se khulta hai, woman ke apne decision se nahi, jaisa us rule par hamara myth-check samjhata hai. Yeh Act woman ka right kam, aur un conditions ki list zyada hai jinmein doctor act kar sakta hai.

Zyada tar abortions kabhi kisi health facility tak pahunchte hi nahi. 2015 mein India mein andaazan 15.6 million abortions hue, aur unmein se 11.5 million (73%) medication abortions the jo kisi health facility ke bahar hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

24 hafte ke baad law mein theek unhi women ke liye ek chhed hai jinki madad ke liye 2021 ka rewrite aaya tha: rape survivors aur woh ladkiyan jinhe der se pata chalta hai. Jab tak Parliament yeh chhed nahi bharti, unka raasta ab bhi ek lawyer aur courtroom se hokar hi jaata hai.

mtp-amendment-2021-what-changed.en:
For half a century, India's abortion rules barely moved. The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act received the President's assent on 10 August 1971 [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]], and its week limits stood until an amendment took effect on 24 September 2021 [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]]. A 2002 amendment added two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for unqualified providers but left those limits untouched [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. The 2021 rewrite widened access for many women. Set the two texts side by side, though, and you also see what Parliament chose not to touch. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The 1971 rules that lasted half a century

The 1971 Act allowed an abortion up to 12 weeks on the opinion of one registered doctor, and between 12 and 20 weeks only if two registered doctors agreed [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Past 20 weeks there was no route at all, except an abortion done in good faith to save the woman's life, which even the penal code had always allowed [[gazette-bns-2023]].

Its most revealing line was about contraception. A doctor could presume that an unwanted pregnancy gravely injured a woman's mental health when a contraceptive failed, but only one "used by any married woman or her husband for the purpose of limiting the number of children" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The law pictured one kind of woman: a wife managing the size of her family.

For a woman carrying a foetus with a severe abnormality, or a pregnancy from rape, the only door past 20 weeks was a court petition, and the government later cited exactly those petitions as a reason to change the law [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]].

## Before and after, clause by clause

| Question | MTP Act, 1971 | Since 24 September 2021 |
|---|---|---|
| One doctor's opinion is enough | up to 12 weeks | up to 20 weeks |
| Two doctors must agree | 12 to 20 weeks | 20 to 24 weeks, listed categories only |
| After the last limit | only to save her life | to save her life, or with no limit for a substantial foetal abnormality found by a Medical Board |
| Contraceptive-failure ground covers | "any married woman or her husband" | "any woman or her partner" |
| Section 5A on revealing her identity | did not exist | up to one year in prison, a fine, or both |

The new column comes from the amended Act [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. A woman at 15 weeks now needs one doctor's opinion, not two, and every state and union territory must set up a Medical Board, with at least a gynaecologist, a paediatrician and a radiologist or sonologist.

One thing did not change: an adult woman's own consent is still the only consent required [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

## A year's wait in the Rajya Sabha

The rewrite moved slowly. The Lok Sabha passed the amendment bill on 17 March 2020; the Rajya Sabha approved it only on 16 March 2021, almost a year later [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. The President gave assent on 25 March 2021 [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], and the law took effect six months after that.

Even then a piece was missing. The Act does not say who may seek an abortion between 20 and 24 weeks; it leaves that list to rules, which the Health Ministry notified on 12 October 2021, naming seven categories, among them rape survivors and minors [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. From the Lok Sabha vote to the full rules took more than a year and a half.

When the Rajya Sabha passed the bill, the government said the changes would ensure "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" for women [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Those four words are a fair test.

## "Any woman or her partner": a small edit with a long reach

The smallest edit may matter most. The 2021 text swapped "any married woman or her husband" for "any woman or her partner", and added "or preventing pregnancy" to the purpose [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. In plain words, an unmarried 19-year-old whose condom broke now has the presumption the law once kept for wives. For 50 years the statute treated an unwanted pregnancy as a married couple's family-planning problem; now it speaks of a woman and a partner, married or not.

It did not reach every gate. Rule 3B, written for the 20-24 week window, spoke of a "change of marital status" through widowhood or divorce, and on 15 July 2022 the Delhi High Court turned away an unmarried woman about 22 weeks pregnant, saying it "cannot go beyond the Statute" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Only on 29 September 2022 did the Supreme Court hold that excluding unmarried and single women violates Article 14 [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Parliament changed one phrase; a court had to finish the sentence.

## The gaps the amendment did not close

Test the four words. Dignity and confidentiality: real gains, from "any woman or her partner" to a jail term for a doctor who exposes a woman's identity. Autonomy: not yet. Abortion is still not available on request: as our myth-check on the doctor's-opinion rule shows, a doctor's opinion, not her decision, still opens every gate.

Justice: not for the women whose petitions drove the change. The no-limit route after 24 weeks exists only for a substantial foetal abnormality [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], with a board opinion due within three days and the abortion within five days of the request [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Unless her life is in danger, a rape survivor or a girl who learns she is pregnant at 26 weeks has no route in the Act, and no such deadlines: she must still petition a High Court or the Supreme Court.

Nor did it touch the clash with POCSO. A doctor must report any pregnancy in a girl under 18 to the police, and in 2022 the Supreme Court observed that this leaves a pregnant minor and her guardian choosing between a registered doctor, with possible criminal proceedings, and an unqualified provider. The court's own fix was partial: the doctor need not give the girl's name or personal details in that police report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. And the youngest are the most exposed: UNFPA India (2022) reports that young women aged 15-19 were at the highest risk of dying from an abortion-related complication [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

It took fifty years to move the week limits once. The list for the next rewrite is already written: autonomy for adults, a route for survivors past 24 weeks, and safety for pregnant girls.
mtp-amendment-2021-what-changed.hg:
Aadhi sadi tak India ke abortion rules lagbhag hile hi nahi. Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act ko 10 August 1971 ko President ki assent mili [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]], aur iski hafton wali limits tab tak wahi rahi jab tak 24 September 2021 ko ek amendment lagu nahi hua [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]]. 2002 ke ek amendment ne unqualified providers ke liye 2 se 7 saal ki rigorous imprisonment jodi thi, lekin in limits ko waise hi rehne diya [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. 2021 ke rewrite se bahut si women ke liye access badha. Lekin dono texts ko side by side rakho, toh yeh bhi dikhta hai ki Parliament ne kin cheezon ko chhua tak nahi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1971 ke rules jo aadhi sadi chale

1971 ka Act 12 hafte tak ek registered doctor ki opinion par abortion allow karta tha, aur 12 se 20 hafte ke beech tabhi jab do registered doctors agree karein [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 20 hafte ke baad koi raasta nahi tha, siwaye us abortion ke jo good faith mein woman ki jaan bachane ke liye kiya jaye, aur itni chhoot toh penal code bhi hamesha se deta aaya tha [[gazette-bns-2023]].

Is law ki sabse revealing line contraception ke baare mein thi. Contraceptive fail hone par doctor maan sakta tha ki unwanted pregnancy se woman ki mental health ko grave injury ho rahi hai, lekin sirf tab jab woh method "any married woman or her husband" ne "limiting the number of children" ke liye use kiya ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Law ki nazar mein ek hi tarah ki woman thi: apni family ka size plan karti hui wife.

Jis woman ke foetus mein serious abnormality ho, ya jiski pregnancy rape se hui ho, uske liye 20 hafte ke baad bas ek darwaza tha: court petition. Baad mein government ne law badalne ki ek wajah theek inhi petitions ko bataya [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]].

## Pehle aur ab, clause by clause

| Sawaal | MTP Act, 1971 | 24 September 2021 se |
|---|---|---|
| Ek doctor ki opinion kab tak kaafi | 12 hafte tak | 20 hafte tak |
| Do doctors ka agree karna kab zaroori | 12 se 20 hafte | 20 se 24 hafte, sirf listed categories ke liye |
| Last limit ke baad | sirf jaan bachane ke liye | jaan bachane ke liye, ya Medical Board substantial foetal abnormality paaye toh koi limit nahi |
| Contraceptive-failure ground kiske liye | "any married woman or her husband" | "any woman or her partner" |
| Identity reveal karne par Section 5A | tha hi nahi | 1 saal tak jail, fine, ya dono |

Naya column amended Act se hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Ab 15 hafte ki pregnancy mein do nahi, ek doctor ki opinion kaafi hai, aur har state aur union territory ko ek Medical Board banana hai, jismein kam se kam ek gynaecologist, ek paediatrician aur ek radiologist ya sonologist ho.

Ek cheez nahi badli: adult woman ki apni consent hi woh akeli consent hai jo law maangta hai [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

## Rajya Sabha mein ek saal ka wait

Yeh rewrite bahut dheere aaya. Lok Sabha ne amendment bill 17 March 2020 ko pass kiya; Rajya Sabha ne use lagbhag ek saal baad, 16 March 2021 ko approve kiya [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. President ne 25 March 2021 ko assent di [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], aur uske 6 mahine baad law lagu hua.

Tab bhi ek piece missing tha. Act khud nahi batata ki 20 se 24 hafte ke beech kaun abortion kara sakta hai; woh list rules par chhod di gayi, jo Health Ministry ne 12 October 2021 ko notify kiye. Unmein saat categories hain, jinmein rape survivors aur minors bhi hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Lok Sabha ke vote se poore rules tak dedh saal se zyada laga.

Jab Rajya Sabha ne bill pass kiya, government ne kaha ki yeh changes women ko "dignity, autonomy, confidentiality and justice" denge [[pib-mtp-amendment-bill-rs-2021]]. Yeh chaar words is law ko parakhne ka sahi test hain.

## "Any woman or her partner": chhota edit, bada asar

Sabse chhota edit shayad sabse important hai. 2021 ke text ne "any married woman or her husband" ki jagah "any woman or her partner" likha, aur purpose mein "or preventing pregnancy" bhi jod diya [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Simple words mein, agar ek unmarried 19 saal ki ladki ke saath condom phat jaye, toh use bhi woh presumption milta hai jo law pehle sirf wives ke liye rakhta tha. 50 saal tak law unwanted pregnancy ko married couple ki family planning problem maanta raha; ab woh ek woman aur uske partner ki baat karta hai, shaadi hui ho ya nahi.

Lekin yeh edit har gate tak nahi pahuncha. 20-24 hafte ke liye bane Rule 3B mein "change of marital status" ki baat thi, yaani pati ki maut ya divorce, aur 15 July 2022 ko Delhi High Court ne lagbhag 22 hafte pregnant ek unmarried woman ko lauta diya, yeh kehkar ki woh "cannot go beyond the Statute" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. 29 September 2022 ko jaakar Supreme Court ne kaha ki unmarried aur single women ko bahar rakhna Article 14 ke khilaaf hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Parliament ne ek phrase badla tha; sentence court ko poora karna pada.

## Woh gaps jo amendment ne band nahi kiye

Ab chaar words par test karo. Dignity aur confidentiality: asli fayda hua, "any woman or her partner" se lekar us doctor ke liye jail tak jo woman ki identity expose kare. Autonomy: abhi nahi. Abortion aaj bhi sirf request par nahi milta: doctor's-opinion rule par hamara myth-check dikhata hai ki har gate ab bhi doctor ki opinion se khulta hai, woman ke decision se nahi.

Justice: un women ko nahi mila jinki petitions ne yeh change karwaya. 24 hafte ke baad no-limit route sirf substantial foetal abnormality ke liye hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], jismein board ko 3 din mein opinion deni hai aur request ke 5 din ke andar abortion hona hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Lekin jab tak jaan ko khatra na ho, jis rape survivor ya ladki ko week 26 mein pregnancy ka pata chale, uske liye Act mein koi raasta nahi, aur aisi koi deadline bhi nahi: use aaj bhi High Court ya Supreme Court mein petition daalni padti hai.

POCSO ke saath clash ko bhi isne nahi chhua. 18 se kam umar ki ladki ki har pregnancy doctor ko police ko report karni hoti hai, aur 2022 mein Supreme Court ne khud kaha ki isse pregnant minor aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi option bachte hain: registered doctor ke paas jaayen aur shayad criminal proceedings mein phansein, ya kisi unqualified provider ke paas jaayen. Court ka apna hal bhi adhoora tha: agar ladki aur uske guardian kahein, toh doctor ko us police report mein uska naam ya personal details dene ki zaroorat nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Aur sabse zyada khatra sabse kam umar walon ko hai: UNFPA India (2022) ke mutabik abortion se judi complications se marne ka sabse zyada risk 15-19 saal ki young women ko tha [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

Hafton wali limits ko ek baar badalne mein 50 saal lag gaye. Agle rewrite ki list pehle se likhi hui hai: adults ke liye autonomy, 24 hafte ke baad survivors ke liye raasta, aur pregnant ladkiyon ke liye safety.

partner-pregnant-guide-for-men.en:
Imagine a 24-year-old in Indore. His girlfriend of two years sends him a photo of a pregnancy test and one line: she does not want to continue. He does not know what he is allowed to do, what he should pay for, or what to say. This guide is for him, and for husbands too. It is general information, not legal or medical advice.

## Her decision, legally and ethically

Under the MTP Act, no pregnancy can be ended "except with the consent of the pregnant woman". A guardian signs only if she is under 18 or mentally ill [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The Act asks for no husband's signature and no boyfriend's.

Since 2021 the law does mention you. When a contraceptive used by "any woman or her partner" fails, it presumes the anguish of that pregnancy to be a grave injury to her mental health, a ground for abortion [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. It names you as someone who shares the contraception, not the consent.

Being unmarried changes none of this: the Supreme Court held in 2022 that unmarried women get the same access as married women between 20 and 24 weeks [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The ethics follow the law. The pregnancy, the procedure and the recovery all happen in her body.

If she is under 18, a guardian must consent in writing, and the doctor must report the pregnancy to the police, because sexual activity with anyone under 18 is an offence under POCSO whatever was agreed. The Supreme Court ruled in 2022 that the report need not disclose her identity if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. She needs a registered doctor and a trusted adult, not a secret fix.

## What support looks like, and what pressure looks like

In NFHS-5, the most common main reason women gave for an abortion was an unplanned pregnancy, at 47.6%. But 4.1% said the main reason was that their husband or mother-in-law did not want the pregnancy [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For those women, the main reason was somebody else's wish.

Support starts with one question: what does she want? Let her finish. Then tell her that it is her decision and that you are not going anywhere. Vanishing at this point leaves her to do all of it alone.

Pressure rarely sounds like an order. It sounds like "my parents will throw me out", repeated until she gives in. It looks like going silent for days, setting deadlines, offering marriage as a bargain, or asking whether the pregnancy is even yours. Pushing her to end a pregnancy she wants is the same wrong as pushing her to continue one she does not.

## Practicalities: money, travel, privacy

Time comes first. Doctors count a pregnancy from the first day of her last period, so she is further along than the date of sex suggests, and abortion pills are approved only up to nine weeks, or 63 days, on a qualified doctor's prescription [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Help her reach a registered doctor this week.

Do not go to a chemist for a kit on her behalf: without a doctor, nobody confirms how far along she is or whether pills are right for her. With one, abortion is very safe. WHO puts deaths from safe abortion at under 1 per 100,000 abortions [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

Money: in NFHS-5, 52.9% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion had it in the private sector and 20.3% in the public sector [[nfhs5-india-2021]], so expect a bill. Pay at least half without being asked. Paying does not buy you a vote.

Travel: take the day off, go with her if she wants you there, and see her home. Afterwards, very heavy bleeding, fever or severe pain means a hospital the same day.

Privacy: a doctor who reveals her name or details to anyone not authorised by law faces up to a year in prison [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. No such law binds you, so hold yourself to it. Tell no friend, cousin or parent unless she says so.

## If you disagree

You may want this pregnancy when she does not. Say so once, honestly, as a feeling and not a demand, then accept her answer. The Act gives you no veto, and a week of arguing only uses up her calendar.

Or you may want an abortion when she wants to continue. You cannot make that happen. Causing a miscarriage without the woman's consent is a crime under Section 89 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, punishable with up to ten years in prison or life [[gazette-bns-2023]]. Giving her abortion pills without her knowledge can fall under that section.

Either way, you may feel relief, guilt or grief. Those feelings are not hers to manage while she recovers. Talk to someone she is comfortable with you telling, or call Tele-MANAS on 14416 [[tele-manas]].

## Why vasectomy stays at 0.3%, and your share from now on

In NFHS-5, 37.9% of currently married women relied on female sterilisation, about two thirds of all modern contraceptive use. Male sterilisation stood at 0.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For every husband who has been sterilised, more than a hundred wives have.

The survey does not ask men why. But their own answers point to one reason: in the same survey, 35.1% of men aged 15-49 agreed that contraception is "women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Your share starts now: fertility can return soon after an abortion, so ask the doctor about contraception at the same visit [[nhm-cac]]. In typical use, about 13 in 100 women relying on external condoms become pregnant in the first year, against about 20 with withdrawal and about 85 with no method [[who-fp]]. Buy the condoms yourself and use one every time. If one breaks, emergency contraception works up to five days after sex, and sooner is better [[who-ec]]. If your family is complete, ask a doctor about vasectomy.

None of this asks you to be a hero. It asks you to turn up, pay up, keep her secret and carry your half of the contraception from here on.
partner-pregnant-guide-for-men.hg:
Indore ke ek 24 saal ke ladke ko imagine kijiye. Do saal se uski girlfriend hai, aur ek din woh use pregnancy test ki photo ke saath ek line bhejti hai: woh yeh pregnancy continue nahi karna chahti. Use nahi pata ki use kya karne ki ijazat hai, kis cheez ke paise dene chahiye, ya kya bolna chahiye. Yeh guide usi ke liye hai, aur husbands ke liye bhi. Yeh general information hai, legal ya medical advice nahi.

## Faisla uska hai, law mein bhi aur ethics mein bhi

MTP Act ke mutabiq koi bhi pregnancy "except with the consent of the pregnant woman" khatam nahi ki ja sakti, yaani pregnant aurat ki apni consent ke bina nahi. Guardian tabhi sign karta hai jab woh 18 se kam umar ki ho ya mentally ill ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Act na husband ka signature maangta hai, na boyfriend ka.

2021 se law mein aapka zikr zaroor hai. Jab "any woman or her partner" ka use kiya hua contraceptive fail ho jaata hai, toh law maan leta hai ki us pregnancy ki takleef uski mental health ko grave injury hai, jo abortion ka ek ground hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Law aapko contraception mein hissedaar maanta hai, consent mein nahi.

Shaadi nahi hui hai toh bhi isme kuch nahi badalta: Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki 20 se 24 hafte ke beech unmarried aurton ko wahi access milega jo shaadishuda aurton ko milta hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Ethics bhi wahi kehti hai jo law kehta hai. Pregnancy, procedure aur recovery, teeno uske body mein hote hain.

Agar woh 18 se kam umar ki hai, toh guardian ki likhit consent zaroori hai, aur doctor ko pregnancy ki report police ko deni hi hogi, kyunki 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity POCSO ke tehat offence hai, chahe dono ki marzi rahi ho. Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki agar woh aur uske guardian kahein, toh us report mein uski identity batana zaroori nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Use ek registered doctor aur ek bharosemand adult chahiye, koi chhupa hua jugaad nahi.

## Support kaisa dikhta hai, aur pressure kaisa

NFHS-5 mein auraton ne abortion ki jo main wajah sabse zyada batayi, woh thi unplanned pregnancy: 47.6%. Lekin 4.1% ne kaha ki main wajah yeh thi ki unke husband ya saas ko yeh pregnancy nahi chahiye thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In auraton ke liye main wajah kisi aur ki marzi thi.

Support ek sawaal se shuru hota hai: woh kya chahti hai? Use poori baat kehne dijiye. Phir use bataiye ki faisla uska hai aur aap kahin nahi ja rahe. Is mod par gayab ho jaane ka matlab hai ki sab kuch use akele karna padega.

Pressure aksar order jaisa sunai nahi deta. Woh aisa sunai deta hai: "mere parents mujhe ghar se nikaal denge", aur yeh baat tab tak dohrayi jaati hai jab tak woh haar na maan le. Woh aisa dikhta hai: kai din tak chup ho jaana, deadlines dena, shaadi ko saude ki tarah offer karna, ya yeh poochna ki pregnancy aapki hai bhi ya nahi.
