Ek hypothetical sochiye. Teen saal ki beti ki maa, ek 26 saal ki aurat, phir se pregnant hai. Saas ek aise clinic mein scan book karti hain "jahan batate hain", aur pati kehta hai ki bas confirm karna hai. Act ki nazar mein khatra un logon ko hai jo us par pressure daal rahe hain, use nahi.

Isse pressure ko na kehna aasaan nahi ho jaata. Taane, dhamkiyan, ya aise abortion ki taraf dhakelna jo woh nahi chahti, abuse hai, family use kuch bhi naam de. Woh Women Helpline 181 par call kar sakti hai, ya khatre mein ho toh 112 par, aur clinic ki report karne wali woh khud bhi ho sakti hai.

## Complaint kaise karein, aur kya abortion ab bhi legal hai?

Shuruaat Appropriate Authority se kijiye: district ke woh health officials jo yeh Act laagu karte hain. Court kisi case ko tabhi le sakta hai jab complaint us authority ya uske authorised officer ki taraf se ho, ya kisi aise insaan ya social organisation ki taraf se jisne authority ko kam se kam 15 din ka notice diya ho [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Yaani agar officials complaint par baith jaayein, toh notice ka samay poora hone ke baad aap khud court ja sakte hain. Complaint se pehle date, clinic ka naam, kya kaha ya ishaara kiya gaya aur kitne paise diye gaye, sab likh lijiye, aur receipts aur ads ke screenshots sambhaal kar rakhiye.

Aur abortion? Woh legal hai. 2021 mein amend hue MTP Act ke under, 20 hafte tak ki pregnancy ek registered doctor ki raay par khatam ki ja sakti hai, agar use jaari rakhne se aurat ki jaan ko khatra ho ya uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan ho, ya baby mein gambhir abnormality ka bada risk ho [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 20 se 24 hafte ke beech, rules mein likhi categories ki aurton ke liye, do doctors ki sehmati se abortion ki ijaazat hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]].

PC-PNDT Act inmein se kuch nahi badalta. Woh sex ke hisaab se chunne ko rokta hai, pregnancy khatam karne ko nahi. Jis aurat ko abortion chahiye, use registered doctor ya sarkari hospital jaana chahiye, aur sirf isliye door nahi rehna chahiye ki do alag laws aapas mein uljha diye gaye hain.

sex-ratio-at-birth-states-map.en:
For every 1,000 boys born in Uttarakhand in 2021-23, India's official birth survey counted 868 girls [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Delhi counted 872. Haryana counted 884. These are not old census figures or a foreign estimate. They come from the Sample Registration System (SRS), run by the Registrar General of India. Put the states side by side and a map appears of where girls are still being stopped from being born. Read it carefully, though: a single state's number can be made to say more than it knows.

## 917 against nature's 950

Left alone, nature produces slightly more boys than girls: about 105 boys for every 100 girls [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]], or roughly 950 girls for every 1,000 boys. India as a whole recorded 917 in 2021-23 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Biology does not explain that gap. Pew Research Center traces India's "missing" female births to female-selective abortion [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

The national figure is rising slowly, from 904 in 2017-19 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]] to 918 for 2022-24 in the newest report, published in May 2026 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. But a national average is a blend. It mixes states close to nature's level with states far below it, and it is the states that show where the pressure to have a son is still winning.

## The bottom five and the top two

Among the bigger states, these recorded the lowest sex ratios at birth in 2021-23 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]:

| State | Girls born per 1,000 boys, 2021-23 |
|---|---|
| Uttarakhand | 868 |
| Delhi | 872 |
| Haryana | 884 |
| Maharashtra | 894 |
| Bihar | 897 |
| India (all states) | 917 |

At the other end were Chhattisgarh (974) and Kerala (971) [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

The bottom five share no single region: a Himalayan state, the national capital, its neighbour Haryana, the state that is home to Mumbai, and a state in the east. Nor is this only a village story. Nationally, towns and cities recorded a higher ratio than villages, 925 against 914, yet the capital sits second from the bottom [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

The pattern held in the next report. For 2022-24, Uttarakhand was again the lowest, at 872, followed again by Delhi and Haryana, and Chhattisgarh was again the highest, at 978 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. The two periods share two years, so this is not a fully independent check. It does show that Uttarakhand's figure was not a blip.

## When women name a female foetus

A birth ratio shows the outcome. The fifth National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) came closer to the decision itself: it asked women whose last pregnancy ended in an abortion for the main reason. Nationally, 2.1% named a female foetus. Among the larger states, the share was highest in Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) and Punjab (4.2%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Treat these as a floor. Sex selection is a crime, and admitting it to a government surveyor is rare. Consider a hypothetical: the question reaches a woman in a two-room house, with her mother-in-law within earshot. "It was unplanned" is the safer answer, whatever happened. The state shares also rest on small numbers of abortions.

Still, Bihar appears on both lists: fifth from the bottom in SRS, first in women's own answers among the larger states. When two different kinds of evidence point at the same state, the signal is stronger than either alone. Punjab and Jharkhand, which stand out in women's answers, are not in the SRS bottom five. A survey answer and a birth count are different instruments, and neither sees everything.

## Two surveys, two Uttarakhands

NFHS-5 also estimated each state's sex ratio at birth, for children born in the five years before the survey. Its lowest larger states were Himachal Pradesh (875), Tamil Nadu (878), Rajasthan (891) and Haryana (893). For Uttarakhand it gave 984 [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]], well above nature's level. SRS gave 868 for 2021-23, the lowest among bigger states [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

Both cannot be right about the same state. The surveys cover different years, but no real change in so short a time explains a gap that wide. The likelier culprit is sample size: a state estimate rests on far fewer births than a national one, and survey figures for single states have swung sharply between rounds. Even the national numbers differ: 929 in NFHS-5 [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]] against 917 in SRS. SRS is the official annual series, and the two should never be stitched into one trend.

A reader who saw only NFHS-5 would draw the map around Himachal Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. A reader who saw only SRS would draw it around Uttarakhand and Delhi. Haryana is low in both, 893 in one and 884 in the other, and that agreement is worth more than any single figure.

## What a state number can and cannot prove

A state number can prove a pattern. When a ratio sits far below nature's level, stays there across rounds and is matched by another source, as Haryana's is, it is strong evidence of sex selection at scale among that state's births. It can also puncture comfortable stories, such as the idea that this belongs to one region, or only to villages.

It cannot prove where, or who. It cannot name the district, the clinic or the family. It cannot show that every family in a low state chooses sons, or that none in a high state does: Chhattisgarh's 974 does not mean no clinic there reveals a foetus's sex. It cannot settle whether a state improved when two surveys disagree. And it cannot say who decided. The PC-PNDT Act itself presumes, unless proved otherwise, that a pregnant woman who sought sex selection was compelled by her husband or relatives [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

What a state number can do is point enforcement somewhere. Under the same Act, a court can take up an offence only on a complaint from the district Appropriate Authority or an authorised officer, or from a person or organisation that has given the authority 15 days' notice [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. The map shows where to look. Someone still has to look, and to file.
sex-ratio-at-birth-states-map.hg:
2021-23 mein Uttarakhand mein har 1,000 ladkon ke janm par India ke official birth survey ne sirf 868 ladkiyan ginin [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Delhi mein yeh number 872 tha. Haryana mein 884. Yeh kisi purane census ke figures nahi hain, na kisi videshi sanstha ka andaaza. Yeh Sample Registration System (SRS) ke number hain, jise Registrar General of India chalata hai. States ko ek saath rakhiye, toh ek map ubharta hai: kahan aaj bhi ladkiyon ko paida hone se roka ja raha hai. Par is map ko dhyaan se padhiye. Kisi ek state ke number se woh baatein bhi kehlwayi ja sakti hain jo woh number jaanta hi nahi.

## 917 vs nature ka 950

Agar koi dakhal na de, toh nature thode zyada ladke paida karta hai: har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 105 ladke [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]], yaani har 1,000 ladkon par kareeb 950 ladkiyan. Poore India ka figure 2021-23 mein 917 tha [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Yeh gap biology se nahi aata. Pew Research Center ke mutabik India mein "missing" ladkiyon ki wajah female-selective abortion hai, yaani ladki hone ki wajah se karwaya gaya abortion [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

National figure dheere-dheere badh raha hai: 2017-19 mein yeh 904 tha [[srs-statistical-report-2023]], aur May 2026 mein chhapi nayi report mein 2022-24 ke liye 918 hai [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Lekin national average ek mixture hai. Ismein woh states bhi hain jo nature ke level ke kareeb hain, aur woh bhi jo usse bahut neeche hain. Asli kahani states batate hain: kahan bete ki chahat ka pressure aaj bhi jeet raha hai.

## Sabse neeche ke paanch, sabse upar ke do

Bade states mein 2021-23 mein sabse kam sex ratio at birth in states ka tha [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]:

| State | Har 1,000 ladkon par paida hui ladkiyan, 2021-23 |
|---|---|
| Uttarakhand | 868 |
| Delhi | 872 |
| Haryana | 884 |
| Maharashtra | 894 |
| Bihar | 897 |
| India (sab states) | 917 |

Doosre sire par Chhattisgarh (974) aur Kerala (971) the [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

In paanch states ka koi ek region nahi hai: ek Himalayan state, desh ki rajdhani, uska padosi Haryana, Mumbai wala state, aur poorab ka ek state. Yeh sirf gaon ki kahani bhi nahi hai. National level par shehron ka ratio gaon se behtar tha, 925 ke muqable 914, phir bhi rajdhani neeche se doosre number par hai [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

Agli report mein bhi yahi pattern dikha. 2022-24 mein Uttarakhand phir sabse neeche tha, 872 par, uske baad phir Delhi aur Haryana the, aur Chhattisgarh phir sabse upar tha, 978 par [[srs-statistical-report-2024]]. Dono periods mein do saal common hain, isliye yeh poori tarah alag jaanch nahi hai. Par itna saaf hai ki Uttarakhand ka number koi ek baar ki gadbad nahi tha.

## Jab aurtein khud kehti hain: pet mein ladki thi

Birth ratio nateeja dikhata hai. Paanchvaan National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) faisle ke thoda aur kareeb gaya. Usne un aurton se poocha jinki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui ki main wajah kya thi. Poore desh mein 2.1% ne kaha ki pet mein ladki thi. Bade states mein yeh share sabse zyada Bihar (5.3%), Jharkhand (4.9%) aur Punjab (4.2%) mein tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

In numbers ko floor samjhiye, yaani kam se kam itna. Sex selection crime hai, aur sarkari surveyor ke saamne ise maan lena bahut kam hota hai. Ek hypothetical sochiye: yeh sawaal do kamron wale ghar mein ek aurat tak pahunchta hai, aur saas paas hi baithi sun rahi hai. "Pregnancy plan nahi ki thi" kehna zyada safe jawaab hai, sach chahe kuch bhi ho. State-wise share bhi kam abortions ki ginti par tike hain.

Phir bhi Bihar dono list mein aata hai: SRS mein neeche se paanchvan, aur bade states mein aurton ke apne jawabon mein sabse upar. Jab do alag tarah ke saboot ek hi state ki taraf ishara karein, toh signal kisi ek saboot se zyada mazboot hota hai. Punjab aur Jharkhand aurton ke jawabon mein upar hain, par SRS ke bottom five mein nahi. Survey ka jawaab aur janm ki ginti do alag auzaar hain, aur koi bhi akela sab kuch nahi dekhta.

## Do survey, do Uttarakhand

NFHS-5 ne bhi har state ka sex ratio at birth nikala, survey se pehle ke paanch saal mein paida hue bachchon ke liye. Uske hisaab se sabse kam wale bade states the Himachal Pradesh (875), Tamil Nadu (878), Rajasthan (891) aur Haryana (893). Uttarakhand ko usne 984 diya [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]], jo nature ke level se bhi kaafi upar hai. SRS ne 2021-23 ke liye 868 diya, bade states mein sabse kam [[srs-statistical-report-2023]].

Ek hi state ke baare mein dono sahi nahi ho sakte. Dono survey alag saalon ke hain, lekin itne kam samay mein koi asli badlaav itna bada gap nahi bana sakta. Zyada sambhav wajah sample size hai: state ka estimate national estimate se kahin kam births par tika hota hai, aur akele state ke survey figures rounds ke beech bahut uchhalte rahe hain. National number bhi alag hain: NFHS-5 mein 929 [[pib-child-sex-ratio-nfhs5-2021]], SRS mein 917. SRS official saalana series hai, aur dono ko jod kar ek trend kabhi nahi banana chahiye.

Jo reader sirf NFHS-5 dekhega, woh map Himachal Pradesh aur Tamil Nadu ke aas-paas banayega. Jo sirf SRS dekhega, woh Uttarakhand aur Delhi ke aas-paas. Haryana dono mein neeche hai, ek mein 893 aur doosre mein 884, aur dono ki yeh sehmati kisi bhi ek number se zyada keemti hai.

## State ka number kya saabit kar sakta hai, aur kya nahi

State ka number ek pattern saabit kar sakta hai. Jab ratio nature ke level se bahut neeche ho, rounds ke baad bhi wahin tika rahe, aur doosra source bhi wahi kahe, jaise Haryana ke saath hai, toh yeh mazboot saboot hai ki us state ke janmon mein bade paimane par sex selection ho raha hai. Yeh kuch aaraamdeh kahaniyon ko bhi tod deta hai, jaise ki yeh sirf ek region ki, ya sirf gaon ki problem hai.

Lekin yeh nahi bata sakta ki kahan, ya kaun. Yeh district, clinic ya family ka naam nahi le sakta. Yeh saabit nahi kar sakta ki kam number wale state ki har family beta chunti hai, ya zyada number wale state mein koi nahi chunta: Chhattisgarh ke 974 ka matlab yeh nahi ki wahan koi clinic foetus ka sex nahi batata. Jab do survey alag baat kahein, toh yeh tay nahi kar sakta ki state sudhra ya nahi. Aur yeh nahi bata sakta ki faisla kisne liya. PC-PNDT Act khud maan kar chalta hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho, ki jis pregnant aurat ne sex selection karwaya, use uske pati ya rishtedaaron ne majboor kiya tha [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

State ka number itna zaroor kar sakta hai ki enforcement ko sahi jagah ki taraf mod de. Isi Act ke under court kisi offence par tabhi case le sakta hai jab complaint district ki Appropriate Authority ya authorised officer kare, ya koi aisa insaan ya sanstha kare jisne authority ko 15 din ka notice diya ho [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Map batata hai ki kahan dekhna hai. Dekhna aur complaint file karna, phir bhi kisi ko toh karna hoga.

sex-ratio-progress-son-preference-india.en:
India's birth records are changing, slowly enough that it rarely makes the news. In 2017-19, the Sample Registration System (SRS) counted 904 girls born for every 1,000 boys. By 2021-23 it counted 917 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. That is real progress, measured in the government's own data. It is also unfinished, and the wish that drove sex selection in the first place has not gone anywhere.

## Five rounds, thirteen points

SRS reports the sex ratio at birth as three-year averages. Across five rounds, the national figure went 904, 907, 913, 914 and 917 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. The newest report, published in May 2026, puts 2022-24 at 918 [[srs-statistical-report-2024]].

Thirteen points in five rounds is not a revolution. Nature produces about 105 boys for every 100 girls [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]], roughly 950 girls per 1,000 boys, and India is still well short. The climb is uneven too: three points, then six, then one, three and one. Because each round shares two years with the one before, the series moves smoothly by design, and a bad year can hide inside an average.

A separate source points the same way. Pew Research Center, using the census and the National Family Health Survey (NFHS), found the imbalance narrowing from about 111 boys per 100 girls in the 2011 census to about 109 in 2015-16 and 108 in 2019-21 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. Pew counts the other way round, boys per 100 girls, so a falling number is the good news. The two series use different methods and should not be stitched together, but they agree on the direction.

## Fewer missing girls each year

A ratio is easier to feel as a count. Pew estimates that at least 9.0 million female births went "missing" in India between 2000 and 2019 because of female-selective abortions. The yearly number fell from about 480,000 in 2010 to about 410,000 in 2019 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

Read both halves of that sentence. The fall means tens of thousands more girls a year allowed to be born. What remains is still hundreds of thousands a year who were not. And Pew's figure is a floor: it rests on survey data that show a less skewed ratio than SRS does, so other scholars' estimates run higher.

## The Sikh story: a change, not a blame

The sharpest change has come among Sikhs. In the 2001 census, Sikh families recorded 130 boys born for every 100 girls. By 2011 it was 121, and in NFHS-5 (2019-21) about 110, close to the national figure of 108 [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. The latest estimate has a margin of error of about 8 either way, but across two censuses and a national survey the direction is clear. Pew found the biggest falls in sex selection among the groups that had the greatest imbalances.

This is not a story to pin on one community. Read it the other way. A group whose ratio was once far more lopsided than the national average has moved close to it in about two decades. Whatever drove that, it shows sex selection is a practice, not a fixed trait. Practices change.

## Son preference has not gone away

The birth ratio tracks what families do. It does not track what they want. In a 2014 survey by the International Center for Research on Women (ICRW) and UNFPA in seven states, 76% of men and 81% of women said it was very important to have at least one son [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

More women than men said so. That does not make women the problem. A woman's answer can carry the pressure she lives with: the taunts after a second daughter, the sense that her place in her husband's family rests on a son. No woman chooses her baby's sex, yet it is mothers who get blamed.

Son preference does not stop at birth, either. UNFPA reports that sex selection before birth explains about two thirds of India's missing girls, and excess deaths of girls after birth about one third [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. A ratio of births cannot see that third.

Consider a hypothetical family WhatsApp group. A cousin's daughter is born, and the group fills with hearts and congratulations. Then an aunt types: "Next time, a boy." Nobody replies to that line. This is how a preference survives a rising birth ratio: politely, in public, among people who love the baby.

The 2014 survey covered seven states and is twelve years old, so it cannot say whether attitudes have moved since. It does show how deep the wish ran in years when, by Pew's estimate, the yearly loss of girls was already falling.

## What will make the change last

A ratio that rose can stall or slip, and the gap to nature's level remains. Three things would help the gains hold.

Keep counting, honestly. SRS publishes every year. Compare its figures only with its own earlier figures, and watch the states, not just the national average.

Make the law bite where the decision is made. Anyone who seeks sex selection faces up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 50,000 for a first offence, though the law presumes a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives and does not punish a woman who was forced [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Police registered only 31 cases under the PC-PNDT Act in 2024, after 57 in 2022 and 30 in 2023 [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. Most prosecutions under this law start as complaints filed in court, usually by district health officials, so police data undercount them, and any person or organisation can also go to court after giving those officials 15 days' notice [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Change what a daughter is worth at home. Son preference rests on what sons are expected to bring: property, care in old age, the family name. The gains will hold when daughters are expected, and allowed, to bring the same, and when "next time, a boy" gets an answer.
sex-ratio-progress-son-preference-india.hg:
India ke birth records badal rahe hain, itni dheemi raftaar se ki yeh shayad hi kabhi news banta hai. 2017-19 mein Sample Registration System (SRS) ne har 1,000 ladkon par 904 ladkiyon ka janm gina. 2021-23 tak yeh number 917 ho gaya [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. Yeh asli progress hai, sarkar ke apne data mein. Lekin yeh adhoori hai, aur jis chahat ne sex selection ko janm diya, woh kahin nahi gayi.

## Paanch rounds, terah points

SRS sex ratio at birth ko teen-teen saal ke average mein batata hai. Paanch rounds mein national figure aise chala: 904, 907, 913, 914 aur 917 [[srs-statistical-report-2023]]. May 2026 mein chhapi nayi report 2022-24 ke liye 918 batati hai [[srs-statistical-report-2024]].

Paanch rounds mein terah points koi kranti nahi hai. Nature har 100 ladkiyon par lagbhag 105 ladke paida karta hai [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]], yaani har 1,000 ladkon par kareeb 950 ladkiyan, aur India abhi bhi usse kaafi peeche hai. Chadhai ek jaisi bhi nahi rahi: teen points, phir chhah, phir ek, teen aur ek. Har round ke do saal pichhle round se common hote hain, isliye yeh series design se hi smooth chalti hai, aur koi bura saal average ke andar chhup sakta hai.

Ek alag source bhi isi taraf ishara karta hai. Pew Research Center ne census aur National Family Health Survey (NFHS) ke data se dekha ki imbalance 2011 census ke lagbhag 111 ladke per 100 ladkiyon se ghat kar 2015-16 mein lagbhag 109 aur 2019-21 mein 108 par aa gaya [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. Pew ulta ginta hai, yaani 100 ladkiyon par kitne ladke, isliye yahan number ka girna achhi khabar hai. Dono series ke tareeke alag hain aur unhe jod kar ek line nahi banani chahiye, par dono ki disha ek hai.

## Har saal kam 'missing' ladkiyan

Ratio ko ginti mein badliye, toh woh zyada mehsoos hota hai. Pew ka andaaza hai ki 2000 se 2019 ke beech India mein kam se kam 9.0 million ladkiyon ke janm female-selective abortion, yaani ladki hone ki wajah se karwaye gaye abortion, ki wajah se "missing" ho gaye. Saalana number 2010 ke lagbhag 480,000 se ghat kar 2019 mein lagbhag 410,000 reh gaya [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]].

Is line ke dono hisse padhiye. Giravat ka matlab hai ki har saal das hazaron aur ladkiyon ko paida hone diya gaya. Jo bacha hai, woh ab bhi har saal laakhon ladkiyan hain jinhe paida nahi hone diya gaya. Aur Pew ka figure ek floor hai: yeh aise survey data par tika hai jo SRS se kam tircha ratio dikhata hai, isliye doosre researchers ke estimates isse zyada hain.

## Sikhon ki kahani: badlaav ki, ilzaam ki nahi

Sabse tez badlaav Sikhon mein aaya hai. 2001 census mein Sikh families mein har 100 ladkiyon par 130 ladke paida hue the. 2011 tak yeh 121 hua, aur NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein lagbhag 110, jo national figure 108 ke kareeb hai [[pew-india-sex-ratio-2022]]. Latest estimate mein dono taraf lagbhag 8 ka margin of error hai, lekin do census aur ek national survey ko saath rakhein toh disha saaf hai. Pew ne paaya ki sex selection mein sabse badi giravat unhi groups mein aayi jinmein imbalance sabse zyada tha.

Yeh kahani kisi ek community par ungli uthane ki nahi hai. Ise ulti taraf se padhiye. Jis group ka ratio kabhi national average se kahin zyada tircha tha, woh lagbhag do dashakon mein uske kareeb aa gaya. Wajah jo bhi rahi ho, isse yeh saabit hota hai ki sex selection ek practice hai, kisi community ki fixed pehchaan nahi. Aur practices badalti hain.

## Bete ki chahat gayi nahi hai

Birth ratio yeh dikhata hai ki families kya karti hain. Yeh nahi dikhata ki woh kya chahti hain. International Center for Research on Women (ICRW) aur UNFPA ke 2014 ke survey mein, jo saat states mein hua, 76% mardon aur 81% aurton ne kaha ki kam se kam ek beta hona bahut zaroori hai [[icrw-unfpa-masculinity-ipv-son-preference-2014]].

Mardon se zyada aurton ne yeh kaha. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki problem aurtein hain. Aurat ke jawaab mein woh pressure bhi bolta hai jiske saath woh jee rahi hai: doosri beti ke baad ke taane, yeh ehsaas ki sasural mein uski jagah bete par tiki hai. Koi aurat apne baby ka sex nahi chunti, phir bhi blame maa ko hi milta hai.

Bete ki chahat janm par ruk bhi nahi jaati. UNFPA ke mutabik India ki "missing" ladkiyon mein se lagbhag do-tihaai ki wajah janm se pehle ka sex selection hai, aur lagbhag ek-tihaai ki wajah janm ke baad ladkiyon ki zyada maut [[unfpa-swop-2020]]. Janm ka ratio woh ek-tihaai nahi dekh sakta.

Ek hypothetical family WhatsApp group sochiye. Ek cousin ke ghar beti hui hai, aur group hearts aur badhaiyon se bhar jaata hai. Phir ek aunty type karti hain: "Agli baar beta." Us line par koi kuch nahi kehta. Bete ki chahat aise hi badhte birth ratio ke bawajood bachi rehti hai: tameez se, sabke saamne, un logon ke beech jo us bachchi se pyaar karte hain.

2014 ka survey saat states ka tha aur ab baarah saal purana hai, isliye yeh nahi bata sakta ki tab se soch kitni badli. Yeh itna zaroor dikhata hai ki yeh chahat un saalon mein kitni gehri thi jab, Pew ke andaaze se, ladkiyon ka saalana nuksaan pehle se ghat raha tha.

## Yeh badlaav tikega kaise

Jo ratio upar gaya hai, woh ruk bhi sakta hai aur phisal bhi sakta hai, aur nature ke level tak ka gap abhi baaki hai. Teen cheezein is progress ko tikaane mein madad karengi.

Ginti jaari rakhiye, imaandari se. SRS har saal report chhapta hai. Uske figures ko sirf uske apne purane figures se milaiye, aur sirf national average nahi, states par bhi nazar rakhiye.

Law ko wahan laagu kijiye jahan faisla hota hai. Jo bhi sex selection karwana chahe, use pehli baar mein teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 50,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai, lekin law maan kar chalta hai ki pregnant aurat ko uske pati ya rishtedaaron ne majboor kiya tha, aur jis aurat ko majboor kiya gaya, use saza nahi deta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Police ne 2024 mein PC-PNDT Act ke under sirf 31 cases darj kiye, 2022 mein 57 aur 2023 mein 30 ke baad [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. Is law ke zyada tar case court mein complaint se shuru hote hain, aksar district ke health officials ki taraf se, isliye police data unhe poora nahi ginta. Koi bhi insaan ya sanstha bhi un officials ko 15 din ka notice de kar court ja sakti hai [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Ghar mein beti ki keemat badaliye. Bete ki chahat is umeed par tiki hai ki beta kya laayega: property, budhape ka sahara, khandaan ka naam. Yeh progress tab tikegi jab betiyon se bhi yahi umeed ki jaayegi, aur unhe yeh karne diya jaayega, aur jab "agli baar beta" ka jawaab diya jaayega.

teenage-pregnancy-india-child-marriage-m.en:
Imagine a 17-year-old in a village in West Bengal. She left school after Class 8, was married at 16 and is now expecting her first child. Her family does not call this a teenage pregnancy. They call it good news after a wedding. India's national health surveys count her differently, and they show that she is far from alone, and that where she lives matters as much as how old she is.

## 6.8% at 15-19, 20% by 19

In the National Family Health Survey of 2019-21 (NFHS-5), 6.8% of women aged 15-19 had begun childbearing: they had already given birth or were pregnant with their first child. At the top of that age band the share is far higher: 20.0% at 19 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. In that survey, one in five 19-year-olds was already a mother or about to become one.

The next survey shows the figure barely moved. In NFHS-6 (2023-24), 6.7% of women aged 15-19 were mothers or pregnant, and the rural rate (7.9%) was more than double the urban rate (3.4%) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Over the same years, the share of women aged 20-24 married before 18 fell from 23.3% to 20.1% [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Why did one fall and not the other? The teenage figure includes 18- and 19-year-olds, adults who can marry legally, so it measures early marriage and early childbearing together, not only pregnancies under 18. The NFHS-6 numbers are also still provisional. Ending marriage before 18 is not the same as ending marriage in the teens.

## The state map of teenage motherhood

The national average hides a sharp map. In NFHS-5, teenage childbearing was highest in Tripura, where 21.9% of women aged 15-19 had begun childbearing, more than three times the national figure. West Bengal followed at 16.4%, then Andhra Pradesh (12.6%), Assam (11.7%) and Bihar (11.0%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

| State | Women 15-19 who had begun childbearing (NFHS-5) | Women 20-24 married before 18 (NFHS-6) |
|---|---|---|
| Tripura | 21.9% | 34.0% |
| West Bengal | 16.4% | 36.4% |
| Andhra Pradesh | 12.6% | 25.1% |
| Assam | 11.7% | 25.3% |
| Bihar | 11.0% | 34.6% |
| India | 6.8% | 20.1% |

The two columns come from different survey rounds and count different women, so read them as two maps laid side by side, not as one series.

## Child marriage: the engine underneath

Lay the child-marriage map over the first one and the same names appear. In NFHS-5, marriage before 18 among women aged 20-24 was highest in West Bengal (41.6%), Bihar (40.8%) and Tripura (40.1%) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], all three in the top five for teenage childbearing. In NFHS-6 the leaders were West Bengal (36.4%), Bihar (34.6%), Tripura (34.0%), Jharkhand (28.1%), Assam (25.3%) and Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Every one of the five states with the most teenage mothers is on that list of six. Even the rural-urban split repeats: in NFHS-6 the rural rate of marriage before 18 (23.3%) was about double the urban rate (11.4%), much like the gap in teenage pregnancy.

Two maps cannot prove cause on their own, but the pattern is too consistent to ignore. Where girls are married young, they become mothers young.

In law, many of these pregnancies are evidence of a crime (this is general information, not legal advice). Since the Supreme Court's 2017 judgment in Independent Thought v. Union of India, sex with a wife under 18 is rape [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Yet police registered just 1,499 cases under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act in all of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], in a country where one young woman in five was married as a child.

## Married at 17, little say over contraception

A wedding does not make a girl ready for a child, and many married teenagers want to wait. Among currently married girls aged 15-19 in NFHS-5, only 28.1% used any method of contraception, and 17.8% had an unmet need for family planning: they wanted to delay or avoid a pregnancy but were using nothing. That is nearly double the 9.4% unmet need among all married women [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The power to decide often sits with someone else. In the same survey, 35.1% of men agreed that contraception is "women's business", and only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. For a 17-year-old bride in her in-laws' home, with relatives waiting for news, "not yet" is a hard sentence to say.

And if she tries to end an unwanted pregnancy without a trained provider, her age counts against her. UNFPA India calls unsafe abortion the third leading cause of maternal deaths in the country, and says young women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from abortion complications [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Poverty, schooling and what changes the map

NFHS-5 also shows who these girls are. Among girls aged 15-19 with no schooling, 17.6% had begun childbearing; in the poorest households 10.0% had, against 2.2% in the richest [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. UNICEF notes that girls who marry before 18 are less likely to stay in school and more likely to experience domestic violence [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Poverty, an early exit from school, an early wedding and an early first child are one chain, not four separate problems.

What breaks the chain is known. UN Women credits the worldwide fall in child marriage largely to girls' education, economic empowerment and poverty reduction [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. In October 2024 the Supreme Court told states to appoint district Child Marriage Prohibition Officers with no other duties and to have magistrates issue injunctions around "auspicious days" for mass weddings, putting "prevention before protection and protection before penalisation" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Married teenagers also need contraception offered without judgement. Adolescent Friendly Health Centres, which began as reproductive and sexual health clinics for adolescents, offer counselling at primary and community health centres, district hospitals and medical colleges [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

A wedding can still be stopped before it happens: the Child Helpline 1098 is linked to the 112 emergency system [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. And a girl already married as a child can ask a district court to annul the marriage until two years after she becomes an adult [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. The map will change when girls in Tripura, West Bengal and Bihar finish school, marry later and choose when to have a first child.
teenage-pregnancy-india-child-marriage-m.hg:
Sochiye, West Bengal ke ek gaon ki 17 saal ki ladki. Usne Class 8 ke baad school chhod diya, 16 ki umar mein uski shaadi ho gayi, aur ab woh apne pehle bachche ki ummeed se hai. Uski family ise teenage pregnancy nahi kehti. Unke liye yeh shaadi ke baad ki "khushkhabri" hai. India ke national health surveys use alag tarah se ginte hain, aur dikhate hain ki woh akeli nahi hai. Woh kahan rehti hai, yeh utna hi maayne rakhta hai jitna uski umar.

## 15-19 mein 6.8%, 19 tak 20%

National Family Health Survey 2019-21 (NFHS-5) mein 15-19 saal ki 6.8% auratein childbearing shuru kar chuki thi: yaani ya toh bachche ko janm de chuki thi, ya pehle bachche se pregnant thi. Is age group ke upar wale sire par yeh share kaafi zyada hai: 19 saal par 20.0% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani us survey mein 19 saal ki har paanch mein se ek ladki ya toh maa thi ya maa banne wali thi.

Agle survey mein tasveer lagbhag nahi badli. NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 15-19 saal ki 6.7% auratein maa thi ya pregnant thi, aur gaon ka rate (7.9%) shehar ke rate (3.4%) se double se bhi zyada tha [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Unhi saalon mein 20-24 saal ki jin auraton ki shaadi 18 se pehle hui, unka share 23.3% se ghatkar 20.1% ho gaya [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

Ek figure ghata, doosra kyun nahi? Teenage wale figure mein 18 aur 19 saal ki ladkiyan bhi shaamil hain, jo adult hain aur kanooni taur par shaadi kar sakti hain. Isliye yeh figure jaldi shaadi aur jaldi maa banna, dono ko ek saath naapta hai, sirf 18 se kam umar ki pregnancies ko nahi. NFHS-6 ke numbers abhi provisional bhi hain. 18 se pehle ki shaadi khatam hona, teenage mein shaadi khatam hone jaisa nahi hai.

## Teenage maaon ka state-wise naqsha

National average ke peeche ek bahut tez naqsha chhupa hai. NFHS-5 mein teenage childbearing sabse zyada Tripura mein thi, jahan 15-19 saal ki 21.9% auratein maa ban chuki thi ya pregnant thi, yaani national figure se teen guna se bhi zyada. Uske baad West Bengal (16.4%) tha, phir Andhra Pradesh (12.6%), Assam (11.7%) aur Bihar (11.0%) [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

| State | 15-19 saal ki auratein jo maa ban chuki thi ya pregnant thi (NFHS-5) | 20-24 saal ki auratein jinki shaadi 18 se pehle hui (NFHS-6) |
|---|---|---|
| Tripura | 21.9% | 34.0% |
| West Bengal | 16.4% | 36.4% |
| Andhra Pradesh | 12.6% | 25.1% |
| Assam | 11.7% | 25.3% |
| Bihar | 11.0% | 34.6% |
| India | 6.8% | 20.1% |

Dono columns alag survey rounds se hain aur alag auraton ko ginte hain. Isliye inhe ek series ki tarah nahi, balki saath-saath rakhe do naqshon ki tarah padhiye.

## Child marriage: asli engine

Child marriage ka naqsha pehle naqshe ke upar rakhiye, toh wahi naam dikhte hain. NFHS-5 mein 20-24 saal ki auraton mein 18 se pehle shaadi sabse zyada West Bengal (41.6%), Bihar (40.8%) aur Tripura (40.1%) mein thi [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]], aur teeno teenage childbearing ke top paanch mein bhi hain. NFHS-6 mein sabse aage the West Bengal (36.4%), Bihar (34.6%), Tripura (34.0%), Jharkhand (28.1%), Assam (25.3%) aur Andhra Pradesh (25.1%) [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]]. Sabse zyada teenage maaon wale paanchon states is chhe ki list mein hain. Gaon aur shehar ka fark bhi wahi hai: NFHS-6 mein gaon mein 18 se pehle shaadi ka rate (23.3%) shehar ke rate (11.4%) se lagbhag double tha, bilkul teenage pregnancy wale fark jaisa.

Do naqshe akele wajah saabit nahi kar sakte, lekin yeh pattern itna pakka hai ki ise nazarandaaz nahi kiya ja sakta. Jahan ladkiyon ki shaadi jaldi hoti hai, wahan woh maa bhi jaldi banti hain.

Kanoon ki nazar mein inmein se kai pregnancies ek jurm ka saboot hain (yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi). Supreme Court ke 2017 ke Independent Thought v. Union of India faisle ke baad se, 18 se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex rape hai [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Phir bhi 2024 mein poore saal mein police ne Prohibition of Child Marriage Act ke tahat sirf 1,499 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], us desh mein jahan har paanch mein se ek young aurat ki shaadi bachpan mein hui thi.

## 17 mein shaadi, contraception par na ke barabar haq

Shaadi ho jaane se koi ladki bachche ke liye taiyaar nahi ho jaati, aur kai shaadishuda teenagers intezaar karna chahti hain. NFHS-5 mein 15-19 saal ki shaadishuda ladkiyon mein sirf 28.1% koi bhi contraceptive method use kar rahi thi, aur 17.8% ki family planning ki zaroorat poori nahi ho rahi thi (isse "unmet need" kehte hain): woh pregnancy taalna ya rokna chahti thi, par koi method use nahi kar rahi thi. Yeh sabhi shaadishuda auraton ki 9.4% unmet need ka lagbhag double hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Faisla lene ki taakat aksar kisi aur ke haath mein hoti hai. Usi survey mein 35.1% mardon ne maana ki contraception "auraton ka kaam" hai, aur 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% young auraton ko pata tha ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young mardon mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sasural mein rehne wali 17 saal ki dulhan ke liye, jab poora parivaar "khushkhabri" ka intezaar kar raha ho, "abhi nahi" kehna bahut mushkil hai.

Aur agar woh kisi trained provider ke bina ek unwanted pregnancy khatam karne ki koshish karti hai, toh uski umar uske khilaaf jaati hai. UNFPA India ke mutabik unsafe abortion desh mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah hai, aur 15-19 saal ki young auraton ko abortion complications se maut ka sabse zyada khatra hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Gareebi, schooling aur naqsha kaise badlega

NFHS-5 yeh bhi dikhata hai ki yeh ladkiyan kaun hain. Bina schooling wali 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon mein 17.6% maa ban chuki thi ya pregnant thi; sabse gareeb gharon mein yeh 10.0% tha, jabki sabse ameer gharon mein sirf 2.2% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. UNICEF kehta hai ki jin ladkiyon ki shaadi 18 se pehle hoti hai, unke school mein tike rehne ki sambhavna kam hoti hai aur domestic violence jhelne ki sambhavna zyada [[unicef-child-marriage-topic-page]]. Gareebi, jaldi school chhootna, jaldi shaadi aur jaldi pehla bachcha: yeh chaar alag problems nahi, ek hi zanjeer ki kadiyan hain.

Yeh zanjeer kaise tootti hai, yeh pata hai. UN Women ke mutabik duniya bhar mein child marriage mein giravat zyada tar ladkiyon ki padhai, economic empowerment aur gareebi kam hone se aayi [[unwomen-gender-snapshot-2026]]. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne states se kaha ki har district mein aise Child Marriage Prohibition Officers rakhein jinke paas koi aur kaam na ho, aur magistrates saamuhik shaadiyon wale "auspicious days" (shubh muhurat) ke aas-paas injunctions jaari karein. Court ki line thi: "prevention before protection and protection before penalisation" [[sc-seva-child-marriage-2024]]. Shaadishuda teenagers ko bhi bina judge kiye contraception milni chahiye. Adolescent Friendly Health Centres, jo teenagers ke liye reproductive aur sexual health clinics ke roop mein shuru hue the, primary aur community health centres, district hospitals aur medical colleges mein counselling dete hain [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]].

Shaadi ab bhi hone se pehle roki ja sakti hai: Child Helpline 1098, 112 emergency system se judi hai [[mwcd-child-helpline-sop-2023]]. Aur jis ladki ki shaadi bachpan mein ho chuki hai, woh adult hone ke do saal baad tak district court se shaadi annul karwa sakti hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Naqsha tab badlega jab Tripura, West Bengal aur Bihar ki ladkiyan school poora karengi, der se shaadi karengi aur khud tay karengi ki pehla bachcha kab chahiye.

unmarried-women-abortion-supreme-court-2.en:
Imagine a 23-year-old in Lucknow, 21 weeks pregnant. Her relationship has just ended. The clinic's form has a line for her husband's name, and she has none to write. Until 2022, the rules for her week of pregnancy had a category for a widow or a divorcee, but not for her. A Supreme Court judgment on 29 September 2022 changed that. Our story on the 2021 amendment covers how Parliament rewrote the law's married-only words; this one covers the ruling that finished the job. It is general information, not legal advice.

## The married-only clause of 1971

The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act's grounds applied to any pregnant woman, but its easiest door was written for wives. A doctor could presume that an unwanted pregnancy gravely injured a woman's mental health when a contraceptive failed, but only one used by "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

For 50 years that was the text. In 2021 Parliament changed the words to "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], with effect from 24 September 2021 [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]]. That helped single women in the first 20 weeks, where one doctor's opinion is enough.

The next window was another matter. Between 20 and 24 weeks, abortion is allowed only for categories of women listed in the rules, with two doctors' opinions [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Rule 3B, notified on 12 October 2021, listed seven, including women whose marital status changes during the pregnancy through widowhood or divorce [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. A woman who had never married had no matching line to stand in.

## July 2022: a refusal, then an interim order

The gap reached a courtroom within a year. An unmarried woman, about 22 weeks pregnant, asked the Delhi High Court to allow an abortion. On 15 July 2022 the court refused interim relief, saying it "cannot go beyond the Statute" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

She appealed. On 21 July 2022 the Supreme Court modified the High Court's order and allowed her to end the pregnancy if a Medical Board at AIIMS Delhi found it safe. AIIMS later reported that the procedure was carried out safely [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Between those two dates, the pregnancy did not wait. A woman in the same week whose husband had died, or who had divorced, would have fitted a category. What separated them was a marriage.

## 29 September 2022: an 'artificial' distinction rejected

The court did not stop at her case. In its final judgment, Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna and J.B. Pardiwala settled the question for every woman. Reading Rule 3B as limited to married women, they held, would make it discriminatory and violate Article 14, the right to equality; unmarried and single women get the same access between 20 and 24 weeks as married women [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

> "This artificial distinction between married and single women is not constitutionally sustainable. The benefits in law extend equally to both single and married women." [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]

The court also grounded the right in Article 21: "The rights of reproductive autonomy, dignity, and privacy under Article 21 give an unmarried woman the right of choice on whether or not to bear a child, on a similar footing of a married woman" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. In practice, it read the rule's "change of marital status" category to cover unmarried and single women whose circumstances change during the pregnancy [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]].

The same judgment held that "rape" in the abortion law includes marital rape, and that no FIR is needed to rely on it [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]; our story on wives forced into pregnancy explains that part.

## What an unmarried woman can ask for now

| Stage | What the law needs | For a single woman |
|---|---|---|
| Up to 20 weeks | One registered doctor's opinion | Same as anyone; a failed contraceptive used by "any woman or her partner" counts |
| 20 to 24 weeks | Two doctors and a Rule 3B category | Same as a married woman since 29 September 2022 |
| After 24 weeks | A Medical Board finding a substantial foetal abnormality | The same narrow route as everyone |

The stages come from the 2021 amendment [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]; marital status now changes none of them.

**Consent.** If she is 18 or older, hers is the only consent the law asks for. A guardian's written consent is needed only if she is under 18 or mentally ill, and the Act asks for no husband's or partner's consent [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. A partner cannot veto her decision, and his signature cannot replace hers.

**Privacy.** A doctor who reveals her name or details to anyone not authorised by law faces up to one year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. An adult's parents have no legal role in her decision.

**Under 18.** A guardian's written consent is required, and the doctor must report the pregnancy to the police under POCSO. The Supreme Court said the girl's identity can be kept out of that report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## If a clinic asks for a husband

If a receptionist or a doctor asks for a husband's name, a marriage certificate or a partner's signature, you can say, calmly: "I am over 18. Under the MTP Act only my consent is needed. The Supreme Court ruled on 29 September 2022, in X v. Principal Secretary, that unmarried women have the same access as married women."

You do not have to prove a marriage or name a partner. The doctor's task is to judge a legal ground, such as a risk to your health, a failed contraceptive or, between 20 and 24 weeks, a change in your circumstances, not your marital status.

If they still refuse, leave and go the same day to another registered provider or a government hospital. Do not let a refusal push you towards an unqualified one. UNFPA India estimated in 2022 that unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths in India, with close to eight women dying every day from causes related to it [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

The woman who took this to the Supreme Court is known in the law reports only as X. Because she did, the next single woman at 21 weeks has the law on her side.
unmarried-women-abortion-supreme-court-2.hg:
Socho, Lucknow mein 23 saal ki ek ladki hai, 21 hafte pregnant. Uska relationship abhi-abhi khatam hua hai. Clinic ke form mein husband ke naam ki line hai, aur uske paas likhne ko koi naam nahi. 2022 tak uske hafte ke liye bane rules mein widow ya divorced aurat ke liye category thi, par uske liye nahi. 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court ke ek judgment ne yeh badal diya. 2021 ke amendment par hamari story batati hai ki Parliament ne law ke married-only words kaise badle; yeh story us ruling ke baare mein hai jisne baaki kaam poora kiya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1971 ka married-only clause

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act ke grounds har pregnant aurat par lagu hote the, lekin iska sabse aasaan darwaza wives ke liye bana tha. Agar contraceptive fail ho jaaye, to doctor maan sakta tha ki is unwanted pregnancy se aurat ki mental health ko gambhir chot pahunchi hai, par sirf tab jab woh method "any married woman or her husband" use kar rahe hon [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]].

50 saal tak yahi text raha. 2021 mein Parliament ne words badal kar "any woman or her partner" kar diye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], jo 24 September 2021 se lagu hua [[livelaw-mtp-amendment-in-force-2021]]. Isse single aurton ko pehle 20 hafton mein madad mili, jahan ek doctor ki opinion kaafi hai.

Agli window ki kahani alag thi. 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion sirf un aurton ke liye allowed hai jinki category rules mein likhi hai, aur do doctors ki opinion bhi chahiye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 12 October 2021 ko notify hue Rule 3B mein aisi saat categories thin, jinme woh aurtein thin jinka marital status pregnancy ke dauraan badal jaaye, yaani widow ho jaayein ya divorce ho jaaye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-rules-2021]]. Jiski kabhi shaadi hi nahi hui, uske liye is list mein aisi koi line nahi thi.

## July 2022: pehle refusal, phir interim order

Yeh gap ek saal ke andar courtroom tak pahunch gaya. Ek unmarried aurat, qareeb 22 hafte pregnant, ne Delhi High Court se abortion ki permission maangi. 15 July 2022 ko High Court ne interim relief dene se mana kar diya aur kaha ki woh "cannot go beyond the Statute", yaani law se aage nahi ja sakta [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Usne appeal ki. 21 July 2022 ko Supreme Court ne High Court ka order modify kiya aur kaha ki agar AIIMS Delhi ka Medical Board ise safe paaye, to woh pregnancy end kar sakti hai. Baad mein AIIMS ne report kiya ki procedure safely ho gaya [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

In do dates ke beech pregnancy ruki nahi. Usi hafte mein koi aisi aurat hoti jiske husband ki maut ho gayi ho ya jiska divorce hua ho, to woh kisi category mein fit ho jaati. Dono ke beech farq bas ek shaadi ka tha.

## 29 September 2022: ek 'artificial' farq khaarij

Court uske case par nahi ruka. Apne final judgment mein Justices D.Y. Chandrachud, A.S. Bopanna aur J.B. Pardiwala ne yeh sawaal har aurat ke liye settle kar diya. Unhone kaha ki agar Rule 3B ko sirf married aurton tak limited padha jaaye, to woh discriminatory hoga aur Article 14, yaani equality ke right, ko violate karega; unmarried aur single aurton ko bhi 20 se 24 hafte ke beech wahi access milta hai jo married aurton ko [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

> "This artificial distinction between married and single women is not constitutionally sustainable. The benefits in law extend equally to both single and married women." [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]

Court ne is right ko Article 21 se bhi joda: "The rights of reproductive autonomy, dignity, and privacy under Article 21 give an unmarried woman the right of choice on whether or not to bear a child, on a similar footing of a married woman" [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yaani bachcha paida karna hai ya nahi, yeh chunne ka haq unmarried aurat ka bhi utna hi hai. Practically, court ne rule ki "change of marital status" wali category ko aise padha ki usme woh unmarried aur single aurtein bhi aa jaayein jinke halaat pregnancy ke dauraan badal jaate hain [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]].

Isi judgment ne yeh bhi kaha ki abortion law mein "rape" mein marital rape bhi shaamil hai, aur iske liye FIR zaroori nahi [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]; forced pregnancy jhelne wali wives par hamari story us hisse ko samjhati hai.

## Unmarried aurat ab kya maang sakti hai

| Stage | Law ko kya chahiye | Single aurat ke liye |
|---|---|---|
| 20 hafte tak | Ek registered doctor ki opinion | Sabke barabar; "any woman or her partner" wala contraceptive failure gina jaata hai |
| 20 se 24 hafte | Do doctors aur Rule 3B ki koi category | 29 September 2022 se married aurat ke barabar |
| 24 hafte ke baad | Medical Board jo substantial foetal abnormality paaye | Baaki sabki tarah wahi tang raasta |

Yeh stages 2021 ke amendment se aaye hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]; ab marital status inme se kuch nahi badalta.

**Consent.** Agar tum 18 ya usse badi ho, to law sirf tumhari consent maangta hai. Guardian ki likhit consent tabhi chahiye jab umar 18 se kam ho ya mental illness ho, aur Act husband ya partner ki consent kahin nahi maangta [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Partner tumhara decision rok nahi sakta, aur uska signature tumhari jagah nahi le sakta.

**Privacy.** Agar doctor tumhara naam ya details kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne authorise nahi kiya, to use ek saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Adult aurat ke decision mein uske parents ka koi legal role nahi hai.

**18 se kam.** Guardian ki likhit consent zaroori hai, aur doctor ko POCSO ke tahat police ko pregnancy report karni hoti hai. Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki agar ladki aur uske guardian kahein, to us report mein ladki ki identity nahi deni padti [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## Agar clinic husband ke baare mein pooche

Agar receptionist ya doctor husband ka naam, marriage certificate ya partner ka signature maange, to tum shaanti se keh sakti ho: "Main 18 se badi hoon. MTP Act mein sirf meri consent chahiye. Supreme Court ne 29 September 2022 ko X v. Principal Secretary case mein faisla diya hai ki unmarried aurton ko bhi married aurton jitna hi access hai."

Tumhe shaadi saabit karne ya partner ka naam batane ki zaroorat nahi. Doctor ka kaam legal ground ko judge karna hai, jaise tumhari health ko risk, contraceptive ka fail hona, ya 20 se 24 hafte ke beech tumhare halaat ka badalna, tumhara marital status nahi.

Agar phir bhi mana karein, to wahan se niklo aur usi din kisi doosre registered provider ya sarkari hospital jao. Ek refusal ki wajah se kisi unqualified insaan ke paas mat jao. UNFPA India ke 2022 ke andaaze ke mutabik unsafe abortion India mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah hai, aur isse judi wajahon se har din qareeb aath aurtein jaan gawaati hain [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

Jis aurat ne yeh ladai Supreme Court tak ladi, use law reports mein sirf "X" ke naam se jaana jaata hai. Uski wajah se, 21 hafte par khadi agli single aurat ke saath ab law khada hai.

unmet-need-contraception-married-women-i.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in a small town, married at 18, with a four-month-old baby. She does not want to be pregnant again soon. Everyone around her knows about "the operation" women have after their last child; nobody has sat her down to talk about methods for waiting. Her husband thinks contraception is her business. She is using nothing. India's National Family Health Survey has a name for her situation: an unmet need for family planning.

In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 9.4% of currently married women had one: 4.0% wanted to space their next birth and 5.4% wanted no more children, yet none of them was using any method [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That is down from 13% in 2015-16, and the fall is real progress. But the gap that remains has a shape, and the shape shows who India's family planning was not built for.

## What 'unmet need' measures

A woman has an unmet need if she has decided she does not want a child now, or ever again, yet has no method to act on that decision. It measures a decision left without the means.

Two things sit outside the number. First, the headline figure is calculated only for currently married women; an unmarried woman who is having sex and using nothing is not in the 9.4%. Second, any method counts as "met", however unreliable. In NFHS-5, 10.3% of married women relied on traditional methods such as withdrawal or counting days [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. On paper, they are covered.

Overall, 66.7% of currently married women used some method and 56.4% a modern one, up from 48% for modern methods in 2015-16 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Married teenagers: nearly double the gap

The gap is widest at the start of married life [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Currently married women, NFHS-5 (2019-21) | All, aged 15-49 | Aged 15-19 |
|---|---|---|
| Using any method | 66.7% | 28.1% |
| Unmet need for family planning | 9.4% | 17.8% |

At that age the need is overwhelmingly to delay the next birth, not to stop having children. And the pregnancies come early: of all women aged 15-19, 6.8% had already begun childbearing, rising to 20.0% by age 19 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Some of these wives are 18 or 19. Others are 15, 16 or 17. Under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, a girl under 18 is a child and her marriage is a child marriage [[indiacode-pcma-2006]], and since the Supreme Court's 2017 ruling in Independent Thought, sex with a wife under 18 is rape in law [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. For them, contraception is not the first thing that failed.

The risk is also highest for them. Unsafe abortion is the third leading cause of maternal deaths in India, and young women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from abortion complications, UNFPA India reported in 2022 [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## A method mix built on sterilisation

Female sterilisation was used by 37.9% of currently married women, about two thirds of all modern contraceptive use; male sterilisation by just 0.3% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The methods for waiting reach far fewer couples: condoms 9.5%, the pill 5.1%, an IUD 2.1% and injectables 0.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sterilisation is for women who have finished having children. It does nothing for a young wife who wants a gap between babies, or wants her first child later. A system that leans this heavily on one permanent operation serves the end of a woman's childbearing years far better than the beginning, which is exactly where the teenage gap sits.

The reversible methods are not the problem. In typical use, fewer than 1 in 100 women using an implant or IUD get pregnant in a year; about 4 using the injectable and about 7 using the pill do [[who-fp]].

## From unmet need to abortion

A woman who does not want a pregnancy and uses nothing will often get pregnant anyway. The most recent national estimate put India's pregnancies in 2015 at 48.1 million. Nearly half were unintended, and one third ended in induced abortion [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. That came to an estimated 15.6 million abortions (range 14.1 million to 17.3 million), 47.0 for every 1,000 women aged 15-49 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Around the same time, NFHS-4 (2015-16) put unmet need at 13%.

About 11.5 million of those abortions (73%) were medication abortions outside health facilities. That is not automatically unsafe, but little is known about what women were told or whether they took the pills correctly [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

NFHS-5 shows the same chain from the other end. Asked for the main reason for their abortion, 47.6% of women named an unplanned pregnancy and 9.7% said their last child was too young [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. "Last child too young" is the spacing gap, reported after the fact.

## What closes the gap

More operations will not close it. Choices for waiting will: reversible methods offered to young wives early, before a first pregnancy or soon after a birth, with a real choice between them.

Men are part of the gap. In NFHS-5, 35.1% of men agreed that contraception is "women's business and a man should not have to worry about it" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Condoms and vasectomy are men's methods, and male sterilisation stands at 0.3%.

So is information. In NFHS-5, only 54.4% of young women aged 15-24 knew where to get a condom, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The women in the 9.4% have already made their decision. What they lack is a method, the information to use it, and a home that lets them.
unmet-need-contraception-married-women-i.hg:
Imagine kijiye, ek chhote shehar ki 19 saal ki ladki hai. Shaadi 18 mein hui, aur ab uska chaar mahine ka baby hai. Woh jaldi phir se pregnant nahi hona chahti. Aas-paas sab us "operation" ke baare mein jaante hain jo aurtein apne aakhri bachche ke baad karwati hain; lekin kisi ne use baith kar yeh nahi samjhaya ki rukne ke liye kaun se methods hote hain. Uske pati ko lagta hai ki contraception uska kaam hai. Woh kuch bhi use nahi kar rahi. India ke National Family Health Survey ke paas uski situation ka ek naam hai: family planning ki unmet need.

NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein 9.4% currently married aurton ki yahi situation thi: 4.0% agle bachche se pehle gap chahti thi aur 5.4% aur bachche nahi chahti thi, phir bhi inmein se koi bhi koi method use nahi kar rahi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. 2015-16 mein yeh figure 13% tha, aur yeh girawat sach mein progress hai. Lekin jo gap bacha hai uski ek shape hai, aur woh shape dikhati hai ki India ki family planning kiske liye bani hi nahi thi.

## 'Unmet need' asal mein kya naapti hai

Kisi aurat ki unmet need tab maani jaati hai jab woh tay kar chuki ho ki use abhi bachcha nahi chahiye, ya kabhi nahi chahiye, lekin us faisle par chalne ke liye uske paas koi method nahi hai. Yeh number ek aise faisle ko naapta hai jiske paas zariya hi nahi hai.

Do cheezein is number se bahar reh jaati hain. Pehli, headline figure sirf currently married aurton ke liye nikala jaata hai; ek unmarried aurat jo sex kar rahi hai aur kuch use nahi kar rahi, woh is 9.4% mein nahi hai. Doosri, koi bhi method "met" gina jaata hai, chahe woh kitna bhi unreliable ho. NFHS-5 mein 10.3% shaadishuda aurtein traditional methods par tiki thi, jaise withdrawal ya din ginna [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Kaagaz par, woh covered hain.

Kul milakar 66.7% currently married aurtein koi na koi method use kar rahi thi aur 56.4% koi modern method; 2015-16 mein modern methods ka figure 48% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Shaadishuda teenagers: gap lagbhag double

Yeh gap shaadi ki shuruaat mein sabse chauda hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Currently married aurtein, NFHS-5 (2019-21) | Sab, 15-49 saal | 15-19 saal |
|---|---|---|
| Koi bhi method use kar rahi thi | 66.7% | 28.1% |
| Family planning ki unmet need | 9.4% | 17.8% |

Is umar mein zaroorat zyada tar agle bachche ko aage khiskane ki hoti hai, bachche paida karna band karne ki nahi. Aur pregnancies jaldi aa jaati hain: 15-19 saal ki sabhi aurton mein se 6.8% childbearing shuru kar chuki thi, aur 19 saal ki umar tak yeh 20.0% ho jaata hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Inmein se kuch wives 18 ya 19 saal ki hain. Baaki 15, 16 ya 17 ki. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke under 18 se kam umar ki ladki child hai aur uski shaadi child marriage hai [[indiacode-pcma-2006]], aur Supreme Court ke 2017 ke Independent Thought faisle ke baad se, 18 se kam umar ki biwi ke saath sex law ki nazar mein rape hai [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. Unke liye contraception woh pehli cheez nahi hai jo fail hui.

Risk bhi sabse zyada inhi ke liye hai. Unsafe abortion India mein maternal deaths ka teesra sabse bada kaaran hai, aur 15-19 saal ki young women ko abortion complications se maut ka sabse zyada risk hai, UNFPA India ne 2022 mein bataya [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]].

## Sterilisation par tika method mix

Female sterilisation 37.9% currently married aurton ne use kiya, jo saare modern contraceptive use ka lagbhag do-tihaai hai; male sterilisation sirf 0.3% ne [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Rukne ke liye bane methods bahut kam couples tak pahunchte hain: condom 9.5%, pill 5.1%, IUD 2.1% aur injectables 0.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Sterilisation un aurton ke liye hai jo bachche paida karna khatam kar chuki hain. Jo young wife do bachchon ke beech gap chahti hai, ya pehla bachcha thoda baad mein chahti hai, uske liye isse kuch nahi hota. Jo system ek permanent operation par itna zyada tika ho, woh aurat ke childbearing years ke aakhri hisse ko shuruaat se kahin behtar serve karta hai. Aur teenage gap theek shuruaat mein hi baitha hai.

Reversible methods problem nahi hain. Typical use mein, implant ya IUD use karne wali 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam aurtein ek saal mein pregnant hoti hain; injectable par lagbhag 4 aur pill par lagbhag 7 [[who-fp]].

## Unmet need se abortion tak

Jo aurat pregnancy nahi chahti aur kuch use nahi karti, woh aksar phir bhi pregnant ho jaati hai. Sabse recent national estimate ke hisaab se 2015 mein India mein 48.1 million pregnancies hui. Inmein se lagbhag aadhi unintended thi, aur ek-tihaai induced abortion par khatam hui [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Yeh estimate lagbhag 15.6 million abortions ka banta hai (range 14.1 million se 17.3 million), yaani 15-49 saal ki har 1,000 aurton par 47.0 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Lagbhag usi samay NFHS-4 (2015-16) ne unmet need 13% batayi thi.

Inmein se lagbhag 11.5 million abortions (73%) health facilities ke bahar hue medication abortions the. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki woh apne aap unsafe the, lekin yeh bahut kam pata hai ki aurton ko kya bataya gaya, ya unhone pills sahi tarah li ya nahi [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

NFHS-5 yahi chain doosre sire se dikhata hai. Abortion ki main wajah poochhne par 47.6% aurton ne unplanned pregnancy batayi aur 9.7% ne kaha ki pichhla bachcha abhi bahut chhota tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. "Pichhla bachcha bahut chhota tha" asal mein spacing wala gap hi hai, bas baad mein report hua.

## Gap kaise bharega

Aur zyada operations se yeh gap nahi bharega. Rukne ke options se bharega: reversible methods jo young wives ko jaldi offer kiye jaayein, pehli pregnancy se pehle ya delivery ke kuch hi samay baad, aur unke beech asli choice ke saath.

Mard bhi is gap ka hissa hain. NFHS-5 mein 35.1% mardon ne maana ki contraception "aurton ka kaam hai, mard ko iski fikr karne ki zaroorat nahi" [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Condom aur vasectomy mardon ke methods hain, aur male sterilisation sirf 0.3% par atka hai.

Jaankari bhi ek hissa hai. NFHS-5 mein 15-24 saal ki sirf 54.4% young women jaanti thi ki condom kahan milta hai, jabki young men mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Jo aurtein is 9.4% mein hain, woh apna faisla kar chuki hain. Unke paas kami hai ek method ki, use istemaal karne ki jaankari ki, aur ek aise ghar ki jo unhe yeh karne de.

unsafe-abortion-deaths-india-eight-a-day.en:
On 1 April 1972, India's Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act came into force and abortion became legal [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Half a century later, UNFPA India estimated that unsafe abortion was still the third leading cause of maternal deaths in the country, with close to eight women dying every day from causes related to it [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. The procedure itself is not what kills them. Where abortion is safe, deaths are negligible, under 1 per 100,000 abortions; where unsafe abortion is common, they exceed 200 per 100,000, the World Health Organization says [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Indian women are dying in the distance between those two numbers.

## Legal since 1972, still deadly

The law was written around doctors. An abortion is legal only when a registered doctor forms the opinion that a legal ground applies [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], and only at an approved place. Anyone else who performs one faces two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

Real life runs on a different track. Of an estimated 15.6 million abortions in India in 2015, about 11.5 million (73%) were medication abortions done outside any health facility [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. In NFHS-5 (2019-21), 26.2% of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion had it at home, and 26.9% said they did it themselves [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Pills are not the villain. Prescribed by a doctor, the mifepristone-misoprostol combination is approved up to nine weeks and works in 95-99% of early abortions [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The danger lies in what nobody checks when the pills come over a counter: how far along the pregnancy is, whether she knows how to take them, and whether she will reach a hospital if something goes wrong.

## Who is most at risk

UNFPA India says young women aged 15-19 face the highest risk of dying from an abortion-related complication [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. That finding comes from a study of 1.8 million pregnant women in nine poorer states covered by the Annual Health Survey. There, 67% of abortions reported for 2007-2011 were classed as unsafe, from 45.1% in Assam to 78.3% in Chhattisgarh [[bmjgh-yokoe-unsafe-abortion-2019]]. "Unsafe" meant done or completed outside a health facility, by someone other than a skilled attendant, or at 20 weeks or later, and the count includes miscarriages as well as induced abortions.

Early pregnancy has not gone away. In NFHS-6 (2023-24), 6.7% of women aged 15-19 were already mothers or pregnant: 7.9% in rural areas against 3.4% in urban areas, by provisional figures [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

For girls under 18, the law adds a trap. Every pregnancy in a minor must be reported to the police under POCSO, and the Supreme Court observed in 2022 that this leaves a girl and her guardian choosing between a registered doctor, with possible criminal proceedings, and an unqualified provider [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Consider a 17-year-old in a small town who has missed two periods. A clinic feels like a police station, so she waits. A chemist sells her pills weeks past the point they are approved for. When the bleeding does not stop, she hides it for two days, because a hospital means questions. Every step is a delay, and delay is what kills.

## Counting the dead with data from 2001-03

How many women actually die? The best-known figures are either estimates or old. The Health Ministry's 2023 abortion care guidelines say unsafe abortion causes about 8% of maternal deaths, but that share rests on Registrar General cause-of-death data for 2001-03 [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. UNFPA's eight-a-day figure is an estimate, not a count. Maternal deaths from unsafe abortion are often misclassified and under-reported because of stigma, the WHO notes [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. A death after a hidden abortion can easily be recorded under another cause.

The overall toll is measured. India's maternal mortality ratio fell from 130 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2014-16 to 88 in 2021-23, the same as in 2020-22 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. The latest bulletin puts 2022-24 at 87, still above the SDG target of below 70 [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. What these figures cannot tell you is whether abortion deaths fell as fast as the total, or now make up a bigger share of a total that has barely moved in three bulletins.

## Why legality was not enough

For almost 50 years, the clause that let a woman cite failed contraception covered only "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Parliament changed it to "any woman or her partner" only in 2021 [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], and on 29 September 2022 the Supreme Court ruled that unmarried women have the same access as married women between 20 and 24 weeks [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Until 2021, on paper, a single woman whose contraception failed had no such presumption to lean on.

The criminal law still hangs over the back door. Outside the MTP Act's conditions, causing a miscarriage is an offence under Section 88 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which expressly covers a woman who causes her own [[gazette-bns-2023]]. So a woman who took pills alone, and is now bleeding, weighs a hospital visit against the fear of questions. The law gives her a reason to delay at exactly the moment delay is most dangerous.

## What would save lives

None of this needs a medical breakthrough. It needs the safe route to be the easy one: prescribed pills in the first nine weeks, from a doctor at a clinic linked to an approved facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. It needs privacy women can believe in. Since 2021, a doctor who reveals the name or details of a woman whose pregnancy was terminated, except to someone authorised by law, faces up to a year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. For minors, the Supreme Court has allowed doctors to keep a girl's name and details out of the POCSO report if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

It also needs hospitals that treat a woman with complications first and ask questions later, and a fresh national count of what kills mothers. India cannot cut deaths whose share it still takes from 2001-03 data.
unsafe-abortion-deaths-india-eight-a-day.hg:
1 April 1972 ko India ka Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act lagu hua aur abortion legal ho gaya [[indiacode-mtp-act-1971]]. Aadhi sadi baad UNFPA India ne andaaza lagaya ki unsafe abortion ab bhi desh mein maternal deaths ki teesri sabse badi wajah hai, aur isse judi wajahon se roz kareeb aath aurtein marti hain [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Inki jaan procedure khud nahi leta. World Health Organization ke mutabik jahan abortion safe hai, wahan maut na ke barabar hai, har 100,000 abortions par 1 se bhi kam; jahan unsafe abortion aam hai, wahan yeh 200 per 100,000 se upar chali jaati hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Indian aurtein in do numbers ke beech ke faasle mein mar rahi hain.

## 1972 se legal, phir bhi jaanleva

Law doctors ko centre mein rakh kar likha gaya. Abortion tabhi legal hai jab ek registered doctor yeh opinion banaye ki koi legal ground lagu hota hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], aur woh bhi sirf approved jagah par. Koi aur abortion kare to use do se saat saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]].

Asli zindagi doosri patri par chalti hai. 2015 mein India mein andaazan 15.6 million abortions hue, jinmein se kareeb 11.5 million (73%) aise medication abortions the jo kisi health facility ke bahar hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. NFHS-5 (2019-21) mein jin aurton ki pichhli pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 26.2% ka abortion ghar par hua, aur 26.9% ne kaha ki unhone khud kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Pills villain nahi hain. Doctor ki likhi mifepristone-misoprostol combination nau hafte tak ke liye approved hai aur early abortions mein 95-99% cases mein kaam karti hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Khatra us cheez mein hai jo counter par pills bechte waqt koi check nahi karta: pregnancy kitne hafte ki hai, kya use pills lene ka sahi tareeka pata hai, aur kuch gadbad hone par kya woh hospital tak pahunch paayegi.

## Sabse zyada khatra kise hai

UNFPA India kehta hai ki 15-19 saal ki ladkiyon ko abortion se judi complication se maut ka sabse zyada khatra hai [[unfpa-swop-2022-india-insights]]. Yeh nateeja 1.8 million pregnant aurton par hui ek study se aata hai, jo Annual Health Survey wale nau gareeb states mein ki gayi thi. Wahan 2007-2011 ke liye report hue 67% abortions unsafe maane gaye, Assam mein 45.1% se lekar Chhattisgarh mein 78.3% tak [[bmjgh-yokoe-unsafe-abortion-2019]]. Wahan "unsafe" ka matlab tha: health facility ke bahar hua ya poora hua, skilled attendant ki jagah kisi aur ne kiya, ya 20 hafte ya uske baad hua. Is ginti mein induced abortions ke saath miscarriages bhi shaamil hain.

Kam umar ki pregnancy gayab nahi hui hai. NFHS-6 (2023-24) mein 15-19 saal ki 6.7% ladkiyan pehle se maa thin ya pregnant thin: rural areas mein 7.9% aur urban areas mein 3.4%, provisional figures ke hisaab se [[nfhs6-factsheets-2026]].

18 se kam umar ki ladkiyon ke liye law ek aur jaal bichhata hai. POCSO ke tahat minor ki har pregnancy police ko report karni padti hai, aur Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki isse ladki aur uske guardian ke saamne do hi raaste bachte hain: registered doctor, jiske saath criminal proceedings ka darr hai, ya koi unqualified provider [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Ek chhote shehar ki 17 saal ki ladki ke baare mein socho jiske do periods miss ho chuke hain. Clinic use police station jaisa lagta hai, isliye woh intezaar karti hai. Ek chemist use pills bech deta hai, us point se kai hafte baad jahan tak woh approved hain. Jab bleeding nahi rukti, to woh do din tak use chhupaati hai, kyunki hospital ka matlab hai sawaal. Har kadam ek der hai, aur der hi jaan leti hai.

## 2001-03 ke data se maut ki ginti

Asal mein kitni aurtein marti hain? Jo figures sabse zyada dohraye jaate hain, woh ya to andaaze hain ya purane. Health Ministry ki 2023 ki abortion care guidelines kehti hain ki maternal deaths mein se lagbhag 8% unsafe abortion se hoti hain, lekin yeh hissa Registrar General ke 2001-03 ke cause-of-death data par tika hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. UNFPA ka roz aath wala figure ek andaaza hai, ginti nahi. WHO kehta hai ki unsafe abortion se hui maternal deaths stigma ki wajah se aksar galat category mein darj hoti hain aur kam report hoti hain [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]]. Chhupa kar kiye gaye abortion ke baad hui maut aasani se kisi aur wajah ke naam likhi ja sakti hai.

Kul maut ka hisaab zaroor rakha jaata hai. India ka maternal mortality ratio 2014-16 mein har 100,000 live births par 130 se gir kar 2021-23 mein 88 par aaya, jo 2020-22 jitna hi tha [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2021-23]]. Sabse naya bulletin 2022-24 ke liye 87 batata hai, jo ab bhi 70 se neeche ke SDG target se upar hai [[srs-mmr-bulletin-2022-24]]. Yeh figures yeh nahi bata sakte ki abortion se hone wali mautein utni hi tezi se ghati jitna total ghata, ya ab woh ek aise total ka bada hissa hain jo teen bulletins se lagbhag hila hi nahi.

## Sirf legal hona kaafi kyun nahi tha

Kareeb 50 saal tak, jis clause ke tahat aurat contraception fail hone ka hawala de sakti thi, woh sirf "any married woman or her husband", yaani shaadishuda aurat ya uske pati, par lagu hota tha [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. Parliament ne ise "any woman or her partner" sirf 2021 mein kiya [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]], aur 29 September 2022 ko Supreme Court ne faisla diya ki 20 se 24 hafte ke beech unmarried aurton ka access bhi shaadishuda aurton jaisa hi hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. 2021 tak kagaz par, jis single aurat ki contraception fail hui, uske paas tikne ke liye aisa koi presumption nahi tha.

Criminal law ab bhi pichhle darwaze par latka hua hai. MTP Act ki sharton ke bahar miscarriage karwana Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 88 ke tahat apraadh hai, aur yeh section saaf taur par us aurat ko bhi cover karta hai jo khud apna miscarriage karti hai [[gazette-bns-2023]]. To jo aurat akele pills le chuki hai aur ab bleeding ho rahi hai, woh hospital jaane ko sawaalon ke darr ke saamne tolti hai. Law use theek usi waqt der karne ki wajah deta hai jab der sabse khatarnak hai.

## Jaan kaise bachegi

Iske liye kisi medical breakthrough ki zaroorat nahi. Zaroorat yeh hai ki safe raasta hi aasaan raasta bane: pehle nau hafton mein doctor ki likhi pills, aise clinic se jo kisi approved facility se juda ho [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Aisi privacy chahiye jis par aurtein bharosa kar sakein. 2021 se, jo doctor kisi aisi aurat ka naam ya details bataye jiski pregnancy terminate hui, law dwara authorised insaan ke alawa kisi ko bhi, use ek saal tak ki jail, jurmana, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Minors ke liye Supreme Court ne doctors ko ijazat di hai ki agar ladki aur uska guardian kahein, to POCSO report mein ladki ka naam aur details na diye jaayein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Aise hospitals bhi chahiye jo complication wali aurat ka pehle ilaaj karein aur sawaal baad mein poochhein, aur ek nayi national ginti jo bataye ki maaon ki jaan kaun si wajahein le rahi hain. India un mauton ko kam nahi kar sakta jinka hissa woh aaj bhi 2001-03 ke data se leta hai.

where-indian-women-get-abortions-numbers.en:
