Ask Indian women where their last abortion happened, and the government hospital comes third. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 52.9% of women whose last pregnancy ended in an abortion had it in the private sector, 26.2% at home and only 20.3% in a public facility [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A woman was more likely to end a pregnancy in her own home than in a hospital run by the state. Here is that map, number by number.

## Private, public, home: the NFHS-5 split

The survey asked each woman about her most recent pregnancy in the five years before the interview and, if it ended in an abortion, where it happened and who performed it. Nearly three in four of those abortions took place in a clinic or hospital of some kind; the rest happened at home. Two in three of all reported abortions were done with medicines rather than a procedure [[nfhs5-india-2021]], which is what makes a home abortion possible at all.

A national study for 2015, published in The Lancet Global Health, measured the same landscape from the supply side, using facility surveys and pill sales. It found a very different balance: only 22% of an estimated 15.6 million abortions took place in a health facility, and private facilities carried 73% of those [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. The two sources are not one series, and the distance between them is a reminder of how much abortion goes unreported. But they agree on the point that matters here. Where the health system handles abortion, it is mostly the private part of it.

## Who performed it: doctor, nurse or the woman herself

A doctor performed 54.8% of the abortions women reported. A nurse, auxiliary nurse-midwife (ANM) or lady health visitor (LHV) performed 13.5%, and 26.9% of women said they did it themselves [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Close to half of India's reported abortions were not done by a doctor.

The survey records who performed an abortion, not whether it was safe. Prescribed by a doctor, the mifepristone-misoprostol combination works in 95-99% of early abortions, and Health Ministry guidelines let a qualified doctor prescribe it up to nine weeks at a clinic linked to an approved facility [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. The danger lies in taking it blind: no check of how far along the pregnancy is, and no doctor to call if the bleeding does not stop.

The law draws a harder line. Only a registered medical practitioner may end a pregnancy. Since 2002, an abortion by anyone else, or at a place not approved under the Act, can bring two to seven years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Yet in all of 2024, police across India registered 15 cases under the MTP Act [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. The prison term has not pulled abortion into approved clinics. The pill has pulled it out.

## Village versus city

Split the same answers by where women live, and two different pictures appear [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| NFHS-5, 2019-21 | Urban | Rural | India |
|---|---|---|---|
| Private sector | 59.5% | 48.9% | 52.9% |
| Public sector | 18.2% | 21.6% | 20.3% |
| At home | 22.1% | 28.7% | 26.2% |
| Performed by a doctor | 65.7% | 48.1% | 54.8% |
| By a nurse, ANM or LHV | 8.8% | 16.4% | 13.5% |
| By the woman herself | 21.6% | 30.0% | 26.9% |

In cities, two in three abortions were done by a doctor. In villages, fewer than half were. Three in ten rural women who had an abortion ended the pregnancy themselves, and about one in six abortions was handled by a nurse, ANM or LHV: front-line health workers whom the MTP Act does not recognise as abortion providers. Village women used the public sector a little more than city women did, yet even there it handled only about one abortion in five.

## Why public hospitals lose women

NFHS-5 did not ask women why they bypassed the government hospital, so the survey cannot rank the reasons. The data and the law still point to some of them.

The pill is closer. In 2015, 87% of the pill abortions done outside facilities used ready-made combipacks [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]], the kind sold across a chemist's counter, often without a doctor's prescription. And when a woman does want a clinic, the one she finds is usually private.

Fear travels with her. The Supreme Court noted in 2022 that because a doctor must report a minor's pregnancy to police under POCSO, a girl and her guardian may weigh a registered doctor and possible criminal proceedings against an unqualified provider [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Adult women at least have privacy on paper: since 2021 a doctor who reveals a woman's abortion to anyone not authorised by law faces up to a year in prison [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Few are ever told this.

Consider a hypothetical. A 28-year-old near Gaya, a mother of two, finds she is seven weeks pregnant. The community health centre is a bus ride away, and nobody has told her whether it offers abortion care. The chemist in her market sells her a combipack without asking for a prescription. If it works, no register will ever show it. If it does not, she will probably end up at a private clinic.

## When things go wrong: where women seek treatment

Of women whose last pregnancy ended in abortion, 15.6% reported complications. Most did not ignore them: 89.7% sought treatment, and 70.6% of that treatment came from the private sector [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The private sector sees women at both ends of an abortion: the beginning and the emergency.

Those emergencies can be grave. In six states surveyed in 2015, 4-16% of women receiving post-abortion care were being treated for serious complications such as infection, perforation, sepsis or shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. The WHO puts the stakes plainly: deaths from safe abortion are under 1 per 100,000 abortions, but exceed 200 per 100,000 where unsafe abortion is common [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

The map will not redraw itself. Until a woman knows that a government hospital near her will see her early and in confidence, the chemist's counter will keep winning.
where-indian-women-get-abortions-numbers.hg:
India ki auraton se poocho ki unka last abortion kahan hua, toh sarkari hospital teesre number par aata hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein, jin auraton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 52.9% ka abortion private sector mein hua, 26.2% ka ghar par, aur sirf 20.3% ka kisi sarkari facility mein [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani ek aurat ke liye apne ghar mein pregnancy khatam karna, sarkar ke chalaye hospital mein karwane se zyada mumkin tha. Yeh raha woh naksha, number dar number.

## Private, sarkari, ghar: NFHS-5 ka batwara

Survey ne har aurat se interview se pehle ke paanch saal ki uski sabse haal ki pregnancy ke baare mein poocha, aur agar woh abortion par khatam hui thi, toh yeh bhi ki woh kahan hua aur kisne kiya. Inmein se lagbhag chaar mein se teen abortions kisi na kisi clinic ya hospital mein hue; baaki ghar par. Report hue saare abortions mein se teen mein se do kisi procedure se nahi, dawaon se hue [[nfhs5-india-2021]], aur isi wajah se ghar par abortion mumkin ho paata hai.

2015 ki ek national study, jo The Lancet Global Health mein chhapi, ne yahi tasveer supply ki taraf se naapi, yaani facility surveys aur pills ki bikri ke data se. Usmein balance bilkul alag nikla: andaazan 15.6 million abortions mein se sirf 22% kisi health facility mein hue, aur unmein se 73% private facilities mein [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Yeh dono sources ek hi series nahi hain, aur dono ke beech ka farak yaad dilata hai ki kitne abortions kabhi report hi nahi hote. Lekin jo baat yahan maayne rakhti hai, us par dono sehmat hain. Health system jahan abortion sambhalta hai, wahan zyada tar uska private hissa hi sambhalta hai.

## Kisne kiya: doctor, nurse ya aurat khud

Auraton ke report kiye abortions mein se 54.8% ek doctor ne kiye. 13.5% kisi nurse, auxiliary nurse-midwife (ANM) ya lady health visitor (LHV) ne kiye, aur 26.9% auraton ne kaha ki unhone khud kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yaani India ke report hue lagbhag aadhe abortions kisi doctor ne nahi kiye.

Survey yeh record karta hai ki abortion kisne kiya, yeh nahi ki woh safe tha ya nahi. Doctor ke prescription par mifepristone-misoprostol combination shuruaati abortions mein 95-99% case mein kaam karta hai, aur Health Ministry ki guidelines ke mutabik qualified doctor ise nau hafte tak, kisi approved facility se jude clinic mein, prescribe kar sakta hai [[mohfw-cac-guidelines-2023]]. Khatra tab hai jab ise andhere mein liya jaaye: na yeh check ki pregnancy kitne hafte ki hai, na koi doctor jise bleeding na rukne par phone kiya ja sake.

Law isse kahin sakht line kheenchta hai. Sirf ek registered medical practitioner hi pregnancy khatam kar sakta hai. 2002 se, kisi aur ke kiye abortion par, ya Act ke tahat approved na ki gayi jagah par hue abortion par, do se saat saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiankanoon-mtp-act-1971-consolidated]]. Phir bhi poore 2024 mein, India bhar ki police ne MTP Act ke tahat sirf 15 case darj kiye [[ncrb-crime-in-india-2024-vol1]]. Jail ki sazaa abortion ko approved clinics ke andar nahi kheench paayi. Pill ne use bahar kheench liya.

## Gaon banaam shehar

Inhi jawabon ko is hisaab se baanto ki auratein kahan rehti hain, toh do alag tasveerein saamne aati hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| NFHS-5, 2019-21 | Shehar | Gaon | India |
|---|---|---|---|
| Private sector | 59.5% | 48.9% | 52.9% |
| Sarkari sector | 18.2% | 21.6% | 20.3% |
| Ghar par | 22.1% | 28.7% | 26.2% |
| Doctor ne kiya | 65.7% | 48.1% | 54.8% |
| Nurse, ANM ya LHV ne kiya | 8.8% | 16.4% | 13.5% |
| Aurat ne khud kiya | 21.6% | 30.0% | 26.9% |

Shehron mein teen mein se do abortions doctor ne kiye. Gaon mein aadhe se bhi kam. Gaon ki jin auraton ka abortion hua, unmein se das mein se teen ne pregnancy khud khatam ki, aur lagbhag chhe mein se ek abortion kisi nurse, ANM ya LHV ne kiya: woh front-line health workers jinhe MTP Act abortion provider nahi maanta. Gaon ki auraton ne sarkari sector ka use shehar ki auraton se thoda zyada kiya, phir bhi wahan bhi sarkar lagbhag paanch mein se ek abortion hi sambhal paayi.

## Sarkari hospital auraton ko kyun kho dete hain

NFHS-5 ne auraton se yeh nahi poocha ki woh sarkari hospital chhod kar kahin aur kyun gayi, isliye survey wajahon ki ranking nahi kar sakta. Phir bhi data aur law kuch wajahon ki taraf ishaara karte hain.

Pill zyada paas hai. 2015 mein facilities ke bahar hue pill abortions mein se 87% mein ready-made combipacks use hue [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]], wahi jo chemist ke counter par bikte hain, aksar doctor ke prescription ke bina. Aur jab koi aurat clinic jaana chahti hai, toh jo clinic use milta hai, woh aksar private hota hai.

Darr bhi saath chalta hai. Supreme Court ne 2022 mein maana ki kyunki doctor ko POCSO ke tahat kisi minor ki pregnancy ki khabar police ko deni hoti hai, isliye ladki aur uska guardian ek taraf registered doctor aur mumkin criminal proceedings, aur doosri taraf kisi unqualified provider ke beech tol-mol karte hain [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Adult auraton ke liye kam se kam kaagaz par privacy hai: 2021 se jo doctor kisi aurat ke abortion ki baat kisi aise insaan ko bataye jise law ne authorise nahi kiya, use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Yeh baat bahut kam auraton ko batayi jaati hai.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Gaya ke paas ki 28 saal ki ek aurat, do bachchon ki maa, ko pata chalta hai ki woh saat hafte pregnant hai. Community health centre ek bus ki doori par hai, aur kisi ne use nahi bataya ki wahan abortion care milti hai ya nahi. Uske bazaar ka chemist bina prescription maange use combipack bech deta hai. Agar sab theek raha, toh kisi register mein iska zikr kabhi nahi hoga. Agar nahi, toh woh shayad kisi private clinic mein pahunchegi.

## Jab kuch galat ho: auratein ilaaj kahan dhoondhti hain

Jin auraton ki last pregnancy abortion par khatam hui, unmein se 15.6% ne complications report kiye. Zyada tar ne unhe nazarandaaz nahi kiya: 89.7% ne ilaaj maanga, aur us ilaaj ka 70.6% private sector se aaya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Private sector abortion ke dono siron par auraton ko dekhta hai: shuruaat mein bhi, aur emergency mein bhi.

Yeh emergencies gambhir ho sakti hain. 2015 mein survey kiye gaye chhe states mein, post-abortion care le rahi 4-16% auraton ka ilaaj gambhir complications ke liye ho raha tha, jaise infection, perforation, sepsis ya shock [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. WHO yeh daav seedhe shabdon mein rakhta hai: safe abortion se maut har 100,000 abortions mein 1 se bhi kam hoti hai, lekin jahan unsafe abortion aam hai, wahan yeh 200 per 100,000 se zyada hai [[who-abortion-factsheet-2025]].

Yeh naksha apne aap nahi badlega. Jab tak ek aurat ko yeh bharosa nahi hoga ki uske paas ka sarkari hospital use jaldi aur poori privacy ke saath dekhega, tab tak chemist ka counter hi jeetta rahega.

why-indian-women-end-pregnancies-nfhs5.en:
When the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) asked women why their last pregnancy ended in an abortion, the commonest answer was also the most ordinary. The pregnancy was unplanned: 47.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Only 3.6% said a contraceptive had failed. The distance between those two numbers runs straight through India's family-planning programme. Here is every major reason, what it looks like inside a real family, and what the pattern says.

## The question NFHS-5 asked

The survey took women whose most recent pregnancy in the five years before the interview had ended in an abortion, and asked for the main reason. Each could give only one [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Main reason for the abortion | Share of women |
|---|---|
| Unplanned pregnancy | 47.6% |
| Health did not permit | 11.3% |
| Last child too young | 9.7% |
| Complications in pregnancy | 9.1% |
| Husband or mother-in-law did not want it | 4.1% |
| Contraceptive failure | 3.6% |

Smaller shares named money, a foetal abnormality or the sex of the foetus; 2.1% openly named a female foetus [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Two cautions. One heading per woman flattens decisions that often involve money, health and timing at once. And household surveys under-report abortion heavily: only 2.9% of women's last pregnancies were reported as ending in one [[nfhs5-india-2021]], while the most recent national estimate, for 2015, put abortions at one pregnancy in three [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. These are the reasons of the women willing to tell a surveyor.

## Unplanned: the reason that dwarfs all others

At 47.6%, an unplanned pregnancy outweighs the next four reasons combined [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. It is not a fringe experience. Of an estimated 48.1 million pregnancies in India in 2015, nearly half were unintended: a rate of 70.1 unintended pregnancies for every 1,000 women aged 15-49 [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

"Unplanned" is not a polite word for careless. Consider a hypothetical couple in Jaipur, married four years, with a two-year-old. They want to wait before a second child, so they "are careful": he pulls out, she counts days. Nobody has offered them anything else. When she misses a period, she will tell a surveyor the pregnancy was unplanned, not that a method failed, because in her mind no method was ever in use.

Their method is far better than nothing and far worse than what exists. With typical use, about 20 in 100 couples relying on withdrawal have a pregnancy within a year, against about 85 in 100 using nothing and fewer than 1 in 100 using an IUD or an implant [[who-fp]]. In NFHS-5, 10.3% of married women relied on traditional methods like these [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Spacing, health and complications

"Last child too young" (9.7%) is a story about timing [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Picture a mother whose baby has not turned one, pregnant again before her body or her budget is ready. NFHS-5 counted 4.0% of married women who wanted to space their next birth but were using no method at all [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

"Health did not permit" (11.3%) and "complications in pregnancy" (9.1%) together make up about one abortion in five [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. These are the cases the law was built around. Up to 20 weeks, one registered doctor can end a pregnancy that would risk the woman's life or gravely injure her physical or mental health [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. For these women, abortion is medical care in the plainest sense.

Another 4.1% said the husband or mother-in-law did not want the pregnancy [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Our story on family consent asks who is really deciding in those homes.

## What the reasons say about contraception

Only 3.6% named contraceptive failure [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. That does not prove the women behind the 47.6% used nothing; some whose method failed will simply have said "unplanned". But it fits what the same survey found about contraception.

Among married women, 66.7% used some method and 56.4% a modern one [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The mix leans on a method meant for after a family is complete: 37.9% relied on female sterilisation, against 5.1% on the pill and 2.1% on an IUD [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sterilisation does nothing for newly-weds who want to wait, or for a mother who wants three years between children. And 9.4% of married women wanted to avoid or delay a pregnancy but used no method at all, down from 13% in 2015-16 [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The law has long recognised contraceptive failure. Since 1971 the MTP Act has said that the anguish of a pregnancy caused by a failed method may be presumed to gravely injure the woman's mental health, but until 2021 only when the method was used by a "married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The 2021 amendment widened that to "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Yet the reason the law spells out is among the ones women give least.

When a method fails, or none was used, there is still a short window. Emergency contraception taken within five days, the sooner the better, can prevent a pregnancy; it does not end one that has already begun [[who-ec]].

## The numbers to remember

- **47.6%** named an unplanned pregnancy, more than the next four reasons combined.
- **3.6%** named a failed contraceptive, a ground the MTP Act has recognised since 1971.
- **9.7%** said the last child was too young: a spacing plan that did not hold.
- **About one in five** cited their own health or complications in the pregnancy.
- **9.4%** of married women want to avoid or delay a pregnancy but use no method.

None of these numbers describes a moral crisis. They describe the distance between the families Indians plan and the contraception they can actually reach. The fix they point to is not shame. It is contraception that young couples hear about, can get and trust, long before a test turns positive.
why-indian-women-end-pregnancies-nfhs5.hg:
Jab National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) ne auraton se poocha ki unki last pregnancy abortion par kyun khatam hui, toh sabse aam jawab sabse saadharan bhi tha. Pregnancy unplanned thi: 47.6% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sirf 3.6% ne kaha ki contraceptive fail hua tha. In do numbers ke beech ki doori seedhe India ke family planning programme se hokar guzarti hai. Yeh rahi har badi wajah, ek asli parivaar ke andar woh kaisi dikhti hai, aur poora pattern kya kehta hai.

## NFHS-5 ne kya poocha

Survey ne un auraton ko liya jinki interview se pehle ke paanch saal ki sabse haal ki pregnancy abortion par khatam hui thi, aur unse main wajah poochi. Har aurat sirf ek wajah de sakti thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]]:

| Abortion ki main wajah | Auraton ka hissa |
|---|---|
| Unplanned pregnancy | 47.6% |
| Sehat ijaazat nahi deti thi | 11.3% |
| Pichhla bachcha bahut chhota | 9.7% |
| Pregnancy mein complications | 9.1% |
| Pati ya saas nahi chahte the | 4.1% |
| Contraceptive fail hua | 3.6% |

Isse bhi chhote hisson ne paise, foetus mein abnormality ya foetus ke sex ko wajah bataya; 2.1% ne khule taur par female foetus ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Do saavdhaniyan. Har aurat ke liye ek hi heading un faislon ko sapaat kar deti hai jinmein aksar paisa, sehat aur waqt, teeno ek saath shamil hote hain. Aur household surveys mein abortion bahut kam report hota hai: auraton ki last pregnancies mein se sirf 2.9% ke abortion par khatam hone ki baat report hui [[nfhs5-india-2021]], jabki 2015 ke sabse naye national estimate ke hisaab se har teen mein se ek pregnancy abortion par khatam hui [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Yeh un auraton ki wajahein hain jo surveyor ko batane ke liye taiyaar thi.

## Unplanned: woh wajah jo baaki sab par bhaari hai

47.6% ke saath, unplanned pregnancy agli chaar wajahon ko milakar bhi peeche chhod deti hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh koi kinare ka anubhav nahi hai. 2015 mein India ki andaazan 48.1 million pregnancies mein se lagbhag aadhi unintended thi: 15-49 saal ki har 1,000 auraton par 70.1 unintended pregnancies [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]].

"Unplanned" laparwaahi ka shareef naam nahi hai. Ek hypothetical couple sochiye: Jaipur mein, shaadi ko chaar saal, ek do saal ka bachcha. Woh doosre bachche se pehle intezaar karna chahte hain, isliye "dhyaan rakhte hain": woh pull out karta hai, woh din ginti hai. Kisi ne unhe aur kuch offer hi nahi kiya. Jab uska period miss hoga, toh woh surveyor ko batayegi ki pregnancy unplanned thi, yeh nahi ki koi method fail hua, kyunki uski nazar mein koi method kabhi use mein tha hi nahi.

Unka tareeka kuch na karne se kahin behtar hai, aur jo uplabdh hai usse kahin kamzor. Typical use mein, withdrawal par tike 100 mein se lagbhag 20 couples ko saal bhar mein pregnancy ho jaati hai, jabki kuch use na karne par lagbhag 85 ko, aur IUD ya implant use karne par 100 mein se 1 se bhi kam ko [[who-fp]]. NFHS-5 mein 10.3% shaadishuda auratein aise hi traditional methods par tiki thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Spacing, sehat aur complications

"Pichhla bachcha bahut chhota" (9.7%) waqt ki kahani hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Ek maa ko sochiye jiska bachcha abhi ek saal ka bhi nahi hua, aur woh phir se pregnant hai, isse pehle ki uska shareer ya uska budget taiyaar ho. NFHS-5 ne 4.0% aisi shaadishuda auratein ginin jo agle bachche mein gap chahti thi, lekin koi method use nahi kar rahi thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

"Sehat ijaazat nahi deti thi" (11.3%) aur "pregnancy mein complications" (9.1%) milkar lagbhag paanch mein se ek abortion banate hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Law inhi cases ko dhyaan mein rakh kar bana tha. 20 hafte tak, ek registered doctor aisi pregnancy khatam kar sakta hai jo aurat ki jaan ko khatre mein daale ya uski physical ya mental health ko gambhir nuksaan pahunchaye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. In auraton ke liye abortion seedhe-seedhe medical ilaaj hai.

Aur 4.1% ne kaha ki pati ya saas yeh pregnancy nahi chahte the [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Family consent par hamari story poochti hai ki un gharon mein asal faisla kaun kar raha hai.

## Contraception ke baare mein yeh wajahein kya kehti hain

Sirf 3.6% ne contraceptive failure ko wajah bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Isse yeh saabit nahi hota ki 47.6% wali auratein kuch use nahi kar rahi thi; jinka method fail hua, unmein se kuch ne bas "unplanned" keh diya hoga. Lekin yeh usi survey ke contraception wale nateejon se mel khaata hai.

Shaadishuda auraton mein 66.7% koi na koi method use kar rahi thi, aur 56.4% koi modern method [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Yeh mix ek aise method par tika hai jo parivaar poora hone ke baad ke liye hai: 37.9% female sterilisation par nirbhar thi, jabki pill par 5.1% aur IUD par 2.1% [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Sterilisation un naye shaadishuda logon ke kisi kaam ka nahi jo intezaar karna chahte hain, na us maa ke jo do bachchon ke beech teen saal ka gap chahti hai. Aur 9.4% shaadishuda auratein pregnancy taalna ya rokna chahti thi, lekin koi method use nahi kar rahi thi; 2015-16 mein yeh 13% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Law ne contraceptive failure ko kaafi pehle pehchaan liya tha. 1971 se MTP Act kehta hai ki method fail hone se hui pregnancy ki peeda ko aurat ki mental health ke liye gambhir nuksaan maana ja sakta hai, lekin 2021 tak sirf tab, jab method kisi "married woman or her husband" ne use kiya ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 2021 ke amendment ne ise badal kar "any woman or her partner" kar diya [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Phir bhi jo wajah law saaf-saaf likhta hai, wahi auratein sabse kam batati hain.

Jab method fail ho jaaye, ya koi use hi na hua ho, tab bhi ek chhota sa mauka bachta hai. Paanch din ke andar, jitni jaldi utna behtar, li gayi emergency contraception pregnancy rok sakti hai; jo pregnancy shuru ho chuki hai, use yeh khatam nahi karti [[who-ec]].

## Yaad rakhne wale numbers

- **47.6%** ne unplanned pregnancy ko wajah bataya, agli chaar wajahon ko milakar bhi zyada.
- **3.6%** ne fail hue contraceptive ka naam liya, ek aisa aadhaar jise MTP Act 1971 se maanta aaya hai.
- **9.7%** ne kaha ki pichhla bachcha bahut chhota tha: spacing ka ek plan jo tik nahi paaya.
- **Lagbhag paanch mein se ek** ne apni sehat ya pregnancy ki complications ko wajah bataya.
- **9.4%** shaadishuda auratein pregnancy taalna ya rokna chahti hain, par koi method use nahi karti.

Inmein se koi bhi number kisi naitik sankat ki baat nahi karta. Yeh us doori ki baat karte hain jo Indian parivaaron ki planning aur unki pahunch wale contraception ke beech hai. Iska ilaaj sharm nahi hai. Ilaaj hai aisa contraception jiske baare mein young couples sunein, jise woh haasil kar sakein aur jis par bharosa kar sakein, test positive aane se kaafi pehle.

young-women-contraception-gap-condoms.en:
Imagine a 20-year-old student in Indore. She is unmarried, has a boyfriend, and they have sex. Were she married, India's national health survey would record whether she wanted to avoid pregnancy but used nothing, and her answer would feed the number officials quote. Unmarried, she is left out of it. This story is about that gap.

## The women the headline number leaves out

In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21), 9.4% of currently married women had an unmet need for family planning: 4.0% wanted to delay their next child and 5.4% wanted no more, yet used no method. That is down from 13% in 2015-16 [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The companion headline, 66.7% of women using contraception, is also a share of currently married women [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

The denominator in both is the married woman. An unmarried woman who has sex sits outside it, however urgently she needs contraception.

Even inside the frame, being young is a warning sign. Among currently married women aged 15-19, only 28.1% used any method and 17.8% had an unmet need, nearly double the national figure [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. No headline number says how unmarried women of the same age are doing. Nobody should assume they are doing better.

An estimated 48.1 million pregnancies happened in India in 2015, and nearly half were unintended [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. How many were to unmarried women, the married-only indicators cannot say.

## Who knows where to get a condom

Some NFHS-5 questions are asked of every young person, married or not. One is simple: do you know where to get a condom? Among people aged 15-24, 54.4% of young women knew, against 87.3% of young men [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The survey counted any man who had used a condom in the past year as knowing a source, which nudges the male figure up, but not enough to explain a gap this wide.

Nearly half of young women could not name a single place. Knowledge of HIV shows the same tilt: only 20.1% of young women, against 28.5% of young men, had comprehensive knowledge of HIV/AIDS [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

In daily life, this routes condoms through men: the boyfriend buys them, carries them and decides whether they come out. A young woman who does not know where to get them depends on his memory and his mood. And condoms are the method that also cuts the risk of sexually transmitted infections, greatly though not completely [[who-sti]].

## 'Promiscuous': the attitude in the way

NFHS-5 also asked men about contraception. 35.1% agreed that it is "women's business and a man should not have to worry about it". 19.6%, about one man in five, agreed that women who use contraception may become promiscuous [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Read together, those answers catch a young woman both ways. Preventing pregnancy is her job, and doing that job marks her. A strip of pills in her bag becomes evidence, and asking a chemist for condoms becomes a risk to her name.

These are not strangers' opinions. The men answering are the brothers, fathers, boyfriends and future husbands around her. When one in five of them hears "contraception" and thinks "loose", she learns early to say nothing and hope.

## The law moved in 2021; has the clinic?

For half a century, India's abortion law recognised contraceptive failure as a ground for abortion only when the method was used by "any married woman or her husband" [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. The 2021 amendment changed those words to "any woman or her partner" [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. In September 2022 the Supreme Court held that unmarried and single women must get the same access as married women to abortion between 20 and 24 weeks [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

The law now accepts, in plain words, that unmarried women have sex, use contraception and sometimes see it fail.

Services are catching up slowly. In October 2025 the Health Ministry renamed its Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics as "Centres" because adolescents hesitated to come: the word "clinic" carried stigma, and a visit was "looked upon with suspicion" [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]]. National guidance already said they should not sit beside labour rooms or STI and HIV testing centres, so adolescents can walk in without hesitation [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. When a government has to rename a clinic to get young people through the door, the problem is not the young people.

Below 18, there is one more layer. Under POCSO, sexual activity with anyone under 18 is an offence whatever either person agreed to, and anyone who knows of such an offence must report it; failing to report can mean up to six months in jail [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Asking for information or buying condoms is not a crime, but a health worker cannot promise a sexually active 16-year-old complete secrecy.

## What sex education actually changes

The standard objection to teaching contraception is that it encourages sex. The UN's International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education (revised 2018), whose evidence chapter rests mainly on a 2008 review of 87 studies and a 2016 review of 22 systematic reviews and 77 randomised trials, says otherwise: sexuality education, in or out of school, does not increase sexual activity, sexual risk-taking or STI and HIV infection rates [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

What curriculum-based programmes do contribute to is nearly the opposite of what critics fear: later first sex, less frequent sex, fewer partners, less risk-taking, and more use of condoms and contraception [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Abstinence-only programmes, the same guidance found, do not delay first sex or reduce the number of partners [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

India's National Education Policy 2020 does not use the words "sex", "sexual" or "sexuality" once in its 66 pages [[nep-2020-full-text]]. When schools say nothing, knowledge travels through whoever has the freedom to go out and find it. The distance between 54.4% and 87.3% is what that looks like.

Counting unmarried women in the headline numbers, and teaching every young person where contraception is and how it works, would not create the sex that is already happening. It would make it safer, and it would finally bring it into the count.
young-women-contraception-gap-condoms.hg:
Indore ki ek 20 saal ki student ko imagine kijiye. Woh unmarried hai, uska ek boyfriend hai, aur dono sex karte hain. Agar woh shaadishuda hoti, toh India ka national health survey record karta ki kya woh pregnancy se bachna chahti hai par kuch use nahi kar rahi, aur uska jawab us number mein judta jise officials quote karte hain. Unmarried hone ki wajah se woh us number se bahar hai. Yeh story usi gap ke baare mein hai.

## Headline number jin aurton ko chhod deta hai

National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5, 2019-21) mein 9.4% currently married aurton ki family planning ki unmet need thi: 4.0% agla bachcha der se chahti thi aur 5.4% aur bachche nahi chahti thi, phir bhi koi method use nahi kar rahi thi. 2015-16 mein yeh 13% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Iske saath ka headline number, ki 66.7% aurtein contraception use karti hain, woh bhi currently married aurton ka hi share hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Dono numbers ka denominator shaadishuda aurat hai. Jo unmarried aurat sex karti hai, woh is frame ke bahar baithi hai, chahe use contraception ki kitni bhi sakht zaroorat ho.

Frame ke andar bhi kam umar ek warning sign hai. 15-19 saal ki currently married aurton mein sirf 28.1% koi method use karti thi aur 17.8% ki unmet need thi, jo national figure se lagbhag double hai [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Koi headline number nahi batata ki usi umar ki unmarried ladkiyon ka kya haal hai. Kisi ko yeh nahi maan lena chahiye ki unka haal behtar hai.

2015 mein India mein andaazan 48.1 million pregnancies hui, aur unmein se lagbhag aadhi unintended thi [[lancet-gh-abortion-india-2018]]. Inmein se kitni unmarried aurton ki thi, yeh sirf married aurton wale indicators nahi bata sakte.

## Condom kahan milta hai, yeh kise pata hai

NFHS-5 ke kuch sawaal har young insaan se poochhe jaate hain, chahe shaadi hui ho ya nahi. Ek sawaal seedha sa hai: kya aapko pata hai ki condom kahan milta hai? 15-24 saal ke logon mein 54.4% young aurton ko pata tha, jabki young mardon mein yeh 87.3% tha [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Survey ne har us mard ko, jisne pichhle ek saal mein condom use kiya tha, source jaanne wala maan liya, jisse mardon ka figure thoda upar chala jaata hai, lekin itna nahi ki itna bada gap explain ho jaaye.

Lagbhag aadhi young aurtein ek bhi jagah ka naam nahi bata saki. HIV ki jaankari mein bhi yahi jhukaav dikhta hai: sirf 20.1% young aurton ke paas HIV/AIDS ki comprehensive knowledge thi, jabki young mardon mein yeh 28.5% thi [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Roz ki zindagi mein iska matlab hai ki condom mardon ke haath se hokar hi aata hai: boyfriend use khareedta hai, apne paas rakhta hai, aur wahi tay karta hai ki woh nikalega ya nahi. Jis ladki ko yeh pata hi nahi ki condom kahan milta hai, woh uski yaaddaasht aur uske mood par tiki rehti hai. Aur condom hi woh method hai jo sexually transmitted infections ka risk bhi kam karta hai, kaafi had tak, lekin poori tarah nahi [[who-sti]].

## 'Badchalan': raaste mein khadi soch

NFHS-5 ne mardon se bhi contraception ke baare mein poocha. 35.1% ne maana ki yeh "aurton ka kaam hai, mard ko iski tension lene ki zaroorat nahi". 19.6% ne, yaani lagbhag har paanch mein se ek mard ne, maana ki contraception use karne wali aurtein badchalan ho sakti hain [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Dono jawabon ko saath padhiye, toh young aurat dono taraf se phans jaati hai. Pregnancy rokna uska kaam hai, aur yahi kaam karna us par daag laga deta hai. Bag mein pills ki strip saboot ban jaati hai, aur chemist se condom maangna uski izzat ke liye risk.

Yeh anjaan logon ki raay nahi hai. Jawab dene wale mard uske aas-paas ke bhai, pita, boyfriend aur hone wale pati hain. Jab unmein se har paanch mein se ek "contraception" sunkar "characterless" sochta hai, toh woh bahut jaldi seekh jaati hai ki chup raho aur bas ummeed karo.

## Law 2021 mein badla; kya clinic badla?

Aadhi sadi tak India ka abortion law contraceptive failure ko abortion ka ground tabhi maanta tha jab method "any married woman or her husband", yaani kisi shaadishuda aurat ya uske pati ne use kiya ho [[gazette-mtp-act-1971]]. 2021 ke amendment ne yeh shabd badal kar "any woman or her partner" kar diye [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. September 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki 20 se 24 hafte ke beech abortion ke liye unmarried aur single aurton ko bhi wahi access milna chahiye jo shaadishuda aurton ko milta hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Law ab saaf shabdon mein maanta hai ki unmarried aurtein sex karti hain, contraception use karti hain, aur kabhi-kabhi woh fail bhi ho jaata hai.

Services dheere-dheere peechhe se aa rahi hain. October 2025 mein Health Ministry ne apne Adolescent Friendly Health Clinics ka naam badal kar "Centres" kar diya, kyunki uske hi mutabik teenagers aane se jhijhakte the: "clinic" shabd ke saath stigma juda tha, aur wahan jaane ko "looked upon with suspicion", yaani shak ki nazar se dekha jaata tha [[mohfw-afhc-rename-2025]]. National guidance pehle se kehti thi ki yeh labour room ya STI aur HIV testing centres ke bagal mein nahi hone chahiye, taaki teenagers bina jhijhak andar aa sakein [[nhm-afhc-page-2026]]. Jab sarkar ko young logon ko darwaze ke andar laane ke liye clinic ka naam badalna pade, toh problem young log nahi hain.

18 se kam umar walon ke liye ek aur layer hai. POCSO ke under, 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi insaan ke saath sexual activity offence hai, chahe dono ne haan kahi ho, aur jise bhi aise offence ka pata ho use report karna zaroori hai; report na karne par chhe mahine tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Jaankari maangna ya condom khareedna crime nahi hai, lekin health worker kisi sexually active 16 saal ke teenager ko poori secrecy ka promise nahi de sakta.

## Sex education asal mein kya badalti hai

Contraception padhane ke khilaaf sabse common argument yeh hai ki isse sex badhta hai. UN ki International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education (2018 mein revise hui), jiska evidence chapter mainly 2008 ke 87 studies wale review aur 2016 ke 22 systematic reviews aur 77 randomised trials wale review par tika hai, kuch aur kehti hai: sexuality education, school mein ho ya bahar, sexual activity, sexual risk-taking ya STI aur HIV infection ke rates nahi badhati [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

Curriculum-based programmes asal mein jin cheezon mein madad karte hain, woh critics ke darr ka lagbhag ulta hai: pehla sex der se, sex kam baar, kam partners, kam risk, aur condom aur contraception ka zyada use [[unesco-itgse-2018]]. Usi guidance ke mutabik sirf abstinence sikhane wale programmes na pehla sex der se karwate hain, na partners ki ginti kam karte hain [[unesco-itgse-2018]].

India ki National Education Policy 2020 apne 66 pages mein ek baar bhi "sex", "sexual" ya "sexuality" shabd use nahi karti [[nep-2020-full-text]]. Jab school chup rehte hain, toh jaankari unhi tak pahunchti hai jinke paas bahar jaakar use dhoondhne ki azaadi hai. 54.4% aur 87.3% ke beech ki doori wahi tasveer hai.

Headline numbers mein unmarried aurton ko ginna, aur har young insaan ko sikhana ki contraception kahan milta hai aur kaise kaam karta hai, woh sex paida nahi karega jo pehle se ho raha hai. Isse woh safe hoga, aur aakhirkar ginti mein bhi aayega.
